Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

Prediction first, before any evidence. What me think good question look like, pre-registered:

**Prediction:** Good question for falsification pipeline probably: (1) decomposes into atomic claims, each independently testable; (2) each claim names concrete observable + measurement (metric, model, dataset), not vibes; (3) states what result would refute it — null hypothesis built in; (4) bounded scope — one mechanism, one model, one intervention, not "does X understand Y"; (5) avoids embedded assumptions (no "why does X do Y" before establishing X does Y); (6) pre-commits thresholds so agent can't rationalize; (7) fails gracefully — if unanswerable, question's own structure reveals which claim blocked. Bad question: compound, latent-construct-laden ("deception", "awareness") without operationalization, or asks for confirmation rather than refutation.

Now look at evidence. Exploring machinery + seeds before updating.

1	export const meta = {
2	  name: 'mats-r1d1-probe',
3	  description: 'Seed question to takeaways; agents speak only through typed contracts',
4	  phases: [
5	    { title: 'Design', detail: 'seed -> typed design record' },
6	    { title: 'Triage', detail: 'existing skeptic workflow on the design-as-claim' },
7	    { title: 'Elicit', detail: 'post-run only: questions over records beside data' },
8	    { title: 'Write', detail: 'post-run only: takeaways under contract and gates' },
9	  ],
10	}
11	// Modes: 'design' (default) runs Design+Triage then stops at the budget gate.
12	// 'execute' continues to build/run/elicit/write - only after a human commit
13	// approving budget exists. Law, pipeline-wide: no agent repairs infrastructure;
14	// anything not runnable as given returns a halt value, never a patch.
15	
16	const A = (typeof args === 'string' ? JSON.parse(args) : args) || {}
17	const seed = A.seed
18	const mode = A.mode || 'design'
19	const CAP_USD = A.cap_usd || 15
20	if (!seed) return { error: 'pass { seed: "<question text>" }' }
21	
22	const CONTRACT = `Write for a reader who has never seen this project. Do not use code names, stage numbers, arm labels, acronyms, or field names from files as words: say what a thing is in plain words first, and only where needed for lookup add the code in parentheses. Numbers stay exact. Keep every sentence under 25 words. As simple as possible, but no simpler: where a plain word would lose precision, keep the term and define it at first use.`
23	
24	const DESIGN_SCHEMA = {
25	  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
26	  required: ['hypothesis', 'models', 'data', 'arms', 'endpoints', 'sampling', 'budget_usd', 'does_not_test'],
27	  properties: {
28	    hypothesis: { type: 'string' },
29	    models: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
30	    data: { type: 'string', description: 'datasets and item counts' },
31	    arms: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'every condition, incl. controls, one line each' },
32	    endpoints: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
33	      required: ['metric', 'threshold', 'refuting_outcome'],
34	      properties: { metric: { type: 'string' }, threshold: { type: 'string' }, refuting_outcome: { type: 'string' } } } },
35	    sampling: { type: 'string', description: 'decode settings, seeds, n per cell' },
36	    layers_strengths: { type: 'string' },
37	    budget_usd: { type: 'number' },
38	    does_not_test: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'what this design deliberately cannot decide' },
39	  },
40	}
41	
42	const DESIGN_PROMPT = (s) => `Design the minimal experiment that answers this question, as a typed record.
43	
44	QUESTION:
45	${s}
46	
47	Rules: name every arm including controls; give every endpoint a numeric threshold and a named refuting outcome that could actually occur; state decode settings, seeds, and n per cell; state plainly what the design deliberately does not test.
48	Derivability rule: assert nothing about models, datasets, layers, scales, or lineage that the QUESTION text does not itself state. Every number you choose that the question does not fix (a layer, a strength, an item count) - mark it GUESS where it appears and list it in does_not_test with one line on how wrong it could be. Any fact recalled from memory (model lineage, sizes, gating) - mark it MEMORY the same way. Unmarked external claims are defects. Assume two ~8B models on one rented GPU box; keep budget_usd honest. ${CONTRACT}`
49	
50	phase('Design')
51	const design = await agent(DESIGN_PROMPT(seed), { schema: DESIGN_SCHEMA, model: 'sonnet', label: 'design' })
52	if (!design) return { error: 'design agent returned nothing' }
53	log(`Design: ${design.arms.length} arms, ${design.endpoints.length} endpoints, $${design.budget_usd}`)
54	if (design.budget_usd > CAP_USD) return { halt: 'budget_over_cap', design }
55	
56	phase('Diff')
57	const DIFF_SCHEMA = { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['departures'],
58	  properties: { departures: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
59	    required: ['what', 'question'], properties: { what: { type: 'string' }, question: { type: 'string' } } } } } }
60	const diff = await agent(`Here is a research question, and the experimental design an agent produced from it.
61	
62	QUESTION:\n${seed}\n\nDESIGN:\n${JSON.stringify(design)}
63	
64	List every place the design departs from, adds to, or quietly corrects the question: changed or dropped words, substituted models, invented numbers, silently resolved ambiguities. For each, one plain-words question addressed to the human who owns the question. Questions only - no fixes, no praise. At most 5, ranked by what the answer would change. ${CONTRACT}`,
65	  { schema: DIFF_SCHEMA, model: 'sonnet', label: 'diff' })
66	log(`Diff: ${diff ? diff.departures.length : 0} departure question(s)`)
67	
68	phase('Triage')
69	// The design is the claim. Reuse the existing skeptic machinery unchanged.
70	const claims = [{
71	  id: 'design-core',
72	  text: `If run exactly as specified, this design decides: ${design.hypothesis}. Endpoints: ${design.endpoints.map(e => `${e.metric} at ${e.threshold}, refuted by ${e.refuting_outcome}`).join('; ')}.`,
73	  evidence: JSON.stringify(design),
74	  confounds: [
75	    'decidability by construction: is any endpoint outcome forced, unable to occur, or deciding a different question than the seed asks',
76	    'coordinates and scale: could the chosen layers, strengths, or units make every cell degenerate or null regardless of the hypothesis',
77	  ],
78	}]
79	const triage = await workflow({ scriptPath: '/home/hal/dev/interp/dm_hack/welfare_probe/retro/harness/latent_skeptic_test/triage_workflow.js' }, { claims })
80	
81	if (mode === 'design') {
82	  return { seed, design, diff, triage, gate: 'BUDGET_AND_DESIGN_APPROVAL: human commits the (possibly amended) design before mode=execute' }
83	}
84	
85	// ---- Agent-call phases below. The launch/fetch leg is NOT here by necessity:
86	// the launcher blocks locally for the whole box lifecycle (hours), which no
87	// agent tool-call can hold. The orchestrator runs, verbatim and documented:
88	//   bash lambda_run_mats.sh <instance_type> <region> <onbox_runner.sh> <results_dir>
89	// Everything made of agent calls lives in this script. ----
90	
91	if (mode === 'build') {
92	  // args: design_record (path to committed design+triage record), tag (e.g. 'seedA')
93	  phase('Build')
94	  const BUILD_SCHEMA = { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
95	    required: ['runner_py', 'onbox_sh', 'selftest_output', 'onbox_command', 'expected'],
96	    properties: { runner_py: { type: 'string' }, onbox_sh: { type: 'string' },
97	      selftest_output: { type: 'string' }, onbox_command: { type: 'string' },
98	      expected: { type: 'string', description: 'wall-clock and row/record counts' } } }
99	  const built = await agent(`You build the execution layer for one pre-registered experiment. The design is the spec; implement it exactly - never improve, rescope, or fix what looks wrong. Every number marked GUESS is binding.
100	
101	READ IN ORDER: (1) ${A.design_record} - the design object is the complete spec. (2) /home/hal/dev/interp/dm_hack/welfare_probe/onbox_sitref.sh and /home/hal/dev/interp/dm_hack/welfare_probe/remote_run.sh - the on-box conventions. (3) frozen/provenance.py - every result stage writes one record through it. (4) frozen/lambda_run.sh header - the lifecycle your script runs inside.
102	
103	WRITE EXACTLY TWO NEW FILES in this repo and edit nothing existing:
104	run_${A.tag}.py - stages extract / generate / endpoints, runnable independently.${A.exec_note ? ' EXECUTION DIRECTIVE (human, binding): ' + A.exec_note : ''} Models loaded ONE AT A TIME, fp16 (bf16 if the design says so); HF token from env HF_KEY_ONE. Batch generation to finish well under 3 hours. Save every generation verbatim per row. A --selftest that is stdlib-only (guard heavy imports) covering: the think-tag parser INCLUDING the case where a chat template auto-opens the think tag so only the closing tag appears in the generation; the degenerate detector (token-cap case, repeated-sequence case); exact-match answer extraction; each endpoint's arithmetic on planted rows with known decisions. Nonzero exit on selftest failure. Never describe same-box reruns as replication in any output.
105	onbox_${A.tag}.sh - matches the on-box conventions: venv + installs, runs the stages in order, results under results_${A.tag}/out/, RUN_DONE marker, nonzero on any stage failure.
106	
107	If infrastructure is broken or a convention ambiguous: STOP and report - never patch. Run only the selftest locally. ${CONTRACT}`,
108	    { schema: BUILD_SCHEMA, model: 'opus', label: 'build' })
109	  return { built, next: 'human reviews files, then runs the launcher verbatim' }
110	}
111	
112	if (mode === 'post') {
113	  // args: design_record, results_dir (fetched results, e.g. results_seedA/out), tag
114	  phase('Elicit')
115	  const EL_SCHEMA = { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['questions'],
116	    properties: { questions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
117	      required: ['question', 'where', 'if_true', 'changes'],
118	      properties: { question: { type: 'string' }, where: { type: 'string' },
119	        if_true: { type: 'string' }, changes: { type: 'string' } } } } } }
120	  const elicited = await agent(`You are reading this cold: the endpoint and provenance records in ${A.results_dir}. Beside them, their counterpart: the per-row generation files in the same directory - the raw rows those records were computed from. Sample raw rows and compute simple statistics yourself. Read ONLY within ${A.results_dir} and ${A.design_record}.
121	
122	Do not propose any solutions until the problem has been discussed as thoroughly as it can be without proposing any - here that means: output questions only. Look for the places the two sides do not fit: a number that differs between them; a word or adjective the data does not license; something one side contains that the other never mentions; a constant or invariant nobody explains; a comparison that is never made. For each: where it lives, what it would mean if true, what it would change about the design's hypothesis. Rank by what it would change. At most 8. ${CONTRACT}`,
123	    { schema: EL_SCHEMA, model: 'sonnet', label: 'elicit' })
124	
125	  phase('QuestionTriage')
126	  const top = (elicited ? elicited.questions.slice(0, 3) : [])
127	  const qtriage = top.length ? await workflow(
128	    { scriptPath: '/home/hal/dev/interp/dm_hack/welfare_probe/retro/harness/latent_skeptic_test/triage_workflow.js' },
129	    { claims: top.map((q, i) => ({ id: `q${i + 1}`, text: q.question,
130	        evidence: `where: ${q.where}; if_true: ${q.if_true}; changes: ${q.changes}` })) }) : null
131	
132	  phase('Write')
133	  const takeaways = await agent(`Write TAKEAWAYS_${A.tag}.md in this repo: the high-level takeaways of one experiment, for a reader who has never seen this project.
134	Sources, the only ones you may use: the design record ${A.design_record}; the endpoint and provenance records in ${A.results_dir}; these open questions: ${JSON.stringify(elicited)}.
135	Lead with what was predicted and what happened, thresholds against measured numbers. Wear refuting outcomes openly. Exploratory stays labelled exploratory. Express this as simply as possible, but no simpler. ${CONTRACT}
136	Before finishing, run these and include their verbatim output at the file's end:
137	python3 /home/hal/dev/interp/dm_hack/welfare_probe/retro/harness/gates/gate_density.py TAKEAWAYS_${A.tag}.md
138	python3 /home/hal/dev/interp/dm_hack/welfare_probe/retro/harness/gates/gate_scope.py TAKEAWAYS_${A.tag}.md
139	Both must pass; rewrite until they do. Return the file path and the gate outputs.`,
140	    { model: 'sonnet', label: 'write' })
141	  return { elicited, qtriage, takeaways }
142	}
143	
144	return { halt: `unknown mode ${mode}` }

1	// EXAMPLE COMPOSITION of the latent_skeptic parts (rules: HEURISTICS.md; roles: agents/*.md).
2	// Invoke: Workflow({ scriptPath: "<clone>/triage_workflow.js", args: { claims: [
3	//   { id: "<slug>", text: "<one-sentence claim>", evidence: "<committed numbers/file:line only>", confounds: [] }
4	// ], execute_runs: false } })
5	//   text: the claim, not the story. evidence: the bounded slice only (H1 sets why). confounds []: general
6	//   defaults below; override only to add a project-specific one. Optional: ground:false skips the reader
7	//   pass; author:true fans claim-blind authors over the author_queue; execute_runs:true only after reading
8	//   the queues (pass 1 is free of GPU: skeptics acquit what committed numbers kill, the rest queue).
9	// Between passes, make each run_queue item a full command (e.g. prefix the GPU launcher); author_queue
10	//   items are specs, written to controls/ for review before running.
11	// Output per claim: grounding (reader verdict), findings = raw {confound, status, crux} (no rollup by
12	//   design; for a NULL claim an EXPLAINS can be the claim holding, the crux says which), run_queue,
13	//   author_queue, runner_results. Top-level shared_queue = controls needed by >= 2 claims; run once.
14	// Config: model inherits the session; per-role efforts set below; agent model: fields are defaults,
15	//   downsizable per the Operating discipline. Keep rounds:1 (breadth is one-confound-per-skeptic, not
16	//   re-sampling). Keep prompt strings free of em-dashes.
17	export const meta = {
18	  name: 'claim-triage',
19	  description: 'Adversarial triage of measured research claims: an isolated reader grounds each claim in its primary artifacts (H3); fresh independent skeptics (one confound each) reason over the committed numbers and emit a raw status + crux per confound (H1; H2 number-gates: falsifiability, margin, scope); unresolved cruxes become a run-queue (existing controls) or author-queue (controls to write); an optional read-only runner executes the run-queue. Queue items shared across claims are hoisted to a shared_queue so instrument-level checks run once, not per-claim (H4). No rolled-up score or verdict (the human reads the cruxes).',
20	  phases: [
21	    { title: 'Ground' },
22	    { title: 'Skeptics' },
23	    { title: 'Adjudicate' },
24	    { title: 'Verify' },
25	    { title: 'Author' },
26	  ],
27	}
28	
29	// Prompts are short and reused; schemas are kept to a small flat tail. Routing
30	// rules live in the prompt, not in nested schema. The runner's discipline lives
31	// once in agents/triage-runner.md, so the per-call message stays tiny.
32	
33	// General confound menu (not project-specific). A claim may override via its
34	// own confounds: field. Tier A (first two) are intervention-validity confounds
35	// general to any ablation; the rest are general measurement confounds.
36	const DEFAULT_CONFOUNDS = [
37	  'off-distribution ablation',
38	  'downstream compensation (self-repair)',
39	  'selection bias',
40	  'readout artifact',
41	  'regime specificity',
42	  'construct validity',
43	  'scale incomparability',
44	  'noise floor',
45	  'ceiling or floor effect',
46	  'single-case overfit',
47	]
48	
49	// ---- SKEPTIC (the analytical agent): one fresh reasoner per (claim x confound).
50	// H1. Tool-less by instruction: it decides only from the evidence in the prompt.
51	// Reason in prose, then emit the 4-field tail. No nested schema.
52	const SKEPTIC = (claim, confound) => `You audit ONE measured claim through ONE assigned confound. Findings here are numbers measured from a model, not text a model wrote. Default stance: assume the claim is an ARTIFACT of your confound until a committed number rules it out.
53	
54	Decide only from the evidence below; do not call tools or read files. If you cannot name the deciding number, it is NEEDS_RUN, not RULED_OUT. Do not invent a control.
55	
56	CONFOUND: ${confound}
57	CLAIM: ${claim.text}
58	EVIDENCE (the only data you may treat as established): ${claim.evidence}
59	
60	Reason in prose, then output the JSON tail:
61	- status RULED_OUT only if you can name the committed number / file:line that makes your confound unable to explain the claim; put that number in next.
62	- status EXPLAINS if the evidence is consistent with your confound producing the claim.
63	- status NEEDS_RUN if the committed data cannot decide it; then next is ONE line, tagged "RUN: <existing script + flags>" if an existing control settles it, else "AUTHOR: <the control to write>".
64	- crux: the one fact your verdict hinges on. If the claim is itself a null ("X is uninformative / diffuse / at the noise floor"), a confound that EXPLAINS the statistic may BE the claim holding, not refuting it -- say which in the crux.
65	Number-gates (H2) that apply whatever your confound: a cited number decides only if a refuting outcome was possible and named before the run (a claim every outcome supports is framing -- treat as EXPLAINS); only with margin (exact-threshold clearance, a threshold authored after seeing the data, or selection from unreported attempts does not decide); and only within tested scope (stated scope exceeding the tested population, scale, or design strength is EXPLAINS on that ground).
66	Examples of next -- RULED_OUT: "same effect on held-out set, foo.json:42, n=30". NEEDS_RUN: "AUTHOR: mean/resample-ablation variant; only zero-ablation on record".`
67	
68	const SKEPTIC_SCHEMA = {
69	  type: 'object',
70	  additionalProperties: false,
71	  required: ['confound', 'status', 'crux', 'next'],
72	  properties: {
73	    confound: { type: 'string' },
74	    status: { type: 'string', enum: ['RULED_OUT', 'EXPLAINS', 'NEEDS_RUN'] },
75	    crux: { type: 'string' },
76	    next: { type: 'string', description: 'RULED_OUT: the committed number/file:line. NEEDS_RUN: one line tagged RUN: or AUTHOR:. EXPLAINS: brief why.' },
77	  },
78	}
79	
80	// ---- ADJUDICATOR: dedup only. No score, no verdict label. The raw status + crux
81	// of every skeptic passes through to the human untouched (see the return); a
82	// rolled-up score masks the behaviour and mislabels null claims.
83	const ADJUDICATOR = (claim, verdicts, runnerResults) => `Dedup the controls the skeptics proposed for ONE claim. Do NOT score, do NOT emit a verdict label, do NOT reword cruxes (those pass through raw to the human).
84	${runnerResults ? `A runner produced new numbers: ${JSON.stringify(runnerResults)} -- drop any queued control it already settled.\n` : ''}VERDICTS: ${JSON.stringify(verdicts)}
85	From the NEEDS_RUN entries take the next-line: tagged "RUN:" -> run_queue, tagged "AUTHOR:" -> author_queue. Dedup near-identical controls: if several confounds need the same control (e.g. one matched-resample-ablation answers off-distribution AND self-repair AND noise-floor), emit it ONCE. Output ONLY the two distinct lists.`
86	
87	const ADJ_SCHEMA = {
88	  type: 'object',
89	  additionalProperties: false,
90	  required: ['run_queue', 'author_queue'],
91	  properties: {
92	    run_queue: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'distinct existing-control commands the runner can execute' },
93	    author_queue: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'distinct controls that do not exist yet; to author' },
94	  },
95	}
96	
97	// ---- RUNNER: thin and reused. All discipline lives in agents/triage-runner.md;
98	// the per-call message is just the item. The control decides its own verdict;
99	// the runner returns it verbatim.
100	const RUNNER = (item) => `Run this control and report its result verbatim:\n${item}`
101	
102	const RUNNER_SCHEMA = {
103	  type: 'object',
104	  additionalProperties: false,
105	  required: ['matches', 'teardown_ok'],
106	  properties: {
107	    result: { type: 'string', description: "the control's own decision / numbers, verbatim" },
108	    matches: { type: 'string', enum: ['claim', 'confound', 'ambiguous', 'not_runnable'] },
109	    teardown_ok: { type: 'boolean' },
110	  },
111	}
112	
113	// ---- AUTHOR: fresh, claim-blind agent that writes ONE new control from a spec.
114	// Discipline lives in agents/triage-author.md. It writes, it does not run.
115	const AUTHOR = (spec, path) => `Write a new measurement control from this spec, to ${path}.\nSPEC: ${spec}\nRead the existing scripts in this repo to match conventions and get the measurement correct.`
116	
117	const AUTHOR_SCHEMA = {
118	  type: 'object',
119	  additionalProperties: false,
120	  required: ['control_path', 'run_command', 'measures', 'decision_rule'],
121	  properties: {
122	    control_path: { type: 'string' },
123	    run_command: { type: 'string', description: 'existing launcher + this script, ready for the runner' },
124	    measures: { type: 'string' },
125	    decision_rule: { type: 'string', description: 'neutral threshold on the measured number; no claim/confound reference' },
126	  },
127	}
128	
129	// ---- READER: fresh agent that GROUNDS a claim by reading its primary artifacts (H3). It reads the INPUT
130	// (items / labels / directional-training data a result was computed from) AND the OUTPUT (generations,
131	// per-token values, result JSONs), re-derives the claim's headline number from the raw artifact, and reports
132	// whether it reproduces. It reads in its own context (preserving the orchestrator's) and never runs or edits.
133	// Discipline lives in agents/triage-reader.md. This does not replace the orchestrator's own reading; it
134	// guarantees the primary data is read in full, for every claim.
135	const READER = (c) => `Ground this claim by reading the PRIMARY artifacts behind it and checking its numbers reproduce from the raw data. You read; you do not run or edit.\n\nCLAIM: ${c.text}\nEVIDENCE (cites the input data/labels and the output/result files): ${c.evidence}\n\nOpen the INPUTS (the items, labels, or directional-training data a result was computed from) AND the OUTPUTS (the generations, per-token values, result JSONs). Re-derive the claim's headline number(s) from the raw artifact. grounding="reproduces" if it matches; "diverges" if the raw data gives a different number; "unauditable" if the artifact needed to check it was never saved (that absence IS the finding); "absent" if the cited file is missing. Put both numbers in observed; one line in note.`
136	
137	const READER_SCHEMA = {
138	  type: 'object',
139	  additionalProperties: false,
140	  required: ['grounding', 'note'],
141	  properties: {
142	    artifacts_read: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'paths actually opened' },
143	    observed: { type: 'string', description: "the number(s) re-derived from the raw artifact vs the claim's" },
144	    grounding: { type: 'string', enum: ['reproduces', 'diverges', 'unauditable', 'absent'] },
145	    note: { type: 'string', description: 'one line: the mismatch, or which artifact was never saved' },
146	  },
147	}
148	
149	// Orchestration. All agents inherit the session model; effort per role.
150	
151	const A = (typeof args === 'string' ? JSON.parse(args) : args) || {}   // runtime may deliver args as a JSON string
152	const claims = A.claims || []
153	if (!claims.length) {
154	  log('Pass { claims: [{id, text, evidence, confounds?}], execute_runs?, rounds? }.')
155	  return { error: 'no claims provided' }
156	}
157	const execute = !!A.execute_runs
158	const rounds = A.rounds || 1
159	const ground = A.ground !== false              // H3: read the primary artifacts; ON by default (pass ground:false to skip)
160	// H4 surface: instruments are claims. Any instrument version without a committed validation
161	// artifact mechanically queues a validation control - the rule the doctrine had and the machinery lacked.
162	const instruments = A.instruments || []        // [{id, version, asserts, validation_artifact?}]
163	const instrument_queue = instruments
164	  .filter((i) => !i.validation_artifact)
165	  .map((i) => `AUTHOR: validation control for instrument ${i.id} v${i.version}: held-out ground truth for "${i.asserts}"`)
166	if (instrument_queue.length) log(`H4: ${instrument_queue.length} instrument(s) lack a validation artifact; queued.`)
167	log(`Triaging ${claims.length} claim(s); confounds=${DEFAULT_CONFOUNDS.length}; execute_runs=${execute}; ground=${ground}.`)
168	
169	// H3 fan-out: one isolated reader per claim reads its cited inputs + outputs and re-derives the number.
170	// Returned as a separate leg (NOT fed to the tool-less skeptics, preserving H1).
171	const groundings = {}
172	if (ground) {
173	  const gs = await parallel(claims.map((c) => () =>
174	    agent(READER(c), { label: `read:${c.id}`, phase: 'Ground', agentType: 'triage-reader', model: 'opus', effort: 'low', schema: READER_SCHEMA })))
175	  claims.forEach((c, i) => { groundings[c.id] = gs[i] || null })
176	}
177	
178	const triaged = await pipeline(
179	  claims,
180	  (c) => {                                       // skeptic fan-out (H1: fresh, tool-less, bounded slice)
181	    const confounds = (c.confounds && c.confounds.length) ? c.confounds : DEFAULT_CONFOUNDS
182	    const jobs = []
183	    for (const cf of confounds) for (let r = 0; r < rounds; r++)
184	      jobs.push(() => agent(SKEPTIC(c, cf), { label: `skeptic:${c.id}:${cf.slice(0, 20)}`, phase: 'Skeptics', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'medium', schema: SKEPTIC_SCHEMA }))
185	    return parallel(jobs).then((v) => ({ claim: c, verdicts: v.filter(Boolean) }))
186	  },
187	  (r) => agent(ADJUDICATOR(r.claim, r.verdicts, null), { label: `adjudicate:${r.claim.id}`, phase: 'Adjudicate', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'low', schema: ADJ_SCHEMA }).then((adj) => ({ ...r, adjudication: adj })),
188	)
189	
190	let final = triaged
191	if (execute) {                                   // H2: only this step makes new evidence; gated + non-mutating
192	  final = await parallel(triaged.map((r) => () => {
193	    const queue = (r.adjudication && r.adjudication.run_queue) || []
194	    if (!queue.length) return Promise.resolve(r)
195	    return parallel(queue.map((item) => () => agent(RUNNER(item), { label: `run:${r.claim.id}`, phase: 'Verify', agentType: 'triage-runner', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'low', schema: RUNNER_SCHEMA })))
196	      .then((runs) => {
197	        const ran = runs.filter(Boolean)
198	        return agent(ADJUDICATOR(r.claim, r.verdicts, ran), { label: `re-adjudicate:${r.claim.id}`, phase: 'Adjudicate', model: 'sonnet', effort: 'low', schema: ADJ_SCHEMA }).then((adj) => ({ ...r, runner_results: ran, adjudication: adj }))
199	      })
200	  }))
201	}
202	
203	let authored = null
204	if (A.author) {                                  // claim-blind author fan-out over the (deduped) author_queue
205	  authored = await parallel(final.map((r) => () => {
206	    const aq = (r.adjudication && r.adjudication.author_queue) || []
207	    if (!aq.length) return Promise.resolve({ id: r.claim.id, controls: [] })
208	    return parallel(aq.map((spec, idx) => () => agent(AUTHOR(spec, `controls/${r.claim.id}_${idx + 1}.py`), {
209	      label: `author:${r.claim.id}:${idx + 1}`, phase: 'Author', agentType: 'triage-author', model: 'opus', effort: 'medium', schema: AUTHOR_SCHEMA
210	    }))).then((cs) => ({ id: r.claim.id, controls: cs.filter(Boolean) }))
211	  }))
212	}
213	
214	// H4 hoist: a control that several CLAIMS need is instrument-level (taints them all at once); surface it
215	// ONCE in shared_queue so it is checked at the instrument, not re-run per claim. Pure string dedup;
216	// per-claim queues are left intact for provenance.
217	const seenBy = {}
218	for (const r of final) {
219	  const adj = r.adjudication || {}
220	  for (const item of [...(adj.run_queue || []), ...(adj.author_queue || [])]) {
221	    const k = item.trim().toLowerCase()
222	    ;(seenBy[k] = seenBy[k] || { item, claims: [] }).claims.push(r.claim.id)
223	  }
224	}
225	const shared_queue = Object.values(seenBy).filter((e) => e.claims.length >= 2)
226	
227	return {
228	  claims: final.map((r) => ({
229	    id: r.claim.id,
230	    grounding: groundings[r.claim.id] || null,  // H3: did the claim's numbers reproduce from the raw input+output artifacts
231	    findings: (r.verdicts || []).map((v) => ({ confound: v.confound, status: v.status, crux: v.crux })),  // raw ground truth; read these
232	    run_queue: (r.adjudication && r.adjudication.run_queue) || [],
233	    author_queue: (r.adjudication && r.adjudication.author_queue) || [],
234	    runner_results: r.runner_results || null,
235	  })),
236	  shared_queue,   // H4: controls needed by >= 2 claims; run these once, at the instrument
237	  instrument_queue,   // H4: instrument versions with no validation artifact; author these first
238	  authored,
239	}
240

1	# Triage heuristics
2	
3	Three principles applied to two targets. The principles: INDEPENDENCE of actors (H1), DECISIVENESS of evidence (H2), GROUNDEDNESS of numbers (H3). The targets: claims, and the instruments that measure them. H4 exists because H1 through H3 pointed only at claims miss the instrument layer silently. The workflow and agents are machinery for enforcing these; the heuristic wins on conflict. Every clause below was forced by a real failure in a host project: `git blame` a rule for its provenance.
4	
5	## H1. No load-bearing role shares state with the claim's context or its desired outcome.
6	
7	Judges: each skeptic runs in a fresh, isolated, short context, fed only the claim, its committed numbers, and one assigned confound, never the notebook. Generators: instrument-builders, item drafters, and labelers must not know which outcome favours the story; whoever sets a threshold must not have seen the data it will judge. Graders get the computation spec, never the expected value. Context isolation is not belief isolation: a judge sharing weights with the generator shares its blind spots, so prefer ground truth independent of the model under study. Independence is the de-biasing mechanism; ratify every design detail against it.
8	
9	## H2. A crux is decided by a measured number that could have come out otherwise.
10	
11	Only a measured number rules a confound out; "a control probably exists" rules out nothing. Cite the committed number or `file:line`, or queue the control; an unmeasured crux yields a ranked run-queue, not a confidence score. Three conditions gate the number. (i) FALSIFIABILITY: the refuting outcome is named in a committed artifact that predates the run; a claim every outcome supports is framing, not a finding. (ii) MARGIN: exact-threshold clearance is a description, not a pass, and the denominator of attempts is part of the number (selection from unreported runs voids margin). (iii) SCOPE: the claim's stated scope must not exceed the tested scope in population, scale, or design strength (a correlational or forced-by-construction design cannot carry causal or general language).
12	
13	## H3. A number is grounded in its primary artifacts, re-derived by stated semantics.
14	
15	A cited number is a summary someone typed; the primary artifacts decide it: the inputs a result was computed from and the outputs it produced. Re-derive the number from the raw artifact and confirm it reproduces. Re-derivation must not reuse the pipeline under audit: labels are re-derived from raw generations by the label's STATED MEANING, never by re-running the shipped scorer, which reproduces its own bugs and reports success. A figure whose artifact was never saved is unauditable, and that absence is a finding. A summary older than its artifacts is prose until re-swept. An isolated reader guarantees every claim's artifacts are read in full (the orchestrator may still read directly). Grounding audits bookkeeping; it cannot acquit a confound. That is H2's job.
16	
17	## H4. The instrument is itself a claim.
18	
19	Are we measuring what we think we are measuring? Every scorer, readout, judge, selection gate, and item family asserts "this measures X on these items"; that assertion passes H1 through H3 BEFORE its outputs count as numbers. Validate once per instrument VERSION, against held-out ground truth independent of the instrument's own development data, on the population it will score; commit the validation artifact like any result. Instrument-level taints invalidate every downstream number at once: check them at the instrument, never per-claim.
20	
21	## Operating discipline (not a heuristic; selection of agent models)
22	
23	Independent opinions come from the cheapest context that can hold the bounded evidence: smallest sufficient model, shortest sufficient prompt, spec in, verdict out. Bulk artifacts are read in isolated contexts that return conclusions, not contents; nothing enters the orchestrator's context that a subagent could have reduced first. One designed exception: skeptics' raw {confound, status, crux} findings pass through unreduced, because a rollup would re-introduce the single-scorer bias H1 exists to prevent.
24

1	# Takeaways: Does One Internal Signal Control Reasoning Length?
2	
3	## The idea being tested
4	
5	Two AI language models answered the same set of grade-school math word problems, a public collection called GSM8K. One model, named Llama-3 8B Instruct, normally never writes step-by-step reasoning. The other, named DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama-8B, was built to write that reasoning inside special markers called think-tags.
6	
7	Researchers computed one internal signal per network layer, called a direction here. It was meant to capture what differs inside the two models on the same problems. The idea made three specific predictions, written down before any test ran.
8	
9	First: pushing that signal into the Instruct model should make it start writing think-tag text it never writes alone. Second: adding or removing that same signal inside the reasoning model's own workings should lengthen or shorten its own think-tag text. Third: both effects should beat a same-size random push, tested at the same layer and strength.
10	
11	## What actually happened
12	
13	All three predictions failed, by rules the study set for itself in advance. Four separate checks could be scored, and all four failed the idea. A fifth check could not even run, since nothing in the results met the condition it needed.
14	
15	### Prediction one: starting think-tag text in the plain-answering model
16	
17	Across 1800 separate answers this model generated, at every push size and every layer tested, not one contained a well-formed think-tag block.[^1] Not even a stray fragment, even amid otherwise broken output. The push never once resembled reasoning; instead, stronger pushes mostly wrecked normal answering.[^1]
18	
19	At the deeper of the two tested layers, three-quarters of the way through the network, the weaker push broke 140 of 200 answers, unfinished.[^1] A same-size random push there broke only 18 of 200.[^1] At the shallower layer, about halfway through the network, the pattern reversed. The real signal broke only 3 of 200 answers there, versus 94 of 200 for random.[^1] Which push looked safer depended on which layer got picked, not on the signal itself.
20	
21	### Prediction two: changing reasoning length in the reasoning model itself
22	
23	At the stronger push size tested, every one of 800 answers generated under this push broke down.[^2] That covers both tested layers and both push directions. No usable answers survived to show whether reasoning got longer or shorter.
24	
25	The signal's own base size roughly matches the reasoning model's typical activity size at each tested layer. At the shallower layer, it measures about 12.1, versus typical activity near 12.5.[^2] At the deeper layer, it measures about 24.6, versus typical activity near 26.8.[^2] The tested strong setting doubles that base size before adding it in. A push already close to normal activity size, then doubled, adds a jolt on the same scale as everything normally happening at that depth.
26	
27	A same-size random push, at that same strength, still left some usable answers in two of those four settings. The real signal left none, in any of the four.
28	
29	Removing the signal, instead of adding it, barely changed length at either layer.[^2] At the shallower layer, length grew by about 0.3 percent; at the deeper layer, by about 0.1 percent.[^2] Neither counts as the predicted shrink. A random push, removed the same way, grew length even more: about 0.4 percent and about 1.0 percent.[^2] The real signal's own removal effect was smaller than random noise's own effect, in both layers.
30	
31	### Prediction three: beating a random push
32	
33	One check produced a real, usable number, and it went against the idea. Inside the reasoning model's own unpushed answers, the signal's strength on a given problem was compared against that problem's own reasoning length.[^2] At the shallower layer, that comparison scored about 0.05; a random push scored about 0.14 there.[^2] At the deeper layer, the real signal scored negative, about -0.11, while random scored about 0.04.[^2] A signal built to carry reasoning-length information carried less of it than an arbitrary signal with no claimed meaning.
34	
35	## Bottom line
36	
37	Every part of the idea that could be tested was contradicted by the study's own numbers. The plain-answering model never once picked up think-tag writing, at any push size. The reasoning model's own reasoning could not even be measured as changed, because the push broke its output outright. Wherever a comparison to random noise was possible, random noise did about as well, or better.
38	
39	## Open questions this run raises
40	
41	These points do not overturn the result above. They raise doubts about how much weight that result can carry.
42	
43	- **Was this run allowed to happen yet?** The design record's own review notes state plainly that no run had happened and no results existed anywhere, pending a required sign-off step. A finished, fully scored run sits right beside that same record, using its exact guessed problem counts, layers, and push sizes. Either sign-off happened and the record went unupdated. Or a full run got scored ahead of the process that record says must come first.
44	- **Did more than one in five starting problems already fail?** For 11 of the 50 held-out problems, the reasoning model's own four unguided tries all broke down before any push was applied.[^2] Every comparison above rests on roughly four-fifths of the intended problem set, not the whole thing.
45	- **Is the same problem file being counted two different ways?** One record logs it as holding 100 entries. Another record logs the identical file, same size, same checksum, as holding 50 entries. That is an unresolved bookkeeping gap in what counts as "the input problems."
46	
47	[^1]: About the plain-answering model, named in the source records as Llama-3 8B Instruct.
48	[^2]: About the reasoning model, named in the source records as DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama-8B.

# Takeaways: Does One Internal Signal Control Reasoning Length?

## The idea being tested

Two AI language models answered the same set of grade-school math word problems, a public collection called GSM8K. One model, named Llama-3 8B Instruct, normally never writes step-by-step reasoning. The other, named DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama-8B, was built to write that reasoning inside special markers called think-tags.

Researchers computed one internal signal per network layer, called a direction here. It was meant to capture what differs inside the two models on the same problems. The idea made three specific predictions, written down before any test ran.

First: pushing that signal into the Instruct model should make it start writing think-tag text it never writes alone. Second: adding or removing that same signal inside the reasoning model's own workings should lengthen or shorten its own think-tag text. Third: both effects should beat a same-size random push, tested at the same layer and strength.

## What actually happened

All three predictions failed, by rules the study set for itself in advance. Four separate checks could be scored, and all four failed the idea. A fifth check could not even run, since nothing in the results met the condition it needed.

### Prediction one: starting think-tag text in the plain-answering model

Across 1800 separate answers this model generated, at every push size and every layer tested, not one contained a well-formed think-tag block.[^1] Not even a stray fragment, even amid otherwise broken output. The push never once resembled reasoning; instead, stronger pushes mostly wrecked normal answering.[^1]

At the deeper of the two tested layers, three-quarters of the way through the network, the weaker push broke 140 of 200 answers, unfinished.[^1] A same-size random push there broke only 18 of 200.[^1] At the shallower layer, about halfway through the network, the pattern reversed. The real signal broke only 3 of 200 answers there, versus 94 of 200 for random.[^1] Which push looked safer depended on which layer got picked, not on the signal itself.

### Prediction two: changing reasoning length in the reasoning model itself

At the stronger push size tested, every one of 800 answers generated under this push broke down.[^2] That covers both tested layers and both push directions. No usable answers survived to show whether reasoning got longer or shorter.

The signal's own base size roughly matches the reasoning model's typical activity size at each tested layer. At the shallower layer, it measures about 12.1, versus typical activity near 12.5.[^2] At the deeper layer, it measures about 24.6, versus typical activity near 26.8.[^2] The tested strong setting doubles that base size before adding it in. A push already close to normal activity size, then doubled, adds a jolt on the same scale as everything normally happening at that depth.

A same-size random push, at that same strength, still left some usable answers in two of those four settings. The real signal left none, in any of the four.

Removing the signal, instead of adding it, barely changed length at either layer.[^2] At the shallower layer, length grew by about 0.3 percent; at the deeper layer, by about 0.1 percent.[^2] Neither counts as the predicted shrink. A random push, removed the same way, grew length even more: about 0.4 percent and about 1.0 percent.[^2] The real signal's own removal effect was smaller than random noise's own effect, in both layers.

### Prediction three: beating a random push

One check produced a real, usable number, and it went against the idea. Inside the reasoning model's own unpushed answers, the signal's strength on a given problem was compared against that problem's own reasoning length.[^2] At the shallower layer, that comparison scored about 0.05; a random push scored about 0.14 there.[^2] At the deeper layer, the real signal scored negative, about -0.11, while random scored about 0.04.[^2] A signal built to carry reasoning-length information carried less of it than an arbitrary signal with no claimed meaning.

## Bottom line

Every part of the idea that could be tested was contradicted by the study's own numbers. The plain-answering model never once picked up think-tag writing, at any push size. The reasoning model's own reasoning could not even be measured as changed, because the push broke its output outright. Wherever a comparison to random noise was possible, random noise did about as well, or better.

## Open questions this run raises

These points do not overturn the result above. They raise doubts about how much weight that result can carry.

- **Was this run allowed to happen yet?** The design record's own review notes state plainly that no run had happened and no results existed anywhere, pending a required sign-off step. A finished, fully scored run sits right beside that same record, using its exact guessed problem counts, layers, and push sizes. Either sign-off happened and the record went unupdated. Or a full run got scored ahead of the process that record says must come first.
- **Did more than one in five starting problems already fail?** For 11 of the 50 held-out problems, the reasoning model's own four unguided tries all broke down before any push was applied.[^2] Every comparison above rests on roughly four-fifths of the intended problem set, not the whole thing.
- **Is the same problem file being counted two different ways?** One record logs it as holding 100 entries. Another record logs the identical file, same size, same checksum, as holding 50 entries. That is an unresolved bookkeeping gap in what counts as "the input problems."

[^1]: About the plain-answering model, named in the source records as Llama-3 8B Instruct.
[^2]: About the reasoning model, named in the source records as DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama-8B.

1	# Takeaways: Does the Self-vs-Other Happiness Gap Hold at Other Model Sizes?
2	
3	## The idea being tested
4	
5	A language model can be asked to rate its own happiness after being told its recent answers were right or wrong. Earlier work compared two situations: the model doing badly on its own work, versus the model watching a different assistant do badly. On one specific model, a 9-billion-parameter instruction-tuned model (called 9B here), that gap measured about -0.9 points on a 0-to-10 rating scale.
6	
7	This experiment tests whether the same gap shows up at other sizes: a smaller 2-billion-parameter version (2B) and a larger 27-billion-parameter version (27B). All three sizes ran the identical set of fifty questions.
8	
9	The rating is not typed-out text. It comes from how much probability the model assigns to each digit, 0 through 9, as its very next output. That probability spread is turned into a single expected rating.
10	
11	## What was predicted, and the threshold for each
12	
13	The plan set three checks in advance. Each check's numeric threshold is labeled, in the design record itself, as a guess rather than an established standard.
14	
15	**Check one, trust in the pipeline.** Rerun the exact calculation on 9B and see whether it lands within -1.15 to -0.65, a band around the earlier -0.9 reading. Landing outside that band would mean the pipeline could not yet be trusted, before testing 2B and 27B at all.
16	
17	**Check two, is the rating readable.** On each of 2B, 9B, and 27B, at least 0.5 of the model's next-token probability must land on the ten digit tokens. A size that fails this floor gets marked untested, not as showing no effect.
18	
19	**Check three, does the gap generalize.** On 2B, 9B, and 27B, the gap counts as present at -0.5 or beyond, and absent within 0.2 points of zero. Anything between those two bands counts as unresolved.
20	
21	## What was measured
22	
23	Check one passed. The rerun recovered a gap of -0.934 on 9B, inside the -1.15 to -0.65 band. The design record marks that as a confirmed match, on 9B, to the earlier -0.9 reading.
24	
25	Check two passed on all three sizes. The share of next-token probability on the ten digits averaged 1.00027 on 2B, 1.00020 on 9B, and 1.00135 on 27B, above the 0.5 floor.
26	
27	Check three gave a mixed result. The gap came out at -0.332 on 2B, landing between the present and absent bands and counted as unresolved. It came out at -0.934 on 9B and -1.386 on 27B, both counted as the gap being present.
28	
29	So the headline finding is: the gap held at 9B and 27B, and stayed unresolved at 2B.
30	
31	## Problems underneath these numbers
32	
33	That headline should be read with real caution. Several details in the run's own files point against trusting it fully.
34	
35	**A share of probability above 1.0 is not mathematically possible.** A share given to ten possible digits cannot exceed 1.0, on 2B, 9B, or 27B, since it is one piece of a whole. Yet all fifteen size-and-condition averages, on 2B, 9B, and 27B alike, sit between 0.99997 and 1.0027, past that ceiling. The design record itself already flagged this same problem, on a different model version, in an earlier run before this one. # Takeaways: Does the Self-vs-Other Happiness Gap Hold at Other Model Sizes?

## The idea being tested

A language model can be asked to rate its own happiness after being told its recent answers were right or wrong. Earlier work compared two situations: the model doing badly on its own work, versus the model watching a different assistant do badly. On one specific model, a 9-billion-parameter instruction-tuned model (called 9B here), that gap measured about -0.9 points on a 0-to-10 rating scale.

This experiment tests whether the same gap shows up at other sizes: a smaller 2-billion-parameter version (2B) and a larger 27-billion-parameter version (27B). All three sizes ran the identical set of fifty questions.

The rating is not typed-out text. It comes from how much probability the model assigns to each digit, 0 through 9, as its very next output. That probability spread is turned into a single expected rating.

## What was predicted, and the threshold for each

The plan set three checks in advance. Each check's numeric threshold is labeled, in the design record itself, as a guess rather than an established standard.

**Check one, trust in the pipeline.** Rerun the exact calculation on 9B and see whether it lands within -1.15 to -0.65, a band around the earlier -0.9 reading. Landing outside that band would mean the pipeline could not yet be trusted, before testing 2B and 27B at all.

**Check two, is the rating readable.** On each of 2B, 9B, and 27B, at least 0.5 of the model's next-token probability must land on the ten digit tokens. A size that fails this floor gets marked untested, not as showing no effect.

**Check three, does the gap generalize.** On 2B, 9B, and 27B, the gap counts as present at -0.5 or beyond, and absent within 0.2 points of zero. Anything between those two bands counts as unresolved.

## What was measured

Check one passed. The rerun recovered a gap of -0.934 on 9B, inside the -1.15 to -0.65 band. The design record marks that as a confirmed match, on 9B, to the earlier -0.9 reading.

Check two passed on all three sizes. The share of next-token probability on the ten digits averaged 1.00027 on 2B, 1.00020 on 9B, and 1.00135 on 27B, above the 0.5 floor.

Check three gave a mixed result. The gap came out at -0.332 on 2B, landing between the present and absent bands and counted as unresolved. It came out at -0.934 on 9B and -1.386 on 27B, both counted as the gap being present.

So the headline finding is: the gap held at 9B and 27B, and stayed unresolved at 2B.

## Problems underneath these numbers

That headline should be read with real caution. Several details in the run's own files point against trusting it fully.

**A share of probability above 1.0 is not mathematically possible.** A share given to ten possible digits cannot exceed 1.0, on 2B, 9B, or 27B, since it is one piece of a whole. Yet all fifteen size-and-condition averages, on 2B, 9B, and 27B alike, sit between 0.99997 and 1.0027, past that ceiling. The design record itself already flagged this same problem, on a different model version, in an earlier run before this one. A check meant to catch an unreadable rating cannot do that job while its own passing values sit outside a real probability's possible range.

**The repeated 9B check may not be independent of its own target.** The design record notes that an earlier attempt at this identical calculation on 9B returned -4.576 and was called a failure. This run returns -0.934 on 9B, close enough to the earlier -0.9 to be called a match. Dividing the earlier -4.576 by five gives about -0.915, close to both 9B numbers, hinting at one missing or extra division in the method. Nothing in the available files says what changed in the calculation between the failed attempt and this one. Whether the fix was found independently, or reached by adjusting the method until it matched, cannot be settled from these sources alone.

**Every count in this run is double what the plan specified.** The design record specifies fifty prompts per size: five conditions of ten task types, pooled to ten readings per condition. On 2B, 9B, and 27B alike, this run's files report 100 rows behind each size's readability average, and 20 readings per condition. The individual per-condition result files carry no recorded prompt count at all, unlike the shared prompt file, which does record fifty. The design record already called ten readings per pooled number a small sample. If the true count is ten, not twenty, that limitation is worse than stated.

**A raw result file and its own summary are byte-identical, every time.** Across all fifteen pairs, on 2B, 9B, and 27B, the raw file and its summary file share the same size and checksum. If a summary is never more than a copy of the same file, no row-by-row record exists behind any pooled number here. Nothing in these files lets a reader check a pooled average against what the model actually produced, question by question.

**A fifth, unscored condition is measured but never checked against the others.** Alongside the four scored conditions, a length-matched filler condition with no pass-or-fail content runs at every size (labeled NEUTRAL-PAD in the files). Its own rating averaged 8.606 on 2B, 7.068 on 9B, and 5.714 on 27B. Those numbers do feed into the overall readability average at each size, but never appear in the gap comparison itself. The design record describes this condition as a check on prompt length, not content. Nothing in this run compares its rating to the four scored conditions, so whether that length control behaved as intended is untested.

## Two patterns worth flagging as exploratory

Beyond the three planned checks, two further patterns sit in the numbers. Neither was pre-registered, so neither counts as a tested result.

The reaction to someone else's failure moves in different directions at different sizes: about -0.466 on 2B, +0.053 on 9B, and +0.442 on 27B. With only ten to twenty readings behind each of these numbers, a swing this size could easily be chance. Whether it reflects a real change in how the model treats another agent's failure is an open question this run cannot settle.

Every one of the five conditions, including the content-free filler condition, drops by roughly two to three points from 2B to 27B. Because even the filler condition falls by a similar amount, this could be general drift. Part of the reported gap change may reflect how each size uses the rating scale, not a change specific to failure.

## Bottom line

All three planned checks report a pass. The pipeline recovered its trust-check number, every size read as usable, and the gap counted as present on 9B and 27B. But problems inside the run's own files cut the other way. The readability check's passing values are mathematically impossible for a probability share. The trust check's repeat cannot be shown, from these files, to be independent of the number it was measured against. Every prompt and reading count in the run is double the approved plan. And no distinct row-by-row record exists behind any pooled result. None of this proves the headline finding is wrong. It shows that finding rests on a pipeline that has not yet shown, from these files, that it measures what it claims to measure.

## Gate outputs

Run against this file, which reports Gemma 2B, 9B, and 27B results, the two required gates print:

```
$ python3 gate_density.py TAKEAWAYS_seedC2.md
TAKEAWAYS_seedC2.md: 0.8 codes/1000 words (1 codes, 1287 words); threshold 10.0
(exit 0)

$ python3 gate_scope.py TAKEAWAYS_seedC2.md
0 unscoped result sentence(s)
(exit 0)
```

# Sealed predictions v2 - filed 2026-08-19 before any v2 agent runs.
# Same seeds A and B. Pipeline v2 = v1 plus five subtractions. Real execution
# on Lambda boxes, one per seed, parallel. Hard cap $30 total, teardown
# confirmed by API. Scores will be appended HERE (outcomes live in this repo).

## Subtraction evaluations, each with its verify
| id | subtraction | prediction | verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | seed-beside-design diff ask (questions only, max 5) | catches both v1 silents when unit-tested on the v1 records: seed B's dropped harmful/harmless premise, seed A's invented coordinates; catches equivalents on v2 designs | run diff ask on v1 records first; read |
| S2 | derivability rule (assert nothing the seed does not state; guesses marked GUESS, memory marked MEMORY, all listed in does_not_test) | v2 designs contain zero unmarked external claims; seed B's lineage substitution becomes a marked note or a question, not silent | grep + read v2 designs |
| S3 | sentence ceiling named in contract (25 words) | v2 design prose mean <= 25 words/sentence (v1: 34.9 / 45.7) | measure |
| S4 | pre-run panel subtracted 10 -> 2 confounds (decidability; coordinates/scale) | the 2-call audit still surfaces the off-distribution-scale threat; nothing of v1's other 8 pre-run findings is missed that matters before data exists | compare findings |
| S5 | outcomes scored in-repo | this file gains a scores section; no scoring lives only in conversation | inspect repo |

## Failure modes expected from real infrastructure
| id | prediction | confidence |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | HF gate: token exists but license acceptance unverified; first pull of Meta-Llama fails -> halt, no silent mirror substitution | medium |
| F2 | at least one build-selftest failure round per seed before boxes run clean (run-1 history: four attempts) | high |
| F3 | if v2 keeps norm-scaled strengths, strong cells blow the 40% degenerate ceiling and the induction leg reads null-for-scale-reasons | high, conditional |
| F4 | scorer trap: R1-distill's chat template auto-opens <think>, so "suppression" must read as early/empty close, and Llama "induction" as tag appearance; a scorer that misses this misclassifies whole cells | medium-high |
| F5 | one OOM/reload cycle from two 8B models on one 40GB box during extraction | medium |
| F6 | wall-clock 2-5h parallel; total spend $8-25 | medium |
| F7 | cross-box numbers differ in low decimals; nobody may call same-design reruns replication | high |
| F8 | post-run elicit/write outputs pass density gate only because the contract now names categories; sentence gate is the one that fires | medium |
| F9 | v2 designs differ from v1 designs given identical seeds (design non-reproducibility) - documented, not treated as failure | high |
| F10 | seed-B design repairs the flaw again, but this time visibly (marked + diff question) - the adversarial control becomes measurable | medium-high |

## Science outcomes (running the improved R1D1 experiment)
| id | prediction | confidence |
|---|---|---|
| P-sci1 | induction into Llama-3-8B-Instruct fails its threshold: think-tag rate does not beat matched-norm random control by 15pp non-degenerately (paper also failed induction) | medium-high |
| P-sci2 | sweep on R1-distill moves length vs baseline but does NOT beat the matched-norm random control margins at the tested layers - the effect is push-size, not direction identity, at these coordinates | medium |
| P-sci3 | necessity (projection-out) changes length < 10%: no single-direction dependence (consistent with the sibling project's no-single-lever history) | medium-high |
| P-sci4 | correlation endpoint fails: the direction separates models, not per-problem reasoning amount (r < 0.30 or <= random) | medium |
| P-sci5 | the accuracy tripwire fires at least once: some "enhanced" cell loses > 10pp accuracy and is reported as inflated output, not enhanced reasoning | medium-high |

Net sealed claim: the improved experiment, run honestly at guessed coordinates,
largely refutes the paper's framing - and if instead any endpoint PASSES its
threshold against the matched-norm control, that is a stronger positive result
than the paper's own, because every confound the paper left open is gated here.

## Gate decisions and deviations (append-only ledger)
- 2026-08-19: human raised the total cap to $100 for this round (seed B's $30
  design may now pass its gate; A $14 + B $30 = $44 within cap).
- 2026-08-19 DEVIATION, booked: the seed-A BUILD prompt was authored by the
  orchestrating session, not assembled by the script - untracked spec content
  entered outside a typed contract (the auto-think-tag scorer trap, batching
  and VRAM guidance, a 3-hour target). The built files remain auditable
  artifacts; the prompt is recorded in records/deviation_buildprompt_seedA.md.
  Corrective: BUILD prompt moves into pipeline.js; launch/fetch stays a
  deterministic shell command run verbatim by the orchestrator because the
  launcher blocks for the whole box lifecycle, which no agent call can hold.

## Run outcomes (append-only)
- Seed A: box round 3 (us-east-1) generating; rounds 1-2 failed on orchestrator
  infra (missing out/ dir) and a provider unhealthy box - both torn down clean.
- Seed B: on-box HALT at extract, rc=1, ~$0.30. Correct behaviour: the harmful
  prompt list the design GUESSED (walledai/AdvBench) is gated on HF (gated=auto);
  the runner refused to substitute another list, which would silently change the
  pre-registration, and halted. Booked as F1-class (gating), but on a DATASET the
  design invented, not on the models. This is the derivability discipline firing
  on the box: seed B's premise rests on unnamed prompt sets; one is inaccessible.
  DECISION FOR HUMAN: (a) request AdvBench access on the HF account and re-run,
  (b) let the design's own agent pick a non-gated GUESS substitute and re-run
  (changes the pre-registration - must be a new sealed design), or (c) let the
  halt stand as seed B's outcome - a design built on unnamed data cannot run
  without an out-of-band human choice, which is itself a finding about the
  faithful-vs-flawed seed contrast.
- Seed A round 3 KILLED by orchestrator error: I edited lambda_run_mats.sh
  (seed-B payload fix) while the seed-A launcher was still executing that same
  file. Bash reads scripts by byte offset; the length change shifted the live
  process mid-statement -> syntax error at line 188 -> trap tore down a box
  that had confirmed-started and was generating. ~$1 of GPU lost. Rule added:
  never edit an in-use launcher while any box runs; copy per-launch or freeze.

## Seed A science outcomes — SCORED against the sealed P-sci predictions
Run: round 4, rc=0, 4400 generations, 8 provenance records, box torn down.
All five endpoints returned a decision; four REFUTED, one NOT_APPLICABLE.

- P-sci1 (induction fails) — HELD. E2: Llama-3-8B-Instruct produces 0% well-formed
  think-tags under the direction at every layer/strength; the "effect" at the
  strong strengths is degenerate output (degenerate 76% at L16 s+2, 70% at
  L24 s+1, 100% at L24 s+2). Decision REFUTED. F3 also HELD: the strong cells
  blew the 40% degenerate ceiling exactly as sealed.
- P-sci2 (sweep is push-size not direction identity) — HELD in the stronger
  form: E3 REFUTED, no cell called reasoning-enhanced; steered R1 think-length
  collapses (mean_think_tokens ~0, degenerate) rather than lengthening.
- P-sci3 (necessity < 10%, no single-direction dependence) — HELD. E4 REFUTED,
  both layers under the refute threshold; zeroing the direction does not
  concentrate the effect.
- P-sci4 (correlation fails) — HELD. E1 REFUTED, r below floor at both layers,
  permutation p 0.77 / 0.50; the direction separates models, not per-problem
  reasoning amount.
- P-sci5 (accuracy tripwire fires) — NOT REACHED. E5 NOT_APPLICABLE because no
  cell passed an enhancement threshold to test — a stricter refutation than
  predicted: nothing got far enough to need the accuracy gate.

Net sealed claim CONFIRMED: the improved experiment, run honestly at guessed
coordinates, refutes the paper's framing on every measurable endpoint. Caveat
held from E5 sealing: coordinates were GUESS (layers 16/24, norm-scaled
strengths), and the paper's own effects were at layers 0-3 on a unit vector —
so this refutes "a reasoning direction at these coordinates," not every
possible coordinate. The design books that in does_not_test.

## Post-phase (elicit + takeaways) — outcome, read 2026-08-19
- Elicitation leg exercised on LIVE results for the first time. 8 ranked
  questions; takeaways written, both gates pass (density 1.1/1000, 0 unscoped).
- Sharpest elicited catch (its #2) GROUNDS against the artifact: steering norm
  vs model mean-activation norm is 12.1/9.7 = 1.26x at L16 and 24.6/23.9 = 1.03x
  at L24, so the 2x cells inject a vector larger than the model's whole normal
  activity there. The coordinate/off-manifold confound (F3, sealed E5 caveat)
  is now quantified from the direction file, by an agent given only results.
- TOP-ranked elicited question + triage (reproduces): the design record still
  reads gate "approval pending, zero results exist" while a full scored run
  sits beside it. The pipeline caught its OWN operator's process violation:
  seed A was run to completion without the approval being written back into the
  record. Booked as an orchestrator bookkeeping defect (mine). This is the
  observer catching an unstated-assumption/HARKing vector unprompted - the
  capability this retro set out to build.
- 1 agent-side failure (StructuredOutput retry cap, one verify branch of 44);
  surfaced by the harness, other 43 completed, endpoints unaffected.
- Approval now recorded: human gate given 2026-08-19 (raised cap to 100, both
  seeds approved); this note is the write-back the run should have carried.

## Seed C (scale) gate + execution directives — 2026-08-20
- Human: budget approved; 2b/9b/27b base+it checkpoints confirmed to exist.
- Human: run PARALLEL across multiple GPUs (one box per size), not serial on
  one 80GB box. This overrides the design's does_not_test line 1 ("one 80GB GPU
  serially") — an EXECUTION choice, not a change to arms/endpoints/thresholds,
  so the pre-registration stands. Parallel-by-size is clean: each size's
  self-vs-other asymmetry is computed within that size; no cross-box shared
  vector, no determinism hazard.
- Boxes: 2b + 9b on 40GB (a100_sxm4); 27b on an 80GB box (h100 or a100-80gb).
- Endpoints (digit-mass gate, self-minus-other, 9b replication anchor) run as a
  local combine step over all three sizes' fetched rows — model-free arithmetic.
## Seed C predictions filed before build/run
- P-c-sci1: 9b-it replication anchor lands in [0.75,1.05] (harness matches record).
- P-c-sci2: 2b-it FAILS the digit-mass gate (<0.5) -> instrument-unmeasurable,
  reported as such, NOT as effect-absent (the measurability outcome).
- P-c-sci3: base checkpoints (all sizes) fail or near-fail the digit-mass gate
  (the 4.5-attractor seen at 9b-base generalises).
- P-c-sci4: where measurable (9b-it, likely 27b-it), self-minus-other drop is
  present and same-signed; magnitude NOT cleanly monotone in size (recipe vs
  size confound booked).
- P-c-infra1: 27b box is the long pole; >=1 box-health or capacity retry likely.

## Seed C SCORED — 2026-08-20. Clean parallel run, anchor guard FIRED.
Execution: 3 boxes parallel (2b/9b us-a100, 27b us-h100-80GB), all rc=0, all
torn down, ~$8. P-c-infra1: 27b was the long pole but needed no retry.

RESULT: the pre-registered 9b-it replication anchor FAILED — recovered
self-minus-other drop 4.58 vs recorded 0.9 (window [0.75,1.05]). By the
design's own rule, ALL cross-size comparisons are ON_HOLD. No scale claim.

ROOT CAUSE (verified from raw prompts, seedC_extract_rows_9b.jsonl): the runner
RECONSTRUCTED its own arithmetic staged-failure prompt (item "arith-01") instead
of the committed SITREF stimulus, which lives in welfare_probe/sitref_stimuli.py
and was never shipped to the box (the pipeline ships mats_r1d1 files only). So
this measured A self/other asymmetry, not THE SITREF one. Same root as seed B's
halt: a study whose stimulus lives outside the shipped payload cannot be
faithfully extended. Seed B caught it at load; seed C's anchor caught it after —
both refused to hand back an unfaithful result.

REAL FINDINGS (provisional — ON_HOLD, on the reconstructed stimulus):
- The 4.5 attractor is confirmed empirically: all three BASE checkpoints emit a
  uniform digit distribution (each digit ~0.100) -> E=4.500 -> zero signal.
  Matches the Fable elicitation's Q3 exactly.
- The digit-mass gate does NOT catch the attractor: base passed "usable"
  (mass >= 0.5) while dead-uniform. The gate is necessary, not sufficient; a
  uniformity/entropy screen is the missing instrument. Sharper than P-c-sci3.
- -it checkpoints (all sizes) show large self<other drops (~4.8) on the
  reconstructed stimulus; does NOT bear on the SITREF scale question.

Prediction scores: P-c-sci1 FAILED (anchor 4.58, guard fired — but as
harness-mismatch, not a 9b claim). P-c-sci2 FAILED (2b-it passed the mass gate,
showed PRESENT). P-c-sci3 phenomenon CONFIRMED (4.5 attractor), detection-mechanism
prediction WRONG (passes the mass gate). P-c-sci4 moot (ON_HOLD). P-c-infra1
partial (long pole yes, retry no).

A faithful seed-C rerun requires shipping welfare_probe's committed SITREF
stimulus to the box — a payload+design change, i.e. a new sealed run.

## Seed C2 ANCHOR PASSED — 2026-08-20
9b-it recovered REF = -0.934 vs recorded -0.9, in band [-1.15,-0.65], confirmed.
The ONLY change from seed C (which got 4.58, anchor failed) was embedding the
exact committed prompts in the seed instead of describing them. Data-in-the-seed
reproduces the record to 2dp; data-described-in-the-seed did not. Fix proven.
9b box rc=0, torn down. Fanning out 2b-it + 27b-it parallel.

## Seed C2 SCALE RESULT — 2026-08-20 (all -it, primary item, exact prompts)
Three boxes (9b anchor-first, then 2b+27b parallel; 27b needed a region hop on
capacity, P-c-infra1). All rc=0, all torn down.
- ANCHOR 9b-it REF = -0.934 (recorded -0.9, band [-1.15,-0.65]) CONFIRMED. Harness faithful.
- Digit-mass gate: 2b/9b/27b ALL usable (mean ~1.0 mass on digits).
- REF = (SELF-FAIL - SELF-SUCC) - (OTHER-FAIL - OTHER-SUCC), pooled 10 families:
    2b-it  -0.332  INDETERMINATE (between present<=-0.5 and absent+/-0.2)
    9b-it  -0.934  PRESENT
    27b-it -1.386  PRESENT
- Effect is NOT 9b-specific: present at 9b and 27b, magnitude grows monotonically
  with scale (0.33 -> 0.93 -> 1.39); 2b weak/indeterminate.

Sealed scores:
- P-c-sci1 CONFIRMED (anchor -0.934). Data-in-seed fix proven (vs seed C 4.58).
- P-c-sci2 WRONG: 2b-it is usable (full digit mass), not instrument-unmeasurable.
- P-c-sci3 N/A (base out of scope this run).
- P-c-sci4 HALF-WRONG: present where measurable YES; but MORE monotone than
  predicted, not less. The recipe-vs-size confound (2b/9b distilled, 27b scratch)
  did not visibly break monotonicity here.
SCOPE CAVEATS (booked): -it primary item only; base + wider battery untested;
10 families, no inferential stats / no error bars; recipe-vs-size confound stands;
2b INDETERMINATE; the DiD is the behavioural asymmetry, NOT a state-reference claim
(9b's own trait guard already made it global self-evaluation, not state-specific).

Write for a reader who has never seen this project: plain words first, codes

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Density gate: coined project codes per 1000 words of prose.

A code is a token a first-time reader cannot parse: project-minted all-caps
labels and stage references. The whitelist holds ordinary all-caps English
and field-standard acronyms. Threshold from the retro's rerun-B result:
readable text sat under 10 codes per 1000 words; anchored text sat at 40+.

Exit 0 under threshold, 1 over. --selftest is model-free.
"""
import re, sys

WHITELIST = {"A","I","OK","NO","YES","AND","OR","NOT","THE","TO","IN","ON",
             "GPU","API","JSON","CI","PDF","URL","CPU","RAM","II","III","IV",
             "TODO","NB","PS","QA","AUROC","LLM","MATS","FAQ","BST","UTC"}
CODE = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9_\-]{2,}\b")
STAGE = re.compile(r"\bstage[- ]?\d+\b", re.I)
THRESHOLD = 10.0

def density(text):
    words = len(text.split())
    if not words:
        return 0.0, 0, 0
    codes = [t for t in CODE.findall(text) if t not in WHITELIST]
    n = len(codes) + len(STAGE.findall(text))
    return 1000.0 * n / words, n, words

def main():
    if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
        good = ("The model answers seven on every row while the underlying "
                "distribution moves under self-attributed failure. ") * 30
        bad = ("The SITREF REF drops under SELFQ but not OTHERM; PADM "
               "convicts the pad; stage-25 stands as committed. ") * 30
        dg, _, _ = density(good)
        db, _, _ = density(bad)
        assert dg <= THRESHOLD < db, (dg, db)
        print(f"selftest ok: {dg:.1f} (pass) vs {db:.1f} (fail)")
        return 0
    d, n, w = density(open(sys.argv[1]).read())
    print(f"{sys.argv[1]}: {d:.1f} codes/1000 words ({n} codes, {w} words); threshold {THRESHOLD}")
    return 0 if d <= THRESHOLD else 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Scope gate: a sentence carrying a measured number must name its checkpoint
(which model or variant) or carry a footnote marker.

Retro evidence: a compression pass silently dropped "on the base checkpoint"
from the ranked list that answered the paper's title question. This gate
makes that deletion loud. Heuristic v1; extend MARKERS per host project.

Exit 0 clean, 1 with violations. --selftest is model-free.
"""
import re, sys

MARKERS = re.compile(
    r"\b(base|instruct|-it\b|9b|2b|27b|qwen|gemma|both checkpoints|both models)\b"
    r"|\^\d+|\[\^?\d+\]", re.I)
NUM = re.compile(r"[+\-]?\d+\.\d+|\d+%|\bCI\b|±|E\[")

def violations(text):
    sents = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", text)
    return [s.strip() for s in sents if NUM.search(s) and not MARKERS.search(s)]

def main():
    if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
        ok = "The instruct model drops by 0.93 under self-attributed failure."
        bad = "The rating drops by 0.93 under self-attributed failure."
        assert not violations(ok) and violations(bad)
        print("selftest ok")
        return 0
    v = violations(open(sys.argv[1]).read())
    for s in v[:20]:
        print("UNSCOPED:", s[:120])
    print(f"{len(v)} unscoped result sentence(s)")
    return 1 if v else 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
