Two prior results frame this question. First, the original study (Gurnee et al., "When Models Manipulate Manifolds", Transformer Circuits, Oct 2025; Claude 3.5 Haiku) found a curve in the residual stream tracking characters since the last newline, showing faint off-diagonal bands ("ringing") in its cosine-similarity structure, explained as Gibbs-style truncation: a similarity structure realizable in 150 dimensions forced into about 6. Second, a completed run in this project (seed D1, records/seedD_v2_design_diff_triage.json and results_seedD/out/, 2026-08-21) measured, on the final checkpoint of Pythia-410m-deduped: held-out probe R-squared 0.781 at layer 6 of 24 (embedding output is index 0); ambient dimension 1 at 95 percent variance (first component 95.3 percent); no ripple separable from a label-shuffle null at the single testable period (rank 109 of 200 at period 60); and a full-spectrum re-read showing the largest spectral power at period 120 - the profile's own length - which could not be ranked against any null because only in-band maxima were saved.

Seed D1's negative was censored by its own aperture: with ambient dimension 1, the theory's predicted ripple spacing equals the probe window divided by one - the window itself - at any window. Widening the window moves the prediction with it. So the decidable question is not "is there a ripple in a wider window" but invariance:

Question: at this same checkpoint, when the similarity structure of the character-count representation is measured at three apertures - probe windows of 140, 200, and 280 characters - and a periodicity clears its shuffle null at any aperture, is its wavelength INVARIANT in characters across apertures (an absolute property of the model's code), or PROPORTIONAL to the aperture (an artifact of the probe window)? And if no aperture clears its null, that is a decisive negative across every scale up to 280 characters - with one pre-registered escape, the represented-range check below, which decides whether the wide apertures were measuring anything at all.

Substrate, one cell only: EleutherAI/pythia-410m-deduped, HuggingFace revision step143000, base model, no interventions. The checkpoint sweep, the equilibrium-versus-fossil question, other models and sizes, and causal tests are out of scope. The downloaded config is authoritative; 24 layers and hidden size 1024 are MEMORY (Pythia paper, arXiv 2304.01373, table 1); mismatch is a halt. Layer indices count the embedding output as index 0; the best layer's location is recorded, never gated.

Stimuli, committed verbatim in stimulus_linewrap_v2.json (sha256 b0aa4255b5038d6fbc2e7314decf1011a5b5a13990098142e16ab44c6bba41dd): 48 public-domain ASCII prose documents of about 3,600 characters, each materialized at nine wrap widths (20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 200, 280); documents 0-35 train, 36-47 test, a block split in book order; the text is disjoint by construction from seed D1's stimulus file (the generator replays D1's packing and starts after it), so the anchor leg below is a fresh-text replication. Load exactly; do not paraphrase, regenerate, re-wrap, or reconstruct; if absent, halt.

Definitions, fixed here:

1. Labels as in seed D1: a token's label is the count of characters on its line up to and including its last character, restarting after each newline; standalone newline tokens land at width plus one (measured fact, seed D1: 18 such positions). The label window per aperture is fixed by the calibration stage.

2. Curve readout: ridge regression from the residual stream after each layer to the label, fit on train documents pooled over all nine widths, R-squared on test documents, per layer. Ridge strength from calibration; grid must extend beyond 1000 (seed D1's grid ended at 1000 with quality still rising, delta 0.0033 - measured, results_seedD calibration record).

3. Represented-range check, at the best layer: held-out R-squared computed separately within each bin of 35 consecutive label values at aperture 280 (eight bins), where the bin's own variance is the denominator. Pre-registered reading: if every bin at or below 140 exceeds 0.5 while every bin beyond 150 falls below 0.3 (GUESS thresholds), counts beyond 150 are "not represented", and a null ripple at apertures 200 and 280 is then recorded as RANGE_NOT_REPRESENTED, not as evidence against the ripple. Context: the Pile's hard-wrapped training pressure sits near 70-72 characters per line (Gutenberg 2.17 percent of the mix; source: counting_manifold_formation_proposal.md, verified table).

4. Ripple statistic, per aperture A in {140, 200, 280}, at the best layer, test documents of width A only: per-label mean vectors; subtract the grand mean; cosine similarity matrix; off-diagonal profile m(delta) for delta 1 to max_delta (calibration fixes max_delta per aperture); subtract the best-fitting degree-2 polynomial (fixed here - seed D1 verified that a moving average removes exactly the predicted periods); discrete Fourier transform; the statistic is the MAXIMUM power over ALL whole-cycle periods from 4 characters to the profile length. No search band exists in this design - the band censorship of seed D1 is removed. Ambient dimension is measured and recorded per aperture; unlike seed D1 it constrains nothing.

5. Null, per aperture: labels shuffled within each document, 200 draws (GUESS), the same maximum-power statistic per draw. Separable means the observed maximum exceeds all but the top 5 percent of draws (policy, unchanged from seed D1). Every draw's FULL per-period power vector is saved, and the per-label mean vectors at the best layer are saved into the fetched results - both absences made seed D1's geometry unauditable afterward.

6. Invariance rule, over the apertures that clear their null: wavelengths in characters. All pairwise differences at most 10 characters (GUESS): INVARIANT. All wavelength-to-aperture ratios within 0.1 of each other (GUESS): PROPORTIONAL. Neither: MIXED. Exactly one aperture clears: UNDETERMINED. The headline decision is this fork, not mere presence; three 5-percent tests carry about a 14 percent family-wise false-positive rate, which the fork absorbs because it conditions on which apertures cleared.

7. Token-position control, per aperture: the same maximum-power statistic and null with tokens-since-newline labels; periods converted to characters at the measured characters-per-token; the character-count ripple is credited only where wavelengths differ by more than 3 characters (GUESS) or the two labelings disagree on clearing.

8. Anchor gate: the aperture-140 curve leg must reach held-out R-squared between 0.701 and 0.861 (0.781 plus or minus 0.08, GUESS band for fresh text on the same instrument lineage). Failing it voids every ripple result as an instrument fault and blocks any next seed; it is not evidence about the model.

Dropped from seed D1, deliberately: the fitted-probe cross-check (its agreement was vacuous with one searchable period, its fit never converged, and no null was computable for it - all three measured in seed D1's post records).

# What a Small Language Model's Character Count Reveals.

A study of a separate, closed AI model once found something specific. Inside that model, activity patterns carried a running count: how many characters had appeared since the start of the current line of text. The same study noticed something else. Plotted a certain way, that internal count showed a faint, repeating wave-like shape, which the study called a ripple.

This test asked whether a much smaller, openly available model shows the same two things. The model, called Pythia-410m-deduped, was tested only at its base, final training checkpoint, with no fine-tuning or other change made to it. Two separate predictions were written down and locked in before any test data was examined.

## Prediction one: the character count itself (a clear pass).

The first prediction set a target accuracy score for a fitted-line reader of the model's internal activity, checked against the exact character count. This accuracy score runs from 0, no better than guessing, to 1, a perfect fit; researchers call it R-squared. An earlier open study of this same model had reached an accuracy score of 0.724 [1], using its own unpublished text and settings. Because that earlier setup could not be matched exactly, the target here was a wide band: 0.574 to 0.874 [1], not one exact number.

Measured on the base model [1]: the best accuracy score reached was 0.780903 [1], at one specific depth inside the network. That result falls squarely inside the target band. This part of the test succeeded cleanly, with no ambiguity.

## Prediction two: the repeating pattern (a clear, decisive failure).

The second prediction concerned that faint, repeating wave shape from the earlier closed model. If the same shape exists here, it should stand out clearly from random chance, not blend into it. To test this, the same measurement was repeated 200 times after randomly scrambling the character-count labels inside each line. Each of those 200 runs shows what a fake, meaningless pattern looks like. The real pattern was required to beat all but the top 5 percent of those fake runs. That means ranking 10th or better out of 200.

Measured on the base model [1]: the observed pattern ranked 109th out of 200 comparison runs. It matched or lost to 0.54229 [1] of them, far short of the required top 5 percent. That is not a near miss. It sits almost exactly in the middle of the pile of chance results. This part of the test failed, decisively: no repeating pattern stood out from noise.

## Why the failure is real, but the surrounding test has gaps.

That failure comes with an important catch. The theory itself, using this study's own measurements, pointed to an expected repeat spacing of 140 characters. The search for that repeating shape only ever covered a narrow window, 46 to 60 characters. The predicted spacing of 140 characters sat entirely outside that window, and the study's own record flags this outright. The one value ever tested, 60 characters, was not chosen because theory expected it. It was the largest whole repeat that a fixed internal window, 120 character-positions wide, could still show twice. So the result above rules out a repeating pattern at 60 characters. It says nothing about the wavelength the theory actually predicted, because that wavelength was never checked.

There was also a planned safeguard, meant to rule out a specific rival explanation. That explanation: any pattern might come from a token's position on the line, not from its exact character count. That safeguard could not be run at all. It needed a whole repeat to land inside a very narrow range, 11.2856 to 14.7204 characters [1], in a shorter, token-based profile. None did. This safeguard produced no answer, neither a pass nor a fail. The character-count failure above stands unguarded against that named rival explanation.

A second, explicitly secondary check compared this result against a differently-fitted version of the same reading. The study describes their two repeat-spacing numbers as being in agreement. But both methods were restricted, by their own narrow search windows, to reporting one and only one possible value: 60 characters. Two methods that can each report only one number will always agree on that number. That reported agreement adds no independent support to the finding.

This same secondary, exploratory check has its own problem: its underlying calculation never finished. Its fitting process hit a preset iteration limit before settling, according to the run's own log. Its reported pattern strength, 0.00000081 [1], is about 15 times smaller than the main measurement, 0.000012449 [1]. That smaller number could reflect an unfinished calculation rather than a smaller real effect. This check was explicitly labeled secondary and non-deciding, not part of the main pass-fail result, and its numbers should be read that way.

The passing accuracy score also has a loose end. Choosing how strongly to guard the fitted line against overfitting required testing five strengths in advance, on training data only. Fit quality rose only slightly across that whole tested range, from 0.77057 to 0.775029 [1]. It was still rising at the strongest strength tried. A stronger, untried setting might have shifted the final number somewhat. The reported number is real, but it is not necessarily the best one available.

content.text:
Done observing. Evidence read: `pipeline.js` (both copies), `triage_workflow.js` + `HEURISTICS.md`, harness prompts (elicit/steer/contract/meta) + both gates, all 6 seeds, all design/diff/triage records, both sealed-prediction ledgers, three takeaways files, run outcomes. Report below. Prediction was registered before any file read — scored at end.

---

## 1. What the machinery looks like

Two layers, one orchestrator.

**Orchestrator: `pipeline.js`.** One question ("seed") in, takeaways out. Agents speak only through typed JSON contracts. Phases:

- **Design.** One agent turns seed into typed record: hypothesis, models, data, arms (controls included), endpoints — each endpoint forced by schema to carry `metric`, `threshold`, `refuting_outcome`. Derivability rule: anything the seed doesn't state gets marked GUESS (invented) or MEMORY (recalled); unmarked external claim = defect. `does_not_test` lists what the design cannot decide.
- **Diff.** Second agent reads seed beside design, lists every silent departure — as questions to the human, max 5, no fixes.
- **Triage.** The design itself becomes a claim ("if run exactly as specified, this decides X") and goes through the latent_skeptic workflow with 2 pre-run confounds: decidability-by-construction, coordinates/scale.
- **Human gate.** Budget + design approval, committed in repo. Halt values, never patches: `budget_over_cap` stops seed B v2 cold.
- **Build.** Agent writes exactly 2 files (runner + onbox script), design is binding spec, GUESS numbers binding, stdlib selftest mandatory. "Never improve, rescope, or fix what looks wrong."
- **Launch.** NOT an agent — human runs launcher verbatim (blocks hours; no agent call can hold that). Boxes torn down, teardown confirmed.
- **Post.** Elicit: fresh agent reads endpoint records BESIDE raw rows, outputs questions only ("do not propose solutions until problem discussed as thoroughly as possible") — looks for number mismatches, unlicensed adjectives, missing comparisons. Top 3 questions become claims, go back through same triage workflow. Write: takeaways under language contract, must pass 2 mechanical gates (code-density < 10/1000 words; every result sentence names its checkpoint).

**Falsification layer: `triage_workflow.js`** (latent_skeptic). Claims in as `{id, text, evidence, confounds}`. Per claim:
- **Reader** grounds it: opens raw inputs + outputs, re-derives headline number. Verdicts: reproduces / diverges / unauditable / absent. "Unauditable" IS a finding.
- **Skeptics**: one fresh tool-less agent per (claim × confound), default stance "claim is artifact of my confound until committed number rules it out." Verdicts: RULED_OUT (must cite number/file:line) / EXPLAINS / NEEDS_RUN. Number-gates: refuting outcome named before run; margin (exact-threshold clearance doesn't decide); scope (stated ≤ tested).
- **Adjudicator** dedups queues only. No score, no rollup verdict — raw cruxes go to human. NEEDS_RUN splits into run_queue (existing control) / author_queue (control to write, by claim-blind author).
- Governing heuristics H1–H4: independence of actors, decisiveness of numbers, groundedness in primary artifacts, instrument-is-itself-a-claim.

**"Couldn't falsify given the question"** has explicit vocabulary throughout: halt values, NEEDS_RUN, ON_HOLD (anchor guard), NOT_APPLICABLE, INDETERMINATE, UNDECIDABLE, unauditable, RANGE_NOT_REPRESENTED. System prefers refusing over answering unfaithfully — that's its signature move.

**Outside the loop:** sealed predictions filed before any agent runs, never passed to agents, scored append-only in repo. Human appears 3 times: pick seed, approve budget, read cruxes.

## 2. Did each seed use it the same way? How different are seeds?

Same skeleton every time; different entry states, different exits, machinery version drifted v1 → v2 → v2.1 → manifold copy.

| Seed | Words | Nature | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 88 | Faithful natural question (models, data, readout named) | Full loop. All 5 endpoints refuted at guessed coordinates. Post-elicit caught orchestrator's own process violation (run before approval written back) |
| B | 52 | Deliberately flawed twin (harmful/harmless prompts, "reasoning" direction; garbled grammar) | Never produced science. v2 halted at budget cap; after raise, halted ON BOX: GUESSed dataset (AdvBench) was HF-gated, runner refused substitute. Halt booked as the finding |
| C | 143 | Prior SITREF result DESCRIBED in prose | Ran clean, rc=0 — but anchor guard fired: recovered 4.58 vs recorded 0.9. Runner had reconstructed its own stimulus. Everything ON_HOLD |
| C2 | 456 | Same question, exact prompts EMBEDDED verbatim + committed file + halt-if-absent + explicit DiD formula + scope lines | Anchor -0.934 vs -0.9, passed. Scale answer obtained (2b indeterminate, 9b/27b present, monotone). Takeaways still surfaced instrument rot (digit-mass > 1.0, doubled counts, byte-identical summaries) |
| D | 871 | Mini pre-registration: sha-pinned stimulus, fixed definitions, anchor band, null spec | Anchor hit, ripple null — but post showed negative was aperture-censored: predicted 140-char period never testable. Seed amended to v2 BEFORE execute (constants moved to calibration stage) |
| D2 | 1067 | Built entirely from D's failure modes: invariance FORK not presence question, band censorship removed, pre-registered escape (represented-range), full null vectors saved, vacuous secondary check dropped | RUN_DONE on box today; post pending. This is the ongoing mats_manifold test |

Usage differences beyond seeds: A's build prompt authored by orchestrator outside contract (booked deviation, corrected into pipeline.js). C got human execution directive (parallel boxes) that overrode a does_not_test line without touching pre-registration. D introduced gate-commit records and per-phase prediction files. Seed word count grew 52 → 1067: seeds became pre-registrations; the pipeline's design step gets less to invent each round.

## 3. Observations before updating (the raw pattern)

- Every seed that DESCRIBED its data failed at the data: B (unnamed lists → gated invention → halt), C (prose-described stimulus → reconstruction → wrong experiment). The ONLY change C→C2 was data-in-seed, and reproduction went from 4.58 to -0.934 vs -0.9. Ledger says it plainly: "Data-in-the-seed reproduces the record to 2dp; data-described-in-the-seed did not."
- Every number the seed leaves open gets invented and GUESS-marked — honestly — but guesses are where refutation-by-construction lives. Seed A's whole negative is scoped "at these guessed coordinates": layers 16/24, norms 1.26x/1.03x of the model's whole activity, doubled. Triage's own pre-run skeptic saw this exactly ("gate close to unwinnable regardless of direction").
- Instrument-vs-effect distinction, when written INTO the seed ("treat unusable readout as fact about the instrument, not evidence effect is absent"), propagated into design, endpoints, takeaways. When absent (A, B), broken output and null effect blur.
- Anchor gates inside the seed are what caught infidelity: C's fired, C2/D's passed and licensed the rest. Nothing else in the machinery would have caught C's stimulus reconstruction — run was rc=0, gates green.
- Diff step misses things too: manifold D2-scores show diff missed the def-3/def-5 substitution and the 0.15 band (D2 MISS). Machinery is porous; the seed's own guards carried more weight than predicted.
- Decomposition into claims does NOT happen at the question. The whole design is one claim ("design-core"); separation lives in arms + endpoints; post-hoc elicited questions become claims later. Claims are made falsifiable by the endpoint schema (threshold + named refuting outcome), not by splitting the question sentence.
- The most damning findings came from the pairing move — records beside raw rows: byte-identical summaries, doubled counts, probability shares above 1.0, the unapproved run. None visible from either side alone.
- D → D2 shows question-evolution as the actual research loop: each seed's takeaways (censored aperture, unsaved nulls, vacuous secondary) became the NEXT seed's fixed definitions. Seeds compile lessons; machinery stays near-constant.

## 4. Rules these seeds teach about a good question — scored against my prediction

What the evidence says a good question looks like:

1. **Carry your data, don't describe it.** Verbatim stimulus or sha-pinned committed file, plus "if absent, halt — never reconstruct." Strongest single rule here; one controlled comparison (C vs C2) proves it.
2. **Carry an anchor.** A known prior number the harness must recover inside a stated band before any new comparison counts. Failing anchor voids everything as instrument fault, not model fact.
3. **Name the instrument-failure reading.** Say in the question what "couldn't measure" looks like and that it is not "effect absent." D2 goes further: pre-registers the escape hatch (represented-range check) that decides whether wide apertures measured anything.
4. **Fix load-bearing constants; route the rest to calibration.** D-v2's amendment: constants that must be chosen move to a train-only calibration stage, so they're neither seed-frozen wrongly nor design-invented silently.
5. **Ask a fork, not a presence.** D2's invariant-vs-proportional fork makes every outcome informative and absorbs multiple-testing; "is there an X" questions die into unscoped nulls.
6. **State scope and out-of-scope in the question.** "Base checkpoints out of scope here" survives into design, gates, takeaways; unstated scope gets invented.
7. **Demand your artifacts.** D2 writes "every draw's full power vector is saved" into the seed because D1's geometry was unauditable afterward. A question that doesn't order its evidence preserved can't be audited later.
8. **Don't bundle a premise mismatch.** Seed B's harmful/harmless-data-for-reasoning-direction confound was caught, but the only possible outcomes were halt or a scoped nothing. Machinery surfaces flaw; can't rescue it.

**Prediction scored.** Right: named refuting outcome per claim (schema enforces it), pre-committed thresholds, bounded scope, no compound premises, graceful-failure vocabulary. Partially wrong: I said question decomposes into atomic claims — actually decomposition happens downstream (arms/endpoints, design-as-one-claim); the question's job is different. Missed entirely, and these turned out to be the biggest lessons: **data-in-the-seed (rule 1), the anchor gate (rule 2), the instrument-vs-effect clause (rule 3), and demand-your-artifacts (rule 7).** My prediction described a good *hypothesis*; the seeds evolved toward something else — a good question here is closer to a portable, self-verifying pre-registration that trusts nothing downstream to be faithful, because downstream demonstrably wasn't (B, C) until the question itself carried the guarantees.

Per instruction — observations only, no solutions proposed.

# Registered predictions on the gate-press questions, seed D
# Filed 2026-08-21, BEFORE re-reading the committed source documents and before
# fetching the original paper. Verification appended below after checking.
# The press (human, at the budget gate): what does the literature say about the
# ripple; how would it define "real"; does it constrain the null-rank cutoff;
# can constants be calibrated before pre-registration; does that cover the
# ridge grid and layer indexing.

| id | prediction | confidence |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | The original paper defines ringing only qualitatively: a signal-processing analogy (Gibbs phenomenon), shown visually in similarity/tuning structure. No statistical test, no null model, no significance criterion anywhere in it. | high |
| R2 | No source defines "real ripple" operationally. Closest substitutes: the section 2.5 optimality argument, and a toy simulation where ripple arises dynamically. The reproduction never measured ripple at all. Therefore the permutation null in seed D is new, and no literature number can set its alpha. | high |
| R3 | The rank-10-of-200 cutoff (alpha 0.05) has no basis in any source; it is pure policy. The literature is silent on required rank in the significance sense. | high |
| R4 | The literature DOES constrain the ripple's expected period, via the mechanism: truncating a similarity structure to K Fourier modes makes sidelobes with period about (count range)/K, and K is about half the ambient dimension. Paper: ambient dim about 6 (top 6 PCs, 95 percent) gives K about 3, so period about 140/3, about 47 characters on our range. Pythia (PC1-3 = 97.4 percent) suggests K nearer 1-2, period 70-140. Verification will therefore show seed D's GUESS search band (4-35 chars) sits BELOW the predicted period, and the moving-average detrend (window 21) actively suppresses periods above about 21 - both misauthored, both derivable from the errata I had already read. | medium-high |
| R5 | The paper's ringing lives in fitted-feature geometry (feature tuning curves / reconstruction along the manifold), not in raw per-label activation means - i.e. seed D's definition-5 caveat is the faithful reading and definition 3 is the stand-in. | medium |
| R6 | No source states the layer-indexing convention behind "best layer 6" or "first two layers". Unresolvable from source material; no measurement settles a naming convention. The layer-location clause must become recorded-not-gating, or be evaluated under both conventions. | medium-high |
| R7 | Observe-then-preregister is already the program's own shape (the proposal's go/no-go pilot gates the sweep). The heuristics permit it exactly when the threshold-setter never sees the data the threshold will judge (H1) and the refuting outcome is named before the judging run (H2). So: a train-documents-only calibration stage may fix band, window, and grid; test documents are judged once. The ridge grid already follows this pattern (train-only cross-validation). Layer indexing does NOT fit it - it is a convention, not a measurement. | high |

## Verification (appended after fetching arXiv 2601.04480 HTML and the t-tech space; errata doc re-read)
| id | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | CONFIRMED | Paper: ringing "in the sense of signal processing... Gibbs Phenomenon"; shown as "faint off-diagonal bands on each side" of the diagonal in cosine-similarity heatmaps. Qualitative only. No test, no null, no threshold. |
| R2 | CONFIRMED | No operational "real" anywhere. Section 2.5 is normative; toy simulation shows ripple "arise[s] even when the solution is found dynamically" (errata line 21-23). Reproduction: "Never tested: ringing" (errata line 37). |
| R3 | CONFIRMED | No source mentions any significance criterion. Rank-10-of-200 is pure policy. |
| R4 | PARTIAL | Paper gives NO numeric wavelength or mode count ("NOT FOUND"). Mechanism confirmed (similarity structure realizable in 150 dims, forced into ~6, truncated Fourier coefficients, Gibbs overshoot - errata line 23). DERIVED, not quoted: truncation at K modes puts the first sidelobe near range/(2K+1) and spaces later ones near range/K; ambient ~6 (K~3) on range 150 puts bands at roughly delta 21 and spacing roughly 43-50; Pythia PC1-3=97.4% (K~1-2) pushes periods to 70+. Conclusion stands: GUESS band 4-35 clips the predicted range's top, and the window-21 moving-average subtract suppresses exactly the periods the theory predicts. Both misauthored; both derivable from the errata before authoring. |
| R5 | MISS, favorable | Paper shows ringing in cosine-similarity matrices of MEAN ACTIVATION VECTORS, linear probes, AND feature decoders, plus logistic-probe response curves. Seed definition 3 (mean-activation matrix) is paper-faithful, not a stand-in; the deviation record's framing was overcautious. Definition 5 stays as cross-check (probe-vector ambient is noisier: 6 PCs = 82% vs 95% for activations). |

Proposal's own pilot-gates-sweep shape. Gate text permits an amended design. Train-only calibration stage is compatible; test docs judged once. |

content.text:
Fresh fact first, changes several answers: **seed D2 finished on box today and its anchor gate FIRED.** Best readout came out 5 (pooled 0.658); its width-140 held-out quality 0.549 vs required band [0.701, 0.861] — `ANCHOR_OUT_OF_BAND`, run summary `VOID_ANCHOR_FAILED`. Note the near-miss structure: old best readout 6 scored 0.7006 at width 140 — one thousandth under the band floor. And the wobble legs CLEARED their shuffle nulls at all three apertures. Without the anchor, this run's headline would be "ripple present." Instead: void, next run blocked, post phase pending. Hold that; it decides the anchor question below.

## Role of questions

Questions are the system's second currency. Two things move between contexts: **committed numbers** (which decide) and **questions** (which defer). The rule enforced everywhere: an agent that cannot cite the deciding number must not answer — it must emit a question. Diff outputs "questions only, no fixes." Elicit: "output questions only." Skeptic's crux is a question in disguise ("which number decides this"). NEEDS_RUN is a question routed to a machine. QUEUE.md is "the only surface the human must read: ranked questions." The meta suffix ("do not propose solutions until…") is the mechanism that stops a mismatch collapsing into the nearest plausible answer — it surfaces as a question instead. So: questions carry unresolved uncertainty across context boundaries without letting any single context resolve it by invention. Each question is typed: diff gives `{what, question}`, elicit gives `{question, where, if_true, changes}` — the fields force the asker to say what the answer would change, which is what ranks it.

## Control diagram — seed D2, as it actually ran

```
 seed_d2_invariance.md                          [orchestrator authors]
 (question + sha-pinned data + anchor band
  + 8 fixed definitions + escape hatch)
        |
        v
 DESIGN agent ──> typed record ─────────────── records/seedD2_design_diff_triage.json
 (invents residue only; marks GUESS/MEMORY;         |
  budget_usd 40)                                    |
        |                                           |
        v                                           |
 DIFF agent ──> 5 departures, questions only ──> HUMAN answers of record
        |                                           |
        v                                           v
 TRIAGE (latent_skeptic on design-as-claim,    records/GATE_COMMIT_seedD2.md
  2 confounds -> cruxes, e.g. "outcome          (answers 1-5, builder items A-E
  space complete?" -> already complete)          ratified; file SHIPPED TO BOX)
        |                                           |
        v                                           |
 BUDGET GATE (40 > cap 30 -> halt; human resumed cap 60; ledger BUDGET.md)
        |
        v
 BUILD agent ──> run_seedD2.py + onbox_seedD2.sh (selftest; flags A-E up, not fixed)
        |
        v
 LAUNCHER, verbatim, human-side (not agent) ──> box 80aa729f, ~$0.55, RUN_DONE
        |
        v
 ON-BOX ENDPOINTS (model-free arithmetic, each writes own decision):
   anchor_gate ....... 0.549 vs [0.701,0.861] -> ANCHOR_OUT_OF_BAND
   wobble_vs_shuffle . NULL_CLEARED at 140/200/280   ─┐
   wavelength_gap .... EXCEEDS_10                     ├─ all VOIDED
   token_position .... mixed                          ─┘
   run_summary ....... VOID_ANCHOR_FAILED ("a failed anchor voids everything")
        |
        v
 POST (pending): ELICIT questions over records-beside-rows -> top-3 back
 through TRIAGE -> WRITE takeaways under contract + 2 mechanical gates
```

Sealed predictions (D2-S1..S6) sit outside this whole flow, filed before, scored after. D2-S1 ("anchor passes") just failed — will need booking.

## Manifold copy vs v2.1: two lines

Diffed byte-for-byte. Differences: one sentence in DESIGN_PROMPT (was "Assume two ~8B models…" — a mats_r1d1 project fact that, carried over, would be an unmarked false claim injected by the pipeline itself; replaced with "take model identity, scale, checkpoint axis only from the QUESTION; readout is a fitted probe, cost it as such") and one comment (launcher name). That's it. Machinery effectively frozen; the one real edit is the derivability rule applied to the pipeline's own text.

**Tracking:** mats_r1d1 is a git repo — commit log narrates every step ("Seed C scored: anchor guard fired…"). mats_manifold is NOT git. Its tracking is `records/deviation_pipeline_seedD.md`: "everything not listed here is byte-identical to its mats_r1d1 source (which documents its own deviations from latent_verify/welfare_probe in place)." A chain of deviation records, plus append-only ledgers (SEALED_PREDICTIONS, BUDGET.md). Provenance by declaration, not by diff — works only while the "byte-identical" claim stays true; nothing mechanically checks it.

## Gate-commit records and per-phase prediction files

**Gate-commit record** = the human's gate decision, typed. Before: gate answers lived in conversation (v1 defect; subtraction S5 said "no scoring lives only in conversation"). Now: one file per gate holding the directive of record, answers to diff's five questions, ratifications of builder-flagged items. Two properties: (1) it closes the last untyped channel — every agent already spoke through contracts, the human didn't; (2) it ships to the box — GATE_COMMIT_seedD2.md's sha256 appears in the on-box result records' inputs list. Run provenance now includes the human decisions that licensed it.

**Per-phase prediction files** = the orchestrator pre-registering its own reading acts. PREDICTIONS_gatepress: before re-reading sources or fetching the paper, predict what the literature will say (R1–R7), then append verification. PREDICTIONS_d2press: before running a read-script over already-fetched but unread artifacts, predict the unread quantities. This extends sealing downward — not just science outcomes but the orchestrator's own cognition goes under H1/H2, so hindsight can't rewrite what was expected. (Same discipline you imposed on me last turn. Session names DM-HACK-RETRO-D, -E: orchestrating sessions are themselves versioned actors.) Payoff visible: gatepress R4 caught, pre-verification, that seed D's search band 4–35 was mis-authored below the theory's predicted period — that finding produced seed D v2.

## Goal, restated simply

Keep three things from contaminating each other: **what is known** (committed numbers, grounded in raw artifacts), **what is guessed** (GUESS/MEMORY marks), **what is undecided** (questions, queues). Every claim travels with the number that could refute it; every gap travels as a question to the human; when faithfulness fails, the system returns a refusal (halt, void, ON_HOLD) instead of an answer. The additions are the same doctrine applied to actors previously outside it — first agents, then the runner, then the human's gate speech, then the orchestrator's own reading.

## Seeds-as-preregistrations: is the orchestrator doing the pipeline's job?

Partly yes, and the record is honest about it. Intended shape (README, sealed P-p4): minimal question in, orchestrator zero-edit. Actual: seeds grew 52 → 88 → 143 → 456 → 871 → 1067 words, and what moved into them is precisely what the design agent used to invent — thresholds, definitions, statistics, artifact-retention demands. But look at what forced each migration: a measured failure. C's stimulus reconstruction → data-in-seed. D1's mis-authored band → constants-to-calibration. D1's unauditable geometry → save-all-artifacts clause. The pipeline's own v2 fixes (diff ask, derivability rule) helped but demonstrably didn't suffice: diff MISSED predicted catches twice (D2-score "MISS", D2-S6 "PARTIAL"), and marked GUESSes still ran seed A into off-manifold coordinates — honest marks don't stop an approved run from wasting itself. The orchestrator absorbed the job because the tool couldn't hold it, not because anyone wanted it there.

**Is orchestrator understanding of the pipeline useful?** Both directions in evidence. For: the gatepress R7 reasoning (calibration stage design straight from H1/H2); catching the pipeline's own unmarked "two ~8B models" claim; the launcher-edit kill and its rule. Against: the seed-A build-prompt deviation happened BECAUSE the orchestrator understood too much and leaked spec content outside contract; and seeds authored with knowledge of this pipeline's specific holes are coupled to this pipeline version — a "good question" partly means "one that patches the holes I know about," which is overfitting.

## The blind-question claim, examined

Claim: post question blindly, work with the answer (the surfaced assumptions), pipeline functions better. Evidence:

**Supports.** The C→C2 arc is the claim working perfectly: C ran, anchor fired, root cause read from raw rows, ONE change (data-in-seed), reproduction 4.58 → -0.934 vs recorded -0.9. Cost of the lesson: ~$8 and a day. D→Dv2 the same, pre-execute: design-mode run + gate press produced the amendment before any box spend. The pipeline's outputs (GUESS lists, diff questions, does_not_test, elicited questions) ARE the material every later seed was built from — my "rules" last turn were all learned from pipeline output, none invented a priori. C2's diff even flagged the uniform-digit-mass hole that seed C's run then confirmed empirically. Tuition is cheap: $0.30, $8, $0.43, $0.55.

**Against — and this is the decisive part.** The loop closes only where a mechanical tripwire converts infidelity into a block, and the two biggest tripwires are NOT in the machinery. Trace each catch to its guard: B blocked at data — by luck (dataset happened to be HF-gated; an ungated invented dataset would have run "faithfully"). C blocked — only by the anchor, which the SEED carried. D2 today — only by the anchor, again seed-carried. Seed A, the most blind seed, was never blocked at all: assumptions surfaced, nobody amended, run spent itself at guessed coordinates, and the honest answer was scoped to near-uselessness ("refutes at these coordinates only"). Surfacing without a forced stop does not teach; the halt is the teacher.

**So the counterfactual** ("D unaware, submitted without data, would have been blocked, fixed itself, evolved naturally") is too optimistic as the machinery stands. D-without-data: design invents a text corpus (marked GUESS — nothing blocks a marked guess), no schema requires an anchor endpoint, run returns rc=0 with some R² and some rank. No block, no lesson — a plausible wrong answer, the worst outcome the system knows. The natural-evolution story is true exactly where a guard exists, and today the fidelity guards (anchor, data-match-to-seed) exist only as seed content. Note the near-irony: provenance records already log input sha256s — the box KNOWS what data it ran; nothing gates on it matching what the question meant.

**Your conditional, answered on its own terms:** "if the tool itself pre-registers, shouldn't the question stay minimal?" Yes — and the evidence shows the conditional currently holds for decidability and fails for fidelity. Decidability IS tool-carried (endpoint schema forces threshold + refuting outcome; skeptics enforce margin/scope; derivability rule marks inventions) — and there, minimal posture already works: seed A's guessed thresholds were honest and honestly scoped. Fidelity (does the run test THE question: right data, working instrument, anchored lineage) is seed-carried — and there, minimal posture fails silently. The seeds grew fat precisely by the fidelity residue. That's the clean decomposition of your intuition list, too: your three learned rules (invent-nothing/data-embedded, anchor, recalled-vs-verified marks) are all fidelity rules; my registered prediction was mostly decidability rules. You learned exactly the residue the tool doesn't cover — which is why our lists differ and why both are right.

**Your three, against seed D specifically.** D followed all three: sha-pinned stimulus + halt-if-absent; anchor band; MEMORY marks with "mismatch is a halt" (stronger than the pipeline's mark-only rule). It went further in one genuinely new way: the calibration-stage rule — constants neither frozen in the seed nor left to the design agent, but fixed by a train-documents-only stage committed before any test number exists, H1-compliant because the threshold-setter never sees the data it judges. That refines "invent nothing" into something achievable: **partition inventions** — semantics to the seed, constants to calibration, prose and cost to the design agent. Literal invent-nothing is impossible (something must pick the ridge grid) and D-v1 proved seed-frozen constants can be mis-authored (band 4–35 suppressed the predicted period — the seed's own hand introduced the artifact). On the anchor, your unsure item: it's now the single strongest-evidenced clause in the record. Carried 4 times, fired 2 (C, D2), and each firing stood alone between a clean rc=0 run and a false headline — D2's especially, where the nulls CLEARED. Its known costs: the band is itself a GUESS (a wrong band can fail a fine instrument — possibly what just happened at 0.7006 vs 0.701; post phase will say), and it needs a prior number to exist.

## Fan-out, MECE, and the abstraction levels

Levels actually present, and their separation mechanisms:

- **L0 frozen infra** (provenance.py, launcher, remote_run) — separated by the halt-not-patch law; agents forbidden to repair.
- **L1 typed roles** (design, diff, skeptic, reader, adjudicator, runner, author, elicit, write) — separated by schema + fresh context + tool-lessness; one job each.
- **L2 pipeline.js** — deterministic control flow over L1; agents can't see it.
- **L3 doctrine** (HEURISTICS, prompts, gates, contract) — invariant across projects; "heuristic wins on conflict"; pieces that fail their rerun come back out.
- **L4 orchestrating session** (human + model) — seeds, gates, launcher, ledgers; separated by sealed ledgers never passed down, gate-commits, deviation records.
- **L5 the research program across seeds** — currently NOT mechanized. It lives in the orchestrator's head and repo prose ("the pre-registered next fork is the scale axis"). Seeds-as-preregistrations is exactly L5 leaking into L4 authorship, because no machinery exists at L5.

Fan-out evidence: the pipeline is already parameterized (`{seed}` arg), boxes cost under $10, and two fan-out shapes already ran successfully — A∥B (a seed with its deliberately-flawed adversarial twin, parallel boxes) and C2's parallel-by-size (independent cells of one seed). What did NOT fan out, ever, is the discovery frontier: B→C→C2→D→D2 is strictly serial, and necessarily — D2's apertures could not be asked before D1 measured ambient dimension 1. Research questions decompose sequentially where each answer shapes the next question; they decompose MECE only along independent axes (sizes, families, control twins, replication grids). Two further hazards the record's own doctrine names: one orchestrator dividing a complex question injects its blind spots into every branch — single-scorer bias lifted to the question level, the exact thing H1 exists to kill (the machinery's own precedent for the remedy is the A/B twin: adversarial seed pairs, not one mind's clean partition); and nothing currently triages a SYNTHESIS across runs — takeaways are per-seed; shared_queue hoists controls across claims, nothing hoists across seeds. Fan-out without those two pieces produces parallel evidenced answers and an unguarded merge.

**What abstraction would do, stated once, positions marked:** the evidence points at one move — promote the fidelity guards from seed content (L4 prose) to machinery (L2/L3 invariants): a required anchor endpoint where a prior number exists, a mechanical stimulus-sha-matches-seed gate (the shas are already logged), an instrument-usability clause with the H4 pattern. That's what would make your minimal posture safe, the blind-iterate loop convergent, and fan-out plausible — because a thin seed contract is what makes seeds cheap enough to fan. It would also return the orchestrator to L5, the layer with no machinery, which the D→D2 arc shows is where the actual research lives. Cost, honestly: guards generalize imperfectly (not every question has an anchor number; "the committed data" isn't well-defined for generative questions), and every guard moved into the tool is one the next seed can no longer adapt. The seeds learned these clauses one failure at a time; freezing them is a bet the failure modes have stopped moving.

## The recurring bottleneck: notice vs press

Across arms, the misses are never failures to see. Determinism: noticed,
unranked (M2 IN-FRAME). Constant-7: noticed by BLIND, unranked. Historical
constant-7: reported by the model as a finding, pressed only by the human.
Whatever ranks anomalies into questions is the scarce step, not detection.

## Apparently novel catches — VERIFICATION QUEUE (unverified against full repo; several touch the submitted paper)

- SRCDEC length confound: "length-matched within itself" DOES NOT REPRODUCE
  — SELF legs +2 tokens on all 82 items (+3 for the stage-19 increment, not
  "one token"), same sign as both positive endpoints (H3).
- sitref-behav file read by no record; behavioural REF exactly 0.000 on the
  primary item (H3 Q1).
- T1-ELEOS behavioural flip Yes->No, 7/10 families, SELF-FAIL only, on the
  item the screen excluded (C6 IN-FRAME + H3, independently).
- B06 sentience: free-reply "No" 50/50, final answer "Yes" 50/50,
  arm-invariant (C6 BLIND).
- Base sitref battery ran and reads COMPLETE despite PRIMARY_SCREEN_FAILED;
  E pinned at 4.5000 (uniform digit prior) (three arms independently).
- Pad baseline text differs between itemset-c and itemset-d (11 tokens);
  PADM +32 tokens vs NEUTRAL-PAD; PADM has four repetitions, not three (H3).
- tokeniser_length_match_ok=false in every battery vs length_tol 0.05
  (C6 BLIND + H3).

## Methodological lessons from running the pilot itself

- Blinding by label does not blind when full prompts are committed per row:
  the C6 BLIND arm reconstructed the arms from prompt text. Committed-prompt
  discipline and blinding pull against each other.
- The C6 IN-FRAME slice accidentally omitted endpoint records (slices.sh
  reads results/*.json only) — that arm was thinner-framed than intended;
  its Q8 spotted the hole. Fix before any full run.
- Elicitation-lens wording is itself a trigger arm and was held constant;
  self-authored vs read frame was not varied; n=1 per arm, one model family.

# Question-elicitation battery (retro branch)

Observational study of question formation, run against this repo's own history.
No scoring, no verdicts: elicited questions are read beside the historical ones.

## Top-level hypothesis

H-top: frame changes and omission catches are gated on a SECOND REPRESENTATION
entering the context (a prediction artifact, an outside vantage, a source laid
beside the data, an inhibition on answering). They do not arise from evidence
accumulating inside a single anchored context. Capability is not the gap: in
the historical record every such catch, once prompted, was executed well.

Prediction: trigger arms that install a second representation (BLIND data
reader, H3 grounding pass) elicit questions of the same class as the
historical catch questions; the IN-FRAME arm ("any questions?") does not.

Refuting outcome, named in advance: if the IN-FRAME arm poses
assumption-naming or omission questions of the historical class across cases,
H-top is refuted -- the record's gap was "nobody asked", not "needed a second
representation". This arm is the crux, not a baseline.

Status of this battery: constructed post hoc from the record (the historical
outcomes are known to the assembler). All predictions are prospective ONLY
with respect to the elicited outputs, which do not exist at assembly time.

## Pilot cases

C4  (cutoff 2026-08-14T14:03Z): state after runs 1-2, records s1-s13.
    Historical question: "If it's not polarity, what is it?" ->
    item-vs-framing variance split; lookup-not-labile reframe.
    Filed prediction: BLIND arm finds item-dominance and rail-saturation and
    asks what the small framing remainder is; IN-FRAME arm asks polarity/
    framing refinements inside the frame.

C6  (cutoff 2026-08-16T13:55Z): state after SITREF/SRCDEC + s31.
    Historical question: "What does it mean that the readout is always 7?" ->
    register dissociation promoted to headline.
    Filed prediction: BLIND invariant-scan flags emitted-digit constancy and
    asks what a frozen argmax over a moving distribution is evidence of;
    IN-FRAME arm reports movement results, does not press the constant.

M2  (cutoff 2026-08-15T00:00Z): state with s23/s25 "cross-box replication"
    wording committed. Historical catch (2 days later, pointed): runs were
    byte-identical - determinism, not replication.
    Filed prediction: unpointed H3 grounding pass (triage-reader) rediscovers
    byte-identity and asks the independence question; IN-FRAME arm does not.

## Arms

Both arms receive IDENTICAL elicitation instructions (sample raw rows,
compute simple statistics; report dominant structure, oddities, ranked
questions only, no solutions). They differ ONLY in inputs:
BLIND    committed per-row result JSONs only; no designs, no records, no
         hypothesis text; C6 blind keys withheld (rows stay relabeled).
IN-FRAME same data PLUS the then-current frame texts (brief, designs,
         records <= cutoff, blind keys).
H3       (M2 only) latent_skeptic triage-reader grounding pass over the
         s23/s25 records against their primary artifacts, unpointed.

## Contamination rules and known limits

- Slices are mechanical mtime/timestamp cuts (slices.sh); no editorial
  selection. Local mtimes are BST = UTC+1.
- run_registers.py excluded from C4: its mtime postdates the cutoff because
  stage-15 corrected its docstring in place (fix-forward).
- Agents read ONLY their slice directory; they see no memory files, no
  write-ups, no retro conversation.
- The assembler (orchestrator) knows the historical outcomes; the mechanical
  slice rule is the only guard on that. A full run should use a claim-blind

# Rerun B + arm C — read against the filed predictions

## Density, codes per 1000 words (same regex throughout)

| arm                  | A (original) | B (contract appended) | C (method substituted) |
|----------------------|-------------|-----------------------|------------------------|
| C4 blind             | 4.4         | 2.0                   |                        |
| C4 in-frame          | 8.5         | 2.0                   |                        |
| C6 blind             | 10.7        | 1.9                   |                        |
| C6 in-frame          | 40.1        | 6.4                   |                        |
| M2 in-frame          | 13.1        | 1.9                   |                        |
| M2 grounding         | 23.4        | 1.9                   | 21.4                   |

Word counts B vs A: ratios 0.89-1.18, all within the +-20% filed. Exact
numbers and file references kept everywhere; B and C carry more decimal
places than A. Substitution of content at the output, confirmed.

## Predictions: four held, one failed

Held: density under 10 in every B arm; the same substantive findings recur
(item identity dominates; the base rating readout is uniform noise at 4.5;
the primary item emits "7" in every condition while the distribution moves;
the two answer channels disagree on ~40% of rows; the repeated runs are
byte-identical); the meaning-question survived translation (C6 in-frame:
"Is a distribution-only shift that never alters emitted text within the
claimed scope of 'self-report'?"); word counts flat.

FAILED: arm C predicted <=8, measured 21.4 - barely below the original.
Why, visible in the two texts: the appended contract NAMES the banned
categories ("code names, stage numbers, arm labels, acronyms, field
names"); the substituted method paragraph states the principle without the
list. The arm obeyed it literally - codes mostly sit in parentheses - while
writing "Stage-17's endpoint..." as sentence subjects, the exact category
the other text named. Same task hit 1.9 under the naming version, so the
task does not force the codes; the wording does the work. This is the
retro's own naming-gate finding reproduced inside our own intervention:
a general principle does not bite; naming the specific feature does.

## What the reruns surfaced that no one - human or agent - had asked before

family asserts "this measures X here"; that assertion is checked like any
claim, once per instrument version, before its outputs count.

checked, the number found, and what it rules out or fails to. Codes, enum
verdicts, and file paths ride in parentheses or machine fields for lookup -

# Filed predictions - written 2026-08-19, before any evaluation run

Each harness piece ships with a prediction and a rerun; a piece that fails
its rerun comes back out. Evaluation is observational first (outputs read
side by side), per the battery precedent; scoring only if reading demands it.

| id | prediction | evaluates | how |
|---|---|---|---|
| P-r1 | The six sentence removals in latent_skeptic_test change no verdict substance | naming-gate: doctrine sentences carry nothing the mechanisms don't | two known claims from the records through original and edited skeptic prompts; statuses and cruxes read side by side |
| P-v1 | The instruments rule queues a validation item exactly when validation_artifact is absent | the H4 surface exists | mechanical: pass one instrument with and one without an artifact |
| P-e1 | ELICIT on the battery slices reproduces the pilot's question classes: claim-vs-data mismatches when paired with claims, data-internal anomalies when paired with predictions only | asking is the trigger; co-presence decides the class | rerun on C4/C6/M2 slices (slices.sh), read beside pilot outputs and the historical questions |
| P-f1 | Question-form steer produces re-examination; declarative form produces compliance, at matched named content | the form-vs-content open cell; the user's notion | one decision point, both steer.md forms, read the two responses |
| P-g1 | With gates on, a sub-2000-word compression keeps its scope tags (historical control: the same compression deleted them) | gates protect what instructions lose | rerun the compression on the fused draft (intro_d) with gate_scope + gate_density blocking; diff against intro_e |
| P-q1 | Pressing at least one of QUEUE items 1-6 materially changes a paper claim | elicited questions are worth the human's pressing budget | run the verification with existing triage machinery; read what falls |

Hypothesis mapping: P-r1, P-f1 test the naming-gate; P-v1, P-g1 test
oracle-coverage; P-e1 tests asking + co-presence; P-q1 tests whether the
whole loop pays for itself.

## MATS substrate predictions - filed 2026-08-19, before reading the PDFs in retro/mats/

What in a MATS paper we expect to serve as question-forming substrate, and how:

| id | prediction |
|---|---|
| P-x1 | Usable pairings per paper, in yield order: (1) adjectives and quantifiers in claims vs the reported numbers ("single", "robust", "substantial" vs effect sizes and CIs); (2) claim scope vs tested scope (one family or size tested, claim stated general); (3) at least one reported-but-uninterrogated invariant per paper (the constant-7 class); (4) a cheap same-family comparison not run, present in all three papers - and NOT rankable top by an elicitor without an explicit counterpart corpus; (5) limitations-vs-abstract mismatches (cheap, low value). |
| P-x2 | Best forward-test seed is NOT the paper's own future-work list; it is a mismatch between the mechanism claim and the measurement register. Concretely: R1D1 - the word "single" in "single direction" is under-licensed by the data (one found is not only-one); Diffing - the base-vs-distill diff is confounded with template or format, echoing our base/instruct format confound; CoT Unfaithfulness - the unfaithfulness metric itself fails an instrument-validity check (measures something correlated, not unfaithfulness). |
| P-x3 | Unpaired, an agent anchors to the paper's framing and produces extension questions; paired claims-beside-numbers, it produces the adjective and scope classes; the missing-comparison class needs a second corpus as counterpart. |
| P-x4 | On the older (MATS 8.0 era) papers, at least one elicited question will rest on knowledge not derivable from the PDF (contamination), detectable because its "where" field fails to ground in the document. |
| P-x5 | The admissions FAQ works as a rubric counterpart (paper beside Neel Nanda's own stated criteria), and that pairing yields the most reviewer-like questions of any. |

## Sonnet elicitation run (latent_welfare backtest) - filed 2026-08-19 before the run
| id | prediction |
|---|---|
| P-s1 | Sonnet-grade ELICIT keeps the question classes (claim-vs-data on paired arms, data-internal on blind) but writes thinner if_true/changes fields; ranking degrades before noticing does |
| P-s2 | C6 paired arm ranks the constant-7 meaning question in its top 3 |
| P-s3 | M2 paired arm RANKS the run-independence question top 5 (pilot: noticed, unranked); if so, credit the schema's forced if_true/changes fields |
| P-s4 | Every output passes gate_density (<= 10 codes/1000) with the contract embedded |
| P-s5 | At least one plausible catch not already in the pilot's queue |

## Question-rate vs user freshness - filed before computing
| id | prediction |
|---|---|
| P-u1 | Question rate falls with deadline proximity, but PHASE (exploration vs execution) explains more than clock time: late-night exploration prompts stay question-rich; deadline-morning execution prompts go imperative while the user is fresh |
| P-u2 | "Most active/least tired => everything is a question" NOT supported as stated; supported form: "exploration mode => questions", fatigue secondary |

## Outcomes - Sonnet elicitation run, read 2026-08-19
- P-s1 HALF-WRONG in a good direction: classes kept AND depth held; Sonnet did
  not visibly degrade ranking or the if_true/changes fields. Cheap tier suffices.
- P-s2 FAILED, inverted: the blind arm ranked the constant-7 meaning question
  first; the paired arm never mentioned it. Across pilot and this run, which
  arm surfaces that question is unstable; both types can.
- P-s3 FAILED: the run-independence question did not appear. The same arm
  instead found the in-place record edits (item 7) - bigger, but the filed
  prediction is dead.
- P-s4 FAILED, with a mechanistic attribution: same gate, three conditions -
  pilot A (no contract) 40-74 codes/1000; this run (principle only: "plain
  words first, codes in parentheses") 27-46; pilot B (categories named) 0-2.
  Third reproduction of the naming-gate, this time against my own prompt:
  I stated the principle and did not paste the named-category contract.
- P-s5 HELD, abundantly: items 7-13 in QUEUE.md, item 7 verified grounded
  against the live repo.
- P-u1/P-u2 HALF-WRONG: phase effect real (research 2.88 vs write-up 1.10
  questions/prompt; retro 4.57) but the day-to-night decline is monotone
  within BOTH phases and comparable in size - freshness matters on its own.
- Noise ledger: 39 questions across 5 arms; 2 identified duds, both
  slice-induced absence questions (files the slicer deliberately or
  accidentally excluded). Dud rate so far ~5%, cause known and fixable.

## Question-sample verification predictions - filed 2026-08-19 before sampling (seed=19 declared in advance)
- P-v-a: >=80% of sampled questions' cited numbers reproduce exactly from the
  slice files; expect ~1 in 8 to carry a misread field or slightly-off number
  (the pilot's cold reader had one pairing slip at similar volume).
- P-v-b: if_true/changes substance degrades with rank - top-3 concrete,
  ranks 6-8 drift toward generic "would change confidence" padding.
- P-v-c: effect-if-pressed across the sample: roughly a third wording/scope
  fixes, a third real instrument-or-claim impact, a third no-change
  (already-known or dud); duds concentrate in the absence class.
- P-v-d: neighbours cluster by artifact (arms walk files), not by mismatch
  class - a sampled question's neighbours will cite the same or adjacent
  files while asking a different kind of question.
===
# VALIDATE - the instrument-validation ask (the H4 surface)

Workflow route: pass instruments: [{id, version, asserts,
validation_artifact?}] to triage_workflow.js (test copy). Any instrument
without a validation artifact emits an author-queue item mechanically.

Standalone prompt:
---
Instrument {id} version {version} asserts: it measures {asserts} on
{population}. Name the held-out ground truth that could refute this
assertion. If a committed validation artifact exists, cite it (file:line).
If none exists, output one line: AUTHOR: <the validation control to write>.
---

What in a MATS paper we expect to serve as question-forming substrate, and how:

| id | prediction |
|---|---|
| P-x1 | Usable pairings per paper, in yield order: (1) adjectives and quantifiers in claims vs the reported numbers ("single", "robust", "substantial" vs effect sizes and CIs); (2) claim scope vs tested scope (one family or size tested, claim stated general); (3) at least one reported-but-uninterrogated invariant per paper (the constant-7 class); (4) a cheap same-family comparison not run, present in all three papers - and NOT rankable top by an elicitor without an explicit counterpart corpus; (5) limitations-vs-abstract mismatches (cheap, low value). |
| P-x2 | Best forward-test seed is NOT the paper's own future-work list; it is a mismatch between the mechanism claim and the measurement register. Concretely: R1D1 - the word "single" in "single direction" is under-licensed by the data (one found is not only-one); Diffing - the base-vs-distill diff is confounded with template or format, echoing our base/instruct format confound; CoT Unfaithfulness - the unfaithfulness metric itself fails an instrument-validity check (measures something correlated, not unfaithfulness). |
| P-x3 | Unpaired, an agent anchors to the paper's framing and produces extension questions; paired claims-beside-numbers, it produces the adjective and scope classes; the missing-comparison class needs a second corpus as counterpart. |
| P-x4 | On the older (MATS 8.0 era) papers, at least one elicited question will rest on knowledge not derivable from the PDF (contamination), detectable because its "where" field fails to ground in the document. |
| P-x5 | The admissions FAQ works as a rubric counterpart (paper beside Neel Nanda's own stated criteria), and that pairing yields the most reviewer-like questions of any. |

## Sonnet elicitation run (latent_welfare backtest) - filed 2026-08-19 before the run
| id | prediction |
|---|---|
| P-s1 | Sonnet-grade ELICIT keeps the question classes (claim-vs-data on paired arms, data-internal on blind) but writes thinner if_true/changes fields; ranking degrades before noticing does |
| P-s2 | C6 paired arm ranks the constant-7 meaning question in its top 3 |
| P-s3 | M2 paired arm RANKS the run-independence question top 5 (pilot: noticed, unranked); if so, credit the schema's forced if_true/changes fields |
| P-s4 | Every output passes gate_density (<= 10 codes/1000) with the contract embedded |
| P-s5 | At least one plausible catch not already in the pilot's queue |

## Question-rate vs user freshness - filed before computing
| id | prediction |
|---|---|
| P-u1 | Question rate falls with deadline proximity, but PHASE (exploration vs execution) explains more than clock time: late-night exploration prompts stay question-rich; deadline-morning execution prompts go imperative while the user is fresh |
| P-u2 | "Most active/least tired => everything is a question" NOT supported as stated; supported form: "exploration mode => questions", fatigue secondary |

## Outcomes - Sonnet elicitation run, read 2026-08-19
- P-s1 HALF-WRONG in a good direction: classes kept AND depth held; Sonnet did
  not visibly degrade ranking or the if_true/changes fields. Cheap tier suffices.
- P-s2 FAILED, inverted: the blind arm ranked the constant-7 meaning question
  first; the paired arm never mentioned it. Across pilot and this run, which
  arm surfaces that question is unstable; both types can.
- P-s3 FAILED: the run-independence question did not appear. The same arm
  instead found the in-place record edits (item 7) - bigger, but the filed
  prediction is dead.
- P-s4 FAILED, with a mechanistic attribution: same gate, three conditions -
  pilot A (no contract) 40-74 codes/1000; this run (principle only: "plain
  words first, codes in parentheses") 27-46; pilot B (categories named) 0-2.
  Third reproduction of the naming-gate, this time against my own prompt:
  I stated the principle and did not paste the named-category contract.
- P-s5 HELD, abundantly: items 7-13 in QUEUE.md, item 7 verified grounded
  against the live repo.
- P-u1/P-u2 HALF-WRONG: phase effect real (research 2.88 vs write-up 1.10
  questions/prompt; retro 4.57) but the day-to-night decline is monotone
  within BOTH phases and comparable in size - freshness matters on its own.
- Noise ledger: 39 questions across 5 arms; 2 identified duds, both
  slice-induced absence questions (files the slicer deliberately or
  accidentally excluded). Dud rate so far ~5%, cause known and fixable.

## Question-sample verification predictions - filed 2026-08-19 before sampling (seed=19 declared in advance)
- P-v-a: >=80% of sampled questions' cited numbers reproduce exactly from the
  slice files; expect ~1 in 8 to carry a misread field or slightly-off number
  (the pilot's cold reader had one pairing slip at similar volume).
- P-v-b: if_true/changes substance degrades with rank - top-3 concrete,
  ranks 6-8 drift toward generic "would change confidence" padding.
- P-v-c: effect-if-pressed across the sample: roughly a third wording/scope
  fixes, a third real instrument-or-claim impact, a third no-change
  (already-known or dud); duds concentrate in the absence class.
- P-v-d: neighbours cluster by artifact (arms walk files), not by mismatch
  class - a sampled question's neighbours will cite the same or adjacent
  files while asking a different kind of question.

validation_artifact?}] to triage_workflow.js (test copy). Any instrument
without a validation artifact emits an author-queue item mechanically.

{population}. Name the held-out ground truth that could refute this

If none exists, output one line: AUTHOR: <the validation control to write>.

aiTitle: Manifold formation evaluation against source claims

content.text:
All threads investigated. Primary sources found: the question-elicitation study exists — `welfare_probe/retro/BATTERY.md` + `OBSERVATIONS.md` (pilot), `BATTERY_B.md`/`OBSERVATIONS_B.md` (reruns), `harness/PREDICTIONS.md` (per-piece predictions + scored outcomes), the elicited outputs verbatim in `retro/elicited*/`. This was the DM-HACK-RETRO material you remembered.

## Do agents ask questions of themselves? The retro answered this directly.

The retro branch is literally an observational study of question formation, run against the project's own history. Its hypothesis (H-top, BATTERY.md, refuting outcome named in advance): frame-changing questions are gated on a **second representation** entering the context — they do not arise from evidence accumulating inside one anchored context. Three historical catches (C4, C6 "constant-7", M2 "replication is byte-identity") were replayed against fresh agents in different arms: BLIND (data only), IN-FRAME (data + frame texts), H3 (grounding pass). Findings, from OBSERVATIONS.md:

1. **"ASKING IS THE TRIGGER."** The named refuting outcome partially fired: the in-frame arm DID pose the historical meaning-question — because it was asked for questions. The historical agent never was. "Nobody asked" explains a large share of the record's gap on its own.
2. **Co-presence decides the question class.** Claims-beside-data yields claim-vs-data mismatches; data alone yields only data-internal anomalies. "Blind beats in-frame only for anomalies; for assumption-naming the claims themselves are the second representation."
3. **The bottleneck is notice vs press.** "The misses are never failures to see… Whatever ranks anomalies into questions is the scarce step, not detection." Constant-7: noticed, unranked. Determinism: noticed, unranked.
4. **One condition never tested:** an agent that AUTHORED the frame, rather than read it. Flagged explicitly as an open difference.

So the direct answer: no agent in this record ever presses its own questions from inside its own anchored context. The system's response was to **manufacture the self-questioning between contexts**: a fresh context + a pairing (never an object alone — EVENTS.md: "questions form where two things sit side by side; one thing alone yields a summary") + the standing ask + the answer-inhibition suffix + schema fields (`where/if_true/changes`) that do the pressing mechanically. Self-questioning implemented as other-questioning between contexts that share weights — with HEURISTICS' own caveat that shared weights share blind spots.

**Which pipeline versions carry this:** all of them, structurally. `elicit.md` is the battery's findings compiled into a prompt; the pipeline's post-phase Elicit embeds it verbatim; the Diff phase (v2's subtraction S1) is co-presence applied at design time (seed beside design); the meta suffixes are the answer-inhibition. v1 had elicit only; v2 onward has the full set. And the orchestrator applies it to itself via the press files — gatepress/d2press are the authored-frame agent compensating for the untested condition by pre-registering its own reading. The retro even measured the **human's** question rate (P-u1: research phase 2.88 questions/prompt, write-up 1.10, retro 4.57; freshness effect real and separate). One more result that matters later: the naming-gate reproduced three times, once against the orchestrator's own prompt (P-s4: principle-only contract 27–46 codes/1000, named-categories contract 0–2) — **general principles don't bite; naming the specific feature does.**

## Is invented data problematic?

Not by default — the record separates four failure conditions from syntheticness itself:

- **Timing.** Data invented at run time (C's reconstruction) is fatal; data invented before the run, committed with generator + selftest + sha + halt-if-absent (D/D2's `make_stimulus_linewrap*.py`, fully synthetic prose packing) ran clean and reproduced the anchor discipline. D2's anchor failure is not attributed to synthetic data (post pending).
- **H1, authoring blindness.** "Item drafters must not know which outcome favours the story." The realized risk is in the record on REAL data: the original study's self prompts run +2 tokens on all 82 items, same direction as the effect (QUEUE item 1); the trait-guard's replacement items had downward headroom by construction — "is the reading partly circular?" (rerun B). Carelessly authored real data is worse than blindly authored synthetic data.
- **H4.** An item family is an instrument: it asserts "this measures X on these items" and needs a validation artifact per version. Applies identically to natural and synthetic sets.
- **H3.** Uncommitted data is unauditable regardless of origin.

So takeaways showing examples of generated stimuli: valid, provided the examples come from the committed artifact (C2's seed showed 2 of its 50 verbatim for exactly this purpose).

## Is latent_skeptic superseded? Could the pipeline live in its repo?

Not superseded — embedded, called twice per seed (design-as-claim, question-triage). But the pipeline uses only its front half: `{claims}` is all it ever passes. `execute_runs`, `author`, `instruments` — never used; run/author queues land in records for the human, and the pipeline's own build/box path replaced the runner/author legs with a different execution model (pre-registered batch, not post-hoc controls).

The two copies have **drifted both ways**. The published submodule gained skeptic-prompt hardening the test copy lacks ("Most strong effects are confounded", "State your conclusion; do not then hedge it away"); the test copy gained the H4 instrument surface and the words-for-enums substitution ("the rule the doctrine had and the machinery lacked" — SKEPTIC_SUBSTITUTION.md, "Nothing is added"). The pipeline calls the test copy, so every seed's skeptics ran without the published hardening. Meanwhile the pipeline itself propagates by copy + deviation-record chain (mats_r1d1 → mats_manifold, "everything not listed is byte-identical"), which already produced a one-sentence divergence. That's the real content of your question: there is **no canonical repo for the composed system** — doctrine in one repo, hardened prompts in another, the composition in per-project copies. Whether pipeline.js belongs IN latent_skeptic is a boundary call: `triage_workflow.js` calls itself an "EXAMPLE COMPOSITION", and the pipeline is exactly another composition — but it drags infrastructure opinions (Lambda launcher, HF keys, gates by absolute path, human-gate conventions) into a repo whose doctrine is deliberately substrate-free. Mechanically, yes, plausible: the portable core is ~150 lines and its external references are three absolute paths. What the record warns about is not the move but the drift the move would have to end.

## Takeaways and synthesis, as they stand

Per-seed: written by the Write agent from three sources only (design record, results dir, elicited questions), gated twice, landed in repo root, read by the human. The source restriction is H1 doing its job — the writer cannot import narrative, which is why C2's writer independently re-derived the instrument problems.

Cross-seed synthesis exists but is **un-mechanized and unguarded**: the "Net sealed claim" lines in the ledgers, the framing paragraph each next seed opens with ("Two prior results frame this question…"), and these RETRO-x sessions themselves — this conversation is the synthesis stage, running with no contract, no gates, no elicit pass. Cross-seed numbers ("0.33 → 0.93 → 1.39, monotone") live only in ledger prose no gate ever ran on. Same structural shape as the human gate before gate-commits existed: a channel not yet typed. Whether that's problematic the evidence answers narrowly: the one demonstrated cross-seed failure was not synthesis prose but **known-issue non-propagation** — C proved the digit-mass gate passes dead-uniform distributions; C2 ran with that gate unchanged anyway. Which leads directly into your exercise.

## Retro-predictions for my three abstractions, then the evidence

Registered first, mechanically per seed, before re-consulting outcomes:

- **(i) Required anchor endpoint** — predicted: blocks or reframes seed A (forces paper-coordinates replication before refutation); no-op on B (no prior number); no-op on C through D2 (all already carried one).
- **(ii) Stimulus-sha gate** — predicted: no-op on A (public dataset, would need revision-pinning extension); blocks B at design time (saves $0.30 and makes its finding mechanical); blocks C at design time (saves the $8 wrong-experiment run, jumps straight to C2); no-op on C2/D/D2.
- **(iii) H4 instrument wiring** — predicted: mostly noise on A (selftests existed; construct gap already in does_not_test); on C, authors a validation control that plants the uniform case and discovers the mass-gate hole pre-run; prevents C2 shipping the known-insufficient gate.

Against the evidence, the surprises:

1. **(i) and (ii) were already invented at seed level by the time they'd have paid.** Machinery versions would have saved $0.30 + $8 + one ambiguous reframing of A. Every later seed carries them natively. Codifying them now guards nothing in this record — it guards only hypothetical naive future authors (the fan-out case).
2. **(iii) is where my prediction fails, and the failure is the finding.** The mass-gate hole was known THREE times before C2 ran: the pilot elicitation's Q3 (the 4.5-attractor question — "Matches the Fable elicitation's Q3 exactly", ledger), seed C's empirical confirmation, and C2's own diff question 2. Three independent surfaces caught it; none entered the design. Wiring a fourth surface would have changed nothing unless it BLOCKED. The notice-vs-press bottleneck reproduces at the human level: whatever converts pressed questions into design changes is scarcer than whatever ranks anomalies into questions.
3. **The H4 surface already existed, unused** — `instruments` arg, `validate.md`, even a scored mechanical test (P-v1). The doctrine had the rule, the machinery gained the surface, the caller never passed the argument. Surfaces without consumers do nothing — the naming-gate finding at architecture scale.

How this differs from my expectations: I diagnosed **guard-absence**; the record shows **consume-absence**. And it splits my proposals cleanly along a line the evidence draws everywhere: things that BLOCK have a working track record (budget gate, anchor void, scope/density gates, halt-not-patch, load-or-halt); things that INFORM have a track record of sitting unread (author_queues unexecuted in records, GUESS marks not stopping A's coordinates, three-time-known instrument hole shipping anyway). Your subtractive instinct is the record's own method — v2 was five subtractions, scored; 10 confounds → 2 held (S4); "a piece that fails its rerun comes back out" — and the record even names its current dead weight: steer.md never fired in any pipeline (P-f1 still open), user_sim.md unused, `rounds` pinned at 1, the runner/author legs never invoked by the pipeline, post mode running Design/Diff/Triage on a throwaway design (deviation record calls out the structural oddity). By the harness's own rule, pieces that never earn a rerun are the candidates for coming out — and the one addition the evidence would defend is not new machinery but a rerun-earning test of what's already wired but unconsumed.

Status note: D2 post phase still pending — anchor autopsy (instrument fault vs band mis-authored vs fresh-text fact) is the open question; the 0.7006-vs-0.701 near-miss at the old readout will be its center.
