content.text:
All verified — including fresh evidence: D2's post phase ran since my last look, and its elicit+triage record answers several of these questions directly. Answer in order.

## What would the INFORM surfaces have yielded, if run?

Item by item, priced against what actually happened:

- **Seed A's author_queue, item 1** (run the random-direction control in isolation across strengths first). The actual run's numbers say what it would have found: at the strong cells ANY vector degenerates output (100% degenerate at layer 24, +2x; injection norms 1.26x/1.03x of the model's entire activity, then doubled). It would have flagged the induction gate as unwinnable-by-construction pre-run, forcing rescaled strengths. **Highest-yield unconsumed item in the record** — it would have converted seed A from "refuted at degenerate coordinates" into a test at viable ones.
- **Seed A's author_queue, item 2** (degenerate-rate reporting for the suppress/removal legs): already realized — the build included it anyway. Zero marginal yield.
- **Instrument validation (`validate.md` + `instruments` arg), applied to C's digit-mass gate**: a validation control against planted ground truth has one obvious planted null — the uniform distribution — and would have caught pre-run both the attractor hole and plausibly the >1.0 bug. Both were instead discovered post hoc, three separate times. Yield: one $8 wrong-experiment run and half of C2's takeaways problem list.
- **Run_queues**: near-zero yield — in design mode they mostly say "run the committed pipeline," which execute mode consumes trivially.
- **GUESS marks**: yielded scope honesty in prose (does_not_test → takeaways caveats), never a better run. They are consumed by writers, not by designs.
- **steer.md**: unknowable — its prediction (P-f1) was filed and never run.

## Is BLOCK/INFORM definitional?

No — it's a property of the **coupling**, not the artifact. The same kind of number sits on both sides: `budget_usd` blocks because one `if` returns a halt; the anchor blocks because the run-summary's decision rule says void; the digit-mass "gate" was named a gate but its predicate was broken, so it blocked on the wrong condition. And D2 just supplied the sharpest version: **a BLOCK is only a block at the surfaces that re-check it.** D2's void is absolute in `run_summary` — and the three per-width wobble files still say `NULL_CLEARED`, clean, no void annotation. The post-elicit's top question (Q1) is exactly this: "did the check meant to void the whole run actually stop the three window results being reported as clean findings?" Grounding: reproduces — the void never propagated. So the split is: *is every downstream reader's execution conditioned on the value?* One conditional per surface, or the block leaks.

## The mass-gate-hole shape, predictions, observations

**Shape:** a known finding with no forced consumer at the next decision point. The next run's inputs are a curated slice (seed + design); prior findings live outside the slice; nothing conditions proceeding on having consumed them. It has a symmetric twin: when knowledge has no legitimate channel in, it gets **smuggled** in untyped.

Predicted instances before re-reading, then observed:

| # | Predicted | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Seed A coordinates: paper's layers 0-3 known, unconsumed → wrong-coordinate refutation | Confirmed (E5 caveat, post-elicit norm catch) |
| 2 | Seed A build: scorer-trap knowledge enters via untyped channel | Confirmed, verbatim — the deviation record IS the smuggling twin; corrective typed that exact knowledge into the pipeline's build contract |
| 3 | Seed B: F1 gating risk known but sealed → quarantined by the sealing discipline itself → box halt | Confirmed. Sealing predictions from agents structurally quarantines orchestrator foreknowledge; the seed is the only legitimate re-entry channel |
| 4 | C→C2: attractor + >1.0 known three times, unconsumed | Confirmed, and stronger than I had it: **C2's own pre-run grounding note flagged ">1.0 non-physical" in the committed design record** — fired, pre-run, in the artifact the human approved. No consumer: C2 predates gate-commits. GATE_COMMIT_seedD then starts consuming grounding notes ("Noted from triage grounding, accepted as-is…") — the fix trajectory already exists in the record |
| 5 | D2 would surface a fresh instance | Confirmed twice: the void-propagation leak (Q1), and Q5 — the anchor failure may itself be a selection-rule artifact (best-readout chosen pooled over nine widths picked readout 5; readout 6's width-140 quality was 0.7006, one-thousandth under the band floor) |

**Delta from my predictions:** I expected only non-consumption; the record adds the smuggling twin (build deviation; also C2's diff agent citing "an earlier run in this project" — knowledge in neither its seed nor its design, an un-prescribed channel with no mechanical slice guard). And I did not predict the void-leak class at all. One more unpredicted find: a skeptic in D2's triage returned `confound: "test", crux: "test"` — schema-valid placeholder garbage sitting in the committed record. Nothing screens finding content.

**Which parts helped, did they fire, effect:** grounding fired pre-run (C2) — no effect, no consumer. Diff fired (C2 q2, the uniformity hole) — no effect at the pre-gate-commit gate; fired in D — consumed via answers-of-record. Elicit fired everywhere — the one surface consistently consumed, because next-seed authoring eats it. The pattern is uniform: **detection never failed; consumption did.**

## What a subtractive resolution looks like

The record's working fixes all have one form: **remove an actor's freedom to proceed without consuming** — load-or-halt removed the runner's freedom to reconstruct; the derivability rule removed the design's freedom to assert; the frozen launcher removed the orchestrator's freedom to edit; gate-commits removed the human's untyped-approval channel. Additions of information never worked; removals of freedom always did. So for this class: not a new producer — an extension of the existing halt mechanism. Design mode already returns `halt: 'budget_over_cap'`; the same return, `halt: 'unconsumed_findings'`, when the instruments list has entries without validation artifacts, or when the lineage's prior grounding notes / diff departures lack an answer-of-record. The human can still answer "accepted as-is" — but cannot not-answer.

## The clone, concretely

1. **One canonical repo.** latent_skeptic gains `compositions/` (pipeline.js, gates, prompts). Per-project copies and the deviation-record chain die; projects pin a version. This alone ends the two-way drift.
2. **Merge the fork by its own rule.** P-r1 (the six sentence removals change no verdict substance) was filed and never run — run it; the losing text comes out. Don't hand-pick.
3. **Wire the consumption halts** (above) into design mode; execute mode takes the gate-commit path as an argument and checks each queued item has an answer line. Freedom-removal, not surface-addition.
4. **Propagate the void**: run-level void stamped into every per-cell file by provenance.py. One field. D2 Q1 is the motivating catch.
5. **Findings selftest**: reject schema-valid placeholders ("test"/empty cruxes) and resample — planted-row discipline applied to agent output.
6. **Subtract by the rerun rule**: `rounds` (pinned 1, never varied) out; steer.md/user_sim.md get their one filed rerun or come out; the runner/author legs stay in latent_skeptic (used elsewhere) but leave the pipeline's call surface, which never passes them.

## The hardened prompts: what are we actually missing?

Almost nothing demonstrable. The lines ("Most strong effects are confounded"; "State your conclusion; do not then hedge it away") target wrongful acquittal and hedging. Observed acquittals in the whole record: one in seed B v1, then nine in D2's post — and the D2 nine are **sound**: the claim was a file-content fact, the measurement confounds genuinely couldn't apply, and skeptics reasoned that correctly without the hardened lines. No covered failure traces to their absence; the one skeptic-side failure observed (the "test" placeholder) is schema-level, untouchable by prompt prose. And the retro's strongest replicated result predicts exactly this: those lines are stated principles, not named categories, and the naming-gate showed three times — once against the orchestrator's own prompt — that principles move outputs barely while naming specifics moves them twenty-fold. What the fork actually costs is not the lines; it's that two doctrinal texts exist with their comparison (P-r1) never run.

## What the new design would miss — answered, then checked against the record

Predicted misses: (1) question quality itself — nothing audits the seed; a flawed question passes every gate (seed B was caught only because a human built it as a control); (2) the synthesis layer — ledger prose and these RETRO-x sessions stay untyped; (3) constructs with no possible validation artifact — the welfare items (free reply "No" 50/50, elicited answer "Yes" 50/50; no held-out ground truth exists for that instrument, so the H4 halt would just park it); (4) gate-commit answer *quality* — consumption is forced, comprehension isn't; a human can "accept as-is" straight through; (5) weight-sharing blind spots — every role, one model family (the battery's own named limit).

Second look at the evidence for what I still hadn't covered: three more. **Selection rules inside instruments** — D2's anchor was consumed, blocked correctly, and may still be wrong by definition (pooled-best-readout vs per-width-best); validation artifacts as specified don't cover selection rules, only outputs. **Slice discipline for workflow agents** — the diff agent's extra-slice knowledge shows prompt-level "read only X" with no mechanical guard; the retro already knew blinding-by-label fails, and the pipeline never got a slices.sh equivalent. **The design's own validation debt** — the harness carries filed-but-never-run predictions (P-r1, P-f1, P-q1), and my clone adds pieces with reruns of their own. What previous seeds predict about that is unambiguous: every surface whose check stayed unrun eventually cost a run (C) or a headline (D2's leak). So the clone's most likely failure site is recursive — its own unconsumed validation queue — and the only consistent posture is that the consumption halt applies to the machinery's rerun ledger too: a piece whose filed rerun has not run is itself an unconsumed finding.

1	// EXAMPLE COMPOSITION of the latent_skeptic parts (rules: HEURISTICS.md; roles: agents/*.md).
2	// Invoke: Workflow({ scriptPath: "<clone>/triage_workflow.js", args: { claims: [
3	//   { id: "<slug>", text: "<one-sentence claim>", evidence: "<committed numbers/file:line only>", confounds: [] }
4	// ], execute_runs: false } })
5	//   text: the claim, not the story. evidence: the bounded slice only (H1 sets why). confounds []: general
6	//   defaults below; override only to add a project-specific one. Optional: ground:false skips the reader
7	//   pass; author:true fans claim-blind authors over the author_queue; execute_runs:true only after reading
8	//   the queues (pass 1 is free of GPU: skeptics acquit what committed numbers kill, the rest queue).
9	// Between passes, make each run_queue item a full command (e.g. prefix the GPU launcher); author_queue
10	//   items are specs, written to controls/ for review before running.
11	// Output per claim: grounding (reader verdict), findings = raw {confound, status, crux} (no rollup by
12	//   design; for a NULL claim an EXPLAINS can be the claim holding, the crux says which), run_queue,
13	//   author_queue, runner_results. Top-level shared_queue = controls needed by >= 2 claims; run once.
14	// Config: model inherits the session; per-role efforts set below; agent model: fields are defaults,
15	//   downsizable per the Operating discipline. Keep rounds:1 (breadth is one-confound-per-skeptic, not
16	//   re-sampling). Keep prompt strings free of em-dashes.
17	export const meta = {
18	  name: 'claim-triage',
19	  description: 'Adversarial triage of measured research claims: an isolated reader grounds each claim in its primary artifacts (H3); fresh independent skeptics (one confound each) reason over the committed numbers and emit a raw status + crux per confound (H1; H2 number-gates: falsifiability, margin, scope); unresolved cruxes become a run-queue (existing controls) or author-queue (controls to write); an optional read-only runner executes the run-queue. Queue items shared across claims are hoisted to a shared_queue so instrument-level checks run once, not per-claim (H4). No rolled-up score or verdict (the human reads the cruxes).',
20	  phases: [
21	    { title: 'Ground' },
22	    { title: 'Skeptics' },
23	    { title: 'Adjudicate' },
24	    { title: 'Verify' },
25	    { title: 'Author' },
26	  ],
27	}
28	
29	// Prompts are short and reused; schemas are kept to a small flat tail. Routing
30	// rules live in the prompt, not in nested schema. The runner's discipline lives
31	// once in agents/triage-runner.md, so the per-call message stays tiny.
32	
33	// General confound menu (not project-specific). A claim may override via its
34	// own confounds: field. Tier A (first two) are intervention-validity confounds
35	// general to any ablation; the rest are general measurement confounds.
36	const DEFAULT_CONFOUNDS = [
37	  'off-distribution ablation',
38	  'downstream compensation (self-repair)',
39	  'selection bias',
40	  'readout artifact',
41	  'regime specificity',
42	  'construct validity',
43	  'scale incomparability',
44	  'noise floor',
45	  'ceiling or floor effect',
46	  'single-case overfit',
47	]
48	
49	// ---- SKEPTIC (the analytical agent): one fresh reasoner per (claim x confound).
50	// H1. Tool-less by instruction: it decides only from the evidence in the prompt.
51	// Reason in prose, then emit the 4-field tail. No nested schema.
52	const SKEPTIC = (claim, confound) => `You audit ONE measured claim through ONE assigned confound. Findings here are numbers measured from a model, not text a model wrote. Default stance: assume the claim is an ARTIFACT of your confound until a committed number rules it out. Most strong effects are confounded.
53	
54	Think before answering; do not guess. Decide only from the evidence below; do not call tools or read files. If you cannot name the deciding number, it is NEEDS_RUN, not RULED_OUT. Do not invent a control. State your conclusion; do not then hedge it away.
55	
56	CONFOUND: ${confound}
57	CLAIM: ${claim.text}
58	EVIDENCE (the only data you may treat as established): ${claim.evidence}
59	
60	Reason in prose, then output the JSON tail:
61	- status RULED_OUT only if you can name the committed number / file:line that makes your confound unable to explain the claim; put that number in next.
62	- status EXPLAINS if the evidence is consistent with your confound producing the claim.
63	- status NEEDS_RUN if the committed data cannot decide it; then next is ONE line, tagged "RUN: <existing script + flags>" if an existing control settles it, else "AUTHOR: <the control to write>".
64	- crux: the one fact your verdict hinges on. If the claim is itself a null ("X is uninformative / diffuse / at the noise floor"), a confound that EXPLAINS the statistic may BE the claim holding, not refuting it -- say which in the crux.
65	Number-gates (H2) that apply whatever your confound: a cited number decides only if a refuting outcome was possible and named before the run (a claim every outcome supports is framing -- treat as EXPLAINS); only with margin (exact-threshold clearance, a threshold authored after seeing the data, or selection from unreported attempts does not decide); and only within tested scope (stated scope exceeding the tested population, scale, or design strength is EXPLAINS on that ground).
66	Examples of next -- RULED_OUT: "same effect on held-out set, foo.json:42, n=30". NEEDS_RUN: "AUTHOR: mean/resample-ablation variant; only zero-ablation on record".`
67	
68	const SKEPTIC_SCHEMA = {
69	  type: 'object',
70	  additionalProperties: false,
71	  required: ['confound', 'status', 'crux', 'next'],
72	  properties: {
73	    confound: { type: 'string' },
74	    status: { type: 'string', enum: ['RULED_OUT', 'EXPLAINS', 'NEEDS_RUN'] },
75	    crux: { type: 'string' },
76	    next: { type: 'string', description: 'RULED_OUT: the committed number/file:line. NEEDS_RUN: one line tagged RUN: or AUTHOR:. EXPLAINS: brief why.' },
77	  },
78	}
79	
80	// ---- ADJUDICATOR: dedup only. No score, no verdict label. The raw status + crux
81	// of every skeptic passes through to the human untouched (see the return); a
82	// rolled-up score masks the behaviour and mislabels null claims.
83	const ADJUDICATOR = (claim, verdicts, runnerResults) => `Dedup the controls the skeptics proposed for ONE claim. Do NOT score, do NOT emit a verdict label, do NOT reword cruxes (those pass through raw to the human).
84	${runnerResults ? `A runner produced new numbers: ${JSON.stringify(runnerResults)} -- drop any queued control it already settled.\n` : ''}VERDICTS: ${JSON.stringify(verdicts)}
85	From the NEEDS_RUN entries take the next-line: tagged "RUN:" -> run_queue, tagged "AUTHOR:" -> author_queue. Dedup near-identical controls: if several confounds need the same control (e.g. one matched-resample-ablation answers off-distribution AND self-repair AND noise-floor), emit it ONCE. Output ONLY the two distinct lists.`
86	
87	const ADJ_SCHEMA = {
88	  type: 'object',
89	  additionalProperties: false,
90	  required: ['run_queue', 'author_queue'],
91	  properties: {
92	    run_queue: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'distinct existing-control commands the runner can execute' },
93	    author_queue: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'distinct controls that do not exist yet; to author' },
94	  },
95	}
96	
97	// ---- RUNNER: thin and reused. All discipline lives in agents/triage-runner.md;
98	// the per-call message is just the item. The control decides its own verdict;
99	// the runner returns it verbatim.
100	const RUNNER = (item) => `Run this control and report its result verbatim:\n${item}`
101	
102	const RUNNER_SCHEMA = {
103	  type: 'object',
104	  additionalProperties: false,
105	  required: ['matches', 'teardown_ok'],
106	  properties: {
107	    result: { type: 'string', description: "the control's own decision / numbers, verbatim" },
108	    matches: { type: 'string', enum: ['claim', 'confound', 'ambiguous', 'not_runnable'] },
109	    teardown_ok: { type: 'boolean' },
110	  },
111	}
112	
113	// ---- AUTHOR: fresh, claim-blind agent that writes ONE new control from a spec.
114	// Discipline lives in agents/triage-author.md. It writes, it does not run.
115	const AUTHOR = (spec, path) => `Write a new measurement control from this spec, to ${path}.\nSPEC: ${spec}\nRead the existing scripts in this repo to match conventions and get the measurement correct.`
116	
117	const AUTHOR_SCHEMA = {
118	  type: 'object',
119	  additionalProperties: false,
120	  required: ['control_path', 'run_command', 'measures', 'decision_rule'],
121	  properties: {
122	    control_path: { type: 'string' },
123	    run_command: { type: 'string', description: 'existing launcher + this script, ready for the runner' },
124	    measures: { type: 'string' },
125	    decision_rule: { type: 'string', description: 'neutral threshold on the measured number; no claim/confound reference' },
126	  },
127	}
128	
129	// ---- READER: fresh agent that GROUNDS a claim by reading its primary artifacts (H3). It reads the INPUT
130	// (items / labels / directional-training data a result was computed from) AND the OUTPUT (generations,
131	// per-token values, result JSONs), re-derives the claim's headline number from the raw artifact, and reports
132	// whether it reproduces. It reads in its own context (preserving the orchestrator's) and never runs or edits.
133	// Discipline lives in agents/triage-reader.md. This does not replace the orchestrator's own reading; it
134	// guarantees the primary data is read in full, for every claim.
135	const READER = (c) => `Ground this claim by reading the PRIMARY artifacts behind it and checking its numbers reproduce from the raw data. You read; you do not run or edit.\n\nCLAIM: ${c.text}\nEVIDENCE (cites the input data/labels and the output/result files): ${c.evidence}\n\nOpen the INPUTS (the items, labels, or directional-training data a result was computed from) AND the OUTPUTS (the generations, per-token values, result JSONs). Re-derive the claim's headline number(s) from the raw artifact. grounding="reproduces" if it matches; "diverges" if the raw data gives a different number; "unauditable" if the artifact needed to check it was never saved (that absence IS the finding); "absent" if the cited file is missing. Put both numbers in observed; one line in note.`
136	
137	const READER_SCHEMA = {
138	  type: 'object',
139	  additionalProperties: false,
140	  required: ['grounding', 'note'],
141	  properties: {
142	    artifacts_read: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'paths actually opened' },
143	    observed: { type: 'string', description: "the number(s) re-derived from the raw artifact vs the claim's" },
144	    grounding: { type: 'string', enum: ['reproduces', 'diverges', 'unauditable', 'absent'] },
145	    note: { type: 'string', description: 'one line: the mismatch, or which artifact was never saved' },
146	  },
147	}
148	
149	// Orchestration. All agents inherit the session model; effort per role.
150	
151	const A = (typeof args === 'string' ? JSON.parse(args) : args) || {}   // runtime may deliver args as a JSON string
152	const claims = A.claims || []
153	if (!claims.length) {
154	  log('Pass { claims: [{id, text, evidence, confounds?}], execute_runs?, rounds? }.')
155	  return { error: 'no claims provided' }
156	}
157	const execute = !!A.execute_runs
158	const rounds = A.rounds || 1
159	const ground = A.ground !== false              // H3: read the primary artifacts; ON by default (pass ground:false to skip)
160	log(`Triaging ${claims.length} claim(s); confounds=${DEFAULT_CONFOUNDS.length}; execute_runs=${execute}; ground=${ground}.`)
161	
162	// H3 fan-out: one isolated reader per claim reads its cited inputs + outputs and re-derives the number.
163	// Returned as a separate leg (NOT fed to the tool-less skeptics, preserving H1).
164	const groundings = {}
165	if (ground) {
166	  const gs = await parallel(claims.map((c) => () =>
167	    agent(READER(c), { label: `read:${c.id}`, phase: 'Ground', agentType: 'triage-reader', effort: 'low', schema: READER_SCHEMA })))
168	  claims.forEach((c, i) => { groundings[c.id] = gs[i] || null })
169	}
170	
171	const triaged = await pipeline(
172	  claims,
173	  (c) => {                                       // skeptic fan-out (H1: fresh, tool-less, bounded slice)
174	    const confounds = (c.confounds && c.confounds.length) ? c.confounds : DEFAULT_CONFOUNDS
175	    const jobs = []
176	    for (const cf of confounds) for (let r = 0; r < rounds; r++)
177	      jobs.push(() => agent(SKEPTIC(c, cf), { label: `skeptic:${c.id}:${cf.slice(0, 20)}`, phase: 'Skeptics', effort: 'medium', schema: SKEPTIC_SCHEMA }))
178	    return parallel(jobs).then((v) => ({ claim: c, verdicts: v.filter(Boolean) }))
179	  },
180	  (r) => agent(ADJUDICATOR(r.claim, r.verdicts, null), { label: `adjudicate:${r.claim.id}`, phase: 'Adjudicate', effort: 'low', schema: ADJ_SCHEMA }).then((adj) => ({ ...r, adjudication: adj })),
181	)
182	
183	let final = triaged
184	if (execute) {                                   // H2: only this step makes new evidence; gated + non-mutating
185	  final = await parallel(triaged.map((r) => () => {
186	    const queue = (r.adjudication && r.adjudication.run_queue) || []
187	    if (!queue.length) return Promise.resolve(r)
188	    return parallel(queue.map((item) => () => agent(RUNNER(item), { label: `run:${r.claim.id}`, phase: 'Verify', agentType: 'triage-runner', effort: 'low', schema: RUNNER_SCHEMA })))
189	      .then((runs) => {
190	        const ran = runs.filter(Boolean)
191	        return agent(ADJUDICATOR(r.claim, r.verdicts, ran), { label: `re-adjudicate:${r.claim.id}`, phase: 'Adjudicate', effort: 'low', schema: ADJ_SCHEMA }).then((adj) => ({ ...r, runner_results: ran, adjudication: adj }))
192	      })
193	  }))
194	}
195	
196	let authored = null
197	if (A.author) {                                  // claim-blind author fan-out over the (deduped) author_queue
198	  authored = await parallel(final.map((r) => () => {
199	    const aq = (r.adjudication && r.adjudication.author_queue) || []
200	    if (!aq.length) return Promise.resolve({ id: r.claim.id, controls: [] })
201	    return parallel(aq.map((spec, idx) => () => agent(AUTHOR(spec, `controls/${r.claim.id}_${idx + 1}.py`), {
202	      label: `author:${r.claim.id}:${idx + 1}`, phase: 'Author', agentType: 'triage-author', effort: 'medium', schema: AUTHOR_SCHEMA
203	    }))).then((cs) => ({ id: r.claim.id, controls: cs.filter(Boolean) }))
204	  }))
205	}
206	
207	// H4 hoist: a control that several CLAIMS need is instrument-level (taints them all at once); surface it
208	// ONCE in shared_queue so it is checked at the instrument, not re-run per claim. Pure string dedup;
209	// per-claim queues are left intact for provenance.
210	const seenBy = {}
211	for (const r of final) {
212	  const adj = r.adjudication || {}
213	  for (const item of [...(adj.run_queue || []), ...(adj.author_queue || [])]) {
214	    const k = item.trim().toLowerCase()
215	    ;(seenBy[k] = seenBy[k] || { item, claims: [] }).claims.push(r.claim.id)
216	  }
217	}
218	const shared_queue = Object.values(seenBy).filter((e) => e.claims.length >= 2)
219	
220	return {
221	  claims: final.map((r) => ({
222	    id: r.claim.id,
223	    grounding: groundings[r.claim.id] || null,  // H3: did the claim's numbers reproduce from the raw input+output artifacts
224	    findings: (r.verdicts || []).map((v) => ({ confound: v.confound, status: v.status, crux: v.crux })),  // raw ground truth; read these
225	    run_queue: (r.adjudication && r.adjudication.run_queue) || [],
226	    author_queue: (r.adjudication && r.adjudication.author_queue) || [],
227	    runner_results: r.runner_results || null,
228	  })),
229	  shared_queue,   // H4: controls needed by >= 2 claims; run these once, at the instrument
230	  authored,
231	}
232

# Wording rerun - decides which skeptic text survives (P-r1, finally run)

Two branches differ in ONE factor: the SKEPTIC prompt text in triage_workflow.js.

- v2.2-a: the published text, three doctrine sentences present ("Most strong
  effects are confounded." / "Think before answering; do not guess." / "State
  your conclusion; do not then hedge it away.")
- v2.2-b: the substituted text, those sentences removed (rationale:
  welfare_probe/retro/SKEPTIC_SUBSTITUTION.md)

Everything else is byte-identical; verify with `git diff v2.2-a v2.2-b`, which
must touch one constant in one file. If it touches more, the rerun is void.

## Protocol

Battery precedent (welfare_probe/retro/BATTERY.md): identical instructions,
arms differ only in the factor under test; observational reading first,
scoring only where mechanical. Claims are KNOWN ones with committed outcomes,
so soundness has an anchor:

1. K1, false-acquittal bait: seed B v1 design-as-claim (the harmful/harmless
   "reasoning direction"). History: construct validity EXPLAINS. A RULED_OUT
   on that confound is a wrongful acquittal.
   Source: mats_r1d1/records/seedB_design_and_triage.json.
2. K2, file-fact claim: seed D2 post question 1 (run-void flag never
   propagated into the three per-width result files). Sound behaviour:
   RULED_OUT on inapplicable measurement confounds, without invented
   statistics. Source: mats_manifold/records/seedD2_post_elicit_qtriage.json.
3. K3, thin-evidence claim: seed C2 design-as-claim pre-run. Sound behaviour:
   NEEDS_RUN. Source: mats_r1d1/records/seedC2_scale_design_diff_triage.json.

Run both branches on all three claims, same confound menu, same model and
effort, one round. Pass ground:false (the artifacts predate this repo).
Read findings side by side. Mechanical scores only: status agreement per
(claim x confound) cell, RULED_OUT counts on K1, crux word counts,
degenerate-finding counts.

## Registered predictions - filed with this commit, before any run

- P-w1: statuses agree across branches in at least 90 percent of the 30
  (claim x confound) cells. Basis: the three sentences are stated principles,
  not named categories, and the naming-gate result reproduced three times
  (rerun B arm C; Sonnet run P-s4): principles move outputs little.
- P-w2: any disagreements sit on the EXPLAINS versus NEEDS_RUN boundary;
  neither branch RULED_OUT-acquits K1's construct-validity confound.
- P-w3: hedged cruxes (a verdict plus its own retraction) are rare in both
  branches and not differential.
- P-w4: without the degeneracy filter the content-free finding rate would be
  near its observed base rate (1 in roughly 80: the committed "test"/"test"
  case in seedD2_post_elicit_qtriage.json); with the filter, zero reach the
  returned findings and any rejections are logged.

## Decision rule - pre-registered

If P-w1 holds and no differential wrongful acquittal appears on K1: the
SHORTER text survives, because a sentence that changes no verdict comes out
(the harness rule: a piece that fails its rerun comes back out). If K1
acquittals differ: the text that refuses the false acquittal survives,
regardless of length. Either way exactly one branch merges to main and the
other is deleted.

Queued, untested here: the agents/*.md wording substitutions (same
SKEPTIC_SUBSTITUTION source) are a separate cell; do not fold them into this
rerun's factor.

## Cost prediction

3 claims x 10 confounds x 2 branches = 60 skeptic calls, plus 6 adjudications.
LLM-only; no GPU; no box.

# compositions/ - the seed pipeline, canonical home

One question in, takeaways out, agents speaking only through typed contracts.
This directory ends the copy-and-deviate chain: projects pin a version of this
repo and pass paths as args; nothing here is copied out and edited in place.

## Pieces

- pipeline.js   design -> diff -> triage -> [human gate] -> build -> [launcher,
                run verbatim by the orchestrator] -> elicit -> question-triage
                -> takeaways. Modes: design / build / post.
- gates/        mechanical prose blocks: code density, scope tags. Model-free
                selftests; run them before trusting a gate.
- prompts/      contract (language), elicit (question formation), meta (the two
                standing suffixes), validate (the H4 ask). steer and user_sim
                are deliberately absent: their reruns never ran (RERUN_LEDGER.md).

## What v2.2 changes, and the evidence that forced each change

1. Consumption law. Build and post halt unless a gate commit file answers, of
   record, every diff question, every non-reproducing grounding note, and every
   queued control or instrument validation. Forced by: seed C2's pre-run
   grounding note flagged its readout as non-physical; nothing consumed it; the
   run shipped with the broken readout and the takeaways rediscovered it.
2. Instruments wired (H4). Each endpoint's readout enters triage as an
   instrument; missing validation artifacts queue mechanically and meet the
   consumption law at the gate. Forced by: the digit-mass gate passed a
   dead-uniform distribution across two seeds while the surface that would have
   caught it sat unwired.
3. Void propagation. The build contract requires run_valid in every record,
   with gate failure propagating to every later record, and a planted
   gate-failure selftest row. Forced by: seed D2's void lived only in its run
   summary while three per-width files reported clean positive decisions.
4. Mode branch above the design phase. Build and post bind to committed
   records and never re-run design. Forced by: the booked v2.1 deviation where
   a throwaway design's guessed budget spuriously halted a post pass.
5. No default paths. triage_path, gates_dir, conventions are required args.
   Forced by: hardcoded absolute paths are how per-project copies drifted.
6. Degenerate-finding rejection (in triage_workflow.js). Forced by: a
   schema-valid skeptic finding of confound "test", crux "test", committed as
   a result.
7. Diff agent is told to decide from its two texts only. Forced by: a diff
   output citing knowledge present in neither its seed nor its design.

## Human appears three times

Chooses the seed; writes the gate commit (now checked for coverage, never for
quality); reads the takeaways and the question ledger. Sealed predictions stay
outside the pipeline entirely: filed before agents run, never passed to them,
scored append-only.

## Deployment

Per project: a frozen/ (provenance writer, launcher) and keys stay project-side;
invoke this pipeline with explicit paths. The launcher is run verbatim by the
orchestrator because it blocks for the whole box lifecycle. Never edit an
in-use launcher while any box runs; copy per-launch or freeze.

Assembled and committed. Repo back on `main`, untouched; two branches registered:

```
latent_skeptic/
  main      (untouched, tracks origin)
  v2.2-a    abbab68  structural changes + published (hardened) skeptic wording
  v2.2-b    ea3718c  = v2.2-a with ONE delta: the three doctrine sentences removed
```

Verified: `git diff v2.2-a v2.2-b` touches one constant in one file — 2 insertions, 2 deletions. Single-factor discipline holds mechanically; WORDING_RERUN.md declares the rerun void if that diff ever grows. Both scripts syntax-check (wrapped in the Workflow runtime's async dialect); both gates pass their model-free selftests.

**What v2.2-a contains** (each change mapped to its forcing failure in `compositions/README.md`):

- `triage_workflow.js`: H4 instruments surface ported (queue fires when `validation_artifact` absent); `rounds` removed (never varied from 1 anywhere); content-free findings rejected with one resample, rejections logged and returned as `rejected_findings` — the committed "test"/"test" case can no longer sit silently as a finding.
- `compositions/pipeline.js`: the consumption law — build/post halt `unconsumed_findings` unless the gate-commit answers every diff question, non-reproducing grounding note, and queued item ("accepted as-is" counts; silence doesn't); endpoint readouts enter triage as instruments; build contract requires `run_valid` in every record with a planted gate-failure selftest row (D2's void leak); mode branch moved above design (the booked v2.1 deviation); no default paths — `triage_path`/`gates_dir`/`conventions` are required args, because hardcoded absolute paths are how copies drifted; diff agent now told to decide from its two texts only (the extra-slice-knowledge catch).
- `WORDING_RERUN.md` + `RERUN_LEDGER.md` at root.

**Is the two-branch approach supported by evidence?** Yes, on four precedents: P-r1's own filed verify is exactly this ("two known claims through original and edited skeptic prompts; statuses and cruxes read side by side"); the battery's arm method (identical instructions, differ only in the factor, observational reading first, scoring only where mechanical); rerun-B's three-arm wording comparison, which produced the record's strongest quantified result (the 20-fold density move); and the A/B twin-seed pattern for adversarial pairs. One evidence-based caution folded into the protocol: F9 (design non-reproducibility) means single samples confound wording with sampling noise — so the rerun runs on **known claims with committed outcomes** (K1: seed B's construct-confounded design, where a RULED_OUT is a wrongful acquittal; K2: D2's file-fact claim, testing menu misfit; K3: C2's thin-evidence design, where NEEDS_RUN is correct), giving soundness an anchor instead of a vibe.

**What it tests and how I predict it runs** — registered in the committed file before any run: P-w1, statuses agree in ≥90% of the 30 cells (the naming-gate extrapolation: these are principles, not named categories, and principles moved outputs little in three reproductions); P-w2, no differential acquittal on K1; P-w3, hedging rare and non-differential; P-w4, the degeneracy filter keeps content-free findings out of the record at the observed ~1-in-80 base rate. Decision rule pre-registered: if P-w1 holds and K1 is clean, the **shorter** text survives — a sentence that changes no verdict comes out; if K1 acquittals differ, the text that refuses the false acquittal survives regardless of length. Exactly one branch merges; the other is deleted. Cost: ~60 skeptic calls plus adjudications, LLM-only, no GPU.

**The blind-spot conclusion, implemented.** The recursive rule — a piece whose filed rerun never ran is itself an unconsumed finding — is now `RERUN_LEDGER.md`: every piece rides with its prediction and a status; OPEN rows block (the wording rerun blocks merging either branch; the GateCheck row carries its own concrete test — run it against C2's design record and the v2.1-era ledger, prediction: it surfaces the ">1.0 non-physical" grounding note nothing ever answered — a backtest with a known miss as ground truth). steer.md and user_sim.md are excluded from compositions/ until their reruns run, not deleted from the harness. The remaining uncovered blind spots stay uncovered and stay named: gate-answer quality (coverage is checked, comprehension isn't), constructs with no possible validation artifact, selection rules inside instruments, the synthesis layer, weight-sharing.

**Are the changes broadly subtractive?** Honestly: subtractive in freedom, roughly neutral in lines, and every added line is a conditional or a ledger row — none is a new producer of information. Subtracted: the copy-and-deviate propagation model, `rounds`, two never-run prompts from the composition, the throwaway design in build/post, all default paths, one of the two competing wordings (pending the rerun), and the agents' freedom to proceed past unconsumed findings. Added: one halt condition, one field requirement, one filter, two protocol documents. The additions exist to make future subtractions decidable — which is what the rerun ledger is for.

Next mover is the human: run the wording rerun (both branches, three claims, `ground:false`), score P-w1–P-w4, merge the survivor.

Registering predictions first — before reading anything further, including the MATS doc.

**P-1 (previously, good question):** the eight learned rules — data embedded or sha-pinned with halt-if-absent; replication anchor with band; instrument-failure named as instrument fact; load-bearing constants fixed, rest to calibration; fork not presence; scope lines; artifact-retention demands; no bundled premises. content.text:
Predictions registered above. Evidence read — MATS doc in full, seed record already in context. Observations, scored against each prediction, then the MATS work.

## Scoring the predictions

**P-1 (what "good" looked like before) — held**, with one correction from the re-read: the eight rules weren't simultaneous; they accreted one failure at a time, and each clause is a fossilized unconsumed finding (C2's data clause ← C's reconstruction; D's artifact demands ← D1's unauditable geometry; D2's escape hatch ← D's aperture censorship; D2's save-all-nulls ← D1's missing per-draw vectors).

**P-2 (what "good" looks like now) — held, but thinner than I predicted in one direction and thicker in another.** Working backward through v2.2's actual constraints: GateCheck + instrument queue absorb the *artifact-retention* and *threshold-hygiene* duties (bad guesses now surface as queued items demanding answers, instead of shipping). But two things I predicted would move to machinery did not: the anchor (deliberately not schema-required — it over-applied to seed A, where failing to reproduce WAS the finding) and construct semantics (a validation artifact proves an instrument measures something; only the seed says what it was supposed to measure). So the five seed-only duties stand: **committed data reference, anchor number + band where a prior number exists, scope lines, the fork, construct semantics.** Everything else may return to the design agent. Predicted seed size 300–500 words looks right: C2 minus its guard-clauses and worked examples is ~300.

**P-3 (run-quickly) — held cleanly.** The three cheap runs (C2 $8, D1 $0.43/13 min, D2 $0.55/~18 min) are all logit-or-probe readouts, no sampling; the expensive one (A, 4400 sampled generations) is the only generation-heavy seed. The 90-minute on-box hard cap institutionalized the property. One addition I missed: **model-free endpoint arithmetic** is what makes the fast runs also *auditable* fast — the combine step runs locally, no second box.

**P-4 (decomposable) — held, plus one property I under-weighted and one I missed.** Confirmed: one varied coordinate per instance (C2's sizes, D2's apertures), frozen definitions in the shared seed, anchor-first-then-fan (C2 ran 9b, confirmed the anchor, THEN fanned 2b/27b), no shared mutable infra (the launcher-edit kill is the precedent; rule: per-launch copy or freeze). Under-weighted: **budget topology** — a fan needs a ledger with headroom (BUDGET.md), one gate approving n boxes. Missed entirely: **the hidden-coordinate hazard** — C2's fan varied more than its named axis (2b/9b distilled, 27b trained from scratch; the recipe-vs-size confound, booked but undecidable). A MECE fan is only MECE in the coordinates you named. The two scenarios otherwise share machinery; they differ in where invention may sit (single-cell can defer constants to calibration; a fan must freeze everything before the split) and in anchor topology.

**P-5 (criteria → pipeline use) — held, with one inversion worth stating.** The progression: A used the pipeline as *author* (17 invented does_not_test entries, heavy post-hoc audit); B as *detector* (halt was the output); C as *faithful extender* (failed — fidelity wasn't the pipeline's to give); C2 as *executor + auditor*; D added a new use — *design-mode as cheap dry-run* (the gate press amended the seed before any GPU spend); D2 as *pure executor with audit*. The design agent's share shrank monotonically from author to type-checker. The inversion: **elicit's yield did not shrink as seeds hardened.** A's elicit found phenomenon-level problems; D2's elicit found instrument-level ones (the void leak, the selection-rule question). Hardening the question moved discovery UP a level; it never reduced it. Contrast with the faults: the faults were consumption failures; the criteria evolution was the orchestrator compensating by pre-consuming findings into seed prose. v2.2 mechanizes consumption — so the honest expectation is that seeds can relax back toward A-like naturalness *except* on the five seed-only duties, and the next seed is the test of that.

## The MATS 12.0 doc

**P-6 half-held, half-wrong.** Wrong half: the doc contains no open-problem list at all — it's evaluation criteria, common mistakes, and six scored past applications (interest areas live behind an external link). Held half, strongly: the runnable material is exactly not a future-work list — it's the *assessments* of past projects, which name mechanism-vs-register mismatches (P-x2's prediction shape, and two of its three named targets appear verbatim in Nanda's own verdicts).

The striking observation: **Nanda's Common Mistakes list is our machinery, stated as human taste.** Near-isomorphic mapping: "not sanity checking your agent's work" = H3 grounding; "think of a way the results could be false, then discover you've already checked it" = named refuting outcome + skeptics; "building on a phenomenon without first checking it replicates in your setting — if the effect isn't there for your setup, everything downstream is noise" = the anchor gate, verbatim (this resolves your earlier unsureness about the anchor criterion — independent convergence from a source that never saw this pipeline); "skipping the cheap control: replace your vector with a random one" = seed A's matched-norm control; "investigating phenomena without checking it's really there" = the existence-check/decidability rule; "not looking at your data — read some data points" = elicit's raw-row sampling. Two lists evolved under different selection pressures converged on the same criteria. That's the strongest evidence yet that the criteria are properties of good questions, not artifacts of this pipeline.

**Refining doc-style material into research questions generally** takes the decidability cluster: an existence check first, one construct operationalized into a measurement register, a refuting outcome named, the simple method first. **Refining into pipeline-runnable questions** takes, additionally, the fidelity cluster plus three practical constraints: committed data (verbatim or generator+sha), model-free decision arithmetic, small open substrate under the 90-minute box cap. The difference is real and has a shape: the doc's ideal workflow is *interactive-exploratory* (talk to the model, look at data, pivot, reset the clock — pivoting is praised); the pipeline is *pre-registered-confirmatory* (a pivot is a new sealed seed, by design). They compose rather than compete: the doc's exploration phase = our seed-authoring plus design-mode dry-runs (LLM-only, cheap); the doc's "truth-seeking and skepticism" criterion = our execute-and-audit, mechanized. What the pipeline cannot supply from the doc's list: **taste** (problem choice, originality) and the pre-seed exploration itself — every seed so far followed completed prior work; the machinery has no pilot mode, and D's pilot lived in a proposal document authored outside it.

**Candidates**, with run sketches:

1. **R1D1 at the paper's own coordinates.** Seed A's refutation is booked as "at these guessed coordinates only"; the paper's effect sits at layers 0–3 on a unit vector. Seed: paper's coordinates fixed, matched-norm random control added (the control the paper lacked), GSM8K revision-pinned with a committed item list, anchor = the paper's own reported induction rate with a D1-style wide band (their exact stimuli are unpublished — the C-risk, absorbed by band width, and an anchor failure here is itself reportable as "does not replicate in our setting"). Generation-heavy, so A-priced (~$15), not C2-priced. Completes our own does_not_test debt; the strongest candidate.
2. **The Diffing project's latent definition as an instrument (H4 seed).** Nanda's own assessment: "a conceptual error in how it defined model-specific latents." Question: does that definition measure model-specificity? Validation control with ground truth by construction: train the same small crosscoder on two runs of the SAME model (true model-specific latents = zero by construction); the definition's false-positive rate is the endpoint, refuting outcome pre-named. Risk: crosscoder training against the 90-minute cap — needs a width/layer-subset GUESS, marked.
3. **CoT-unfaithfulness metric validity (H4 seed, planted rows).** Commit a stimulus where hint-use is true by construction (injected hints the model demonstrably uses); endpoint: the metric's detection rate on planted cases, refuting outcome "misses ≥ X%." Scoped deliberately to "detects planted hint-use," because full "unfaithfulness" has no ground truth — our named blind spot, respected rather than denied.
4. **Empathic Machines, redone under our fidelity cluster.** Nanda's verdict was "conclusions inherently limited by the data quality" — precisely what committed stimuli + instrument validation fix; and it adjoins the welfare_probe instrument stack we already validated the hard way.

**What the candidates reflect and miss.** They reflect the merged criteria almost completely: anchor-in-your-setting, committed data, cheap control, instrument-as-claim, decidable endpoints, small substrate. All four are audits or extensions of existing results — the same shape as seeds A–D2, and the shape both lists reward. What they miss, honestly: none carries an **in-repo prior number** — every anchor comes from a paper with unpublished settings, so all anchors are D1-grade (wide bands) rather than C2-grade (exact reproduction), and an anchor failure is ambiguous between harness-infidelity and non-replication in a way C2's never was; none is de-novo — the pipeline still has zero evidence it can serve a question that doesn't lean on someone's completed work; and taste is imported, not generated — three of four candidates are good *because Nanda's assessments pointed at the flaw*, which is the co-presence trick again: the assessments are the second representation, laid beside the projects.

**Pred-N3 (similarity):** Ideas similar in register — small-model behavioral/probe experiments; at least one near-duplicates an existing published result without knowing (memory of a profuse corpus = high collision rate).

**Pred-N4 (yield, per class):** Generation-heavy survivors project to seed-A economics (hours, degeneracy risk); probe/logit survivors project to D-grade (<$1, <20 min); any steering idea inherits seed A's off-manifold trap unless norm-matched controls are named; anything needing SAE/crosscoder training strains the 90-minute box cap.

**Pred-N5 (what agent 1 optimizes):** Interestingness + Nanda-taste mimicry, not decidability; fidelity criteria (committed data, anchor) absent entirely from its implicit checklist.

You generate candidate research question ideas in mechanistic interpretability, drawn from Neel Nanda's public writings. Nanda writes profusely: his "200 Concrete Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability" sequence (Alignment Forum / LessWrong), his blog (neelnanda.io), his stated research interests page, his recent Alignment Forum posts, and his MATS-related advice. Use web search and fetching to sample BROADLY across this material — do not rely on memory alone, and do not restrict yourself to one post. Recent material (2024-2026) counts more than old material where they conflict, since his interests have shifted over time.

Think and explain yourself as simply as possible, but no simpler. Do not provide solutions until you've thought and reasoned about the problem as thoroughly as possible without providing any.

Your task: produce exactly 20 DISTINCT research question ideas, spanning as many different areas of his material as you can. For each idea, before writing it, reason about what observation or gap in his writing actually motivates it - an idea motivated by a named gap beats an idea that just sounds interesting.

Rules:
- Each idea must come from his material (a post, problem list entry, stated interest, or an assessment/criticism he wrote), not from your own general knowledge of the field. Cite which piece.
- Ideas must be distinct from each other - not 20 variations of one theme. Cover at least 8 different topic areas.
- Do NOT evaluate feasibility, cost, or study design. Do not propose methods, experiments, or implementations. Ideas as QUESTIONS only.
- Phrase each idea the way the source material licenses it - if the source only supports "does X happen?", do not inflate it to "why does X happen?".

Output format, strictly, one block per idea, exactly these fields:

ID: N-01 (through N-20)
QUESTION: <the research question, 1-3 sentences>
SOURCE: <which Nanda piece motivates it - title + rough date; quote the motivating line if short>
REGISTER: <what would be observed or measured, ONLY if the source itself indicates this; otherwise write "unstated">
WHY: <one or two sentences, as simple as possible but no simpler: what gap or observation makes this worth asking>

End with a 5-line NOTES section: what you searched, what you could not access, which areas of his material you knowingly left uncovered, and any place where you were forced to rely on memory instead of a fetched source.

THE CRITERIA (evaluate each idea against each, by name):

3. COMMITTED-DATA: the stimulus or dataset can be committed verbatim before the run (a file with a hash) or produced by a committed deterministic generator. "A public dataset exists" is NOT sufficient unless it can be pinned to a revision and is not license-gated. Data described in prose but not committable fails.
4. ANCHOR: a prior measured number exists that the harness can first reproduce in-setting, with a tolerance band, before any new comparison counts. If no such number exists, the question can still pass ONLY by explicitly declaring the anchor absent.
5. SUBSTRATE: runnable on open-weights models small enough for one rented GPU box, under roughly 90 minutes of compute. Closed models, frontier-scale models, or long training runs fail.
6. READOUT: the measurement is logits, probes, or single forward passes where possible; long free generation is expensive and fragile. The final decision arithmetic must be computable by a model-free script.
7. FORK: every outcome is informative. A presence-only question ("is there an X?") whose null outcome teaches nothing fails; a question whose outcomes fork into named, distinct readings passes.
8. INSTRUMENT: every scorer, readout, or judge the question needs can be validated against ground truth known by construction (planted rows), OR the impossibility of such validation is declared in the question.
9. SCOPE: one cell — one substrate, one intervention axis. Sweeps, multi-model surveys, and "and also" extensions fail unless explicitly cut.
10. NO-BUNDLED-PREMISE: the question does not smuggle a construct mismatch (e.g., building a probe for concept A out of data that varies concept B, then naming it A).

PROCEDURE, in order:
(a) First, reason about the whole set: what kinds of questions are these, which criteria will do the most filtering and why. Write this as a short PREAMBLE (under 200 words).
(b) Then evaluate every idea, N-01 through N-20. For each criterion give PASS, FAIL, or FIXABLE. FIXABLE means one added sentence to the question would satisfy the criterion — state that sentence's content in under 15 words. Do not redesign the idea; if it needs more than one sentence per criterion, it is FAIL.
(c) An idea SURVIVES if it has no FAIL after fixes. Rank survivors (at most 6) by how few fixes they needed, ties broken by SUBSTRATE cheapness.

OUTPUT FORMAT, strictly:

PREAMBLE: <under 200 words>

Then one line per idea, N-01 through N-20:
N-XX | <PASS/FAIL/FIXABLE per criterion, as "1:PASS 2:FIXABLE(...) 3:FAIL ...">, ending with VERDICT: SURVIVES or OUT, and for OUT the single criterion that killed it.

While the filter runs — scoring what can be scored now, and registering per-idea survival predictions before the filter returns.

**Pred-N1 partially wrong, informatively.** ~11 of 20 ideas carry a stated register (correlation, AUROC, win rates, truncation performance) — far above my sub-25% prediction. Cause visible in the sources: the corpus shifted. My prediction was calibrated on the 2022 "200 Open Problems" prose style; agent 1 weighted 2025–26 GDM team updates, which are empirical posts with measurements attached. The anchor/committed-data half of the prediction held: zero ideas mention pinnable data or a reproducible prior number.

**Pred-N3 revised.** Topically diverse (10 distinct areas — the agent obeyed the spread instruction). The real similarity is in the **execution register**: most ideas mirror Nanda's current portfolio — behavioral model-biology at finetuning/agentic scale (SFT ablations, agent tournaments, frontier evals), which is largely not one-box-90-minute shaped. Only ~4 of 20 are single-forward-pass interp on small models.

**Pred-N5 held.** Agent 1's implicit criteria: recency, an explicitly-flagged gap in the source, safety stakes. It did gap-citation well (every WHY quotes a named open flag — better discipline than predicted). Fidelity criteria: entirely absent, as predicted.

**Per-idea survival predictions, registered now, sealed from the filter:** OUT on DECIDABLE ("why/how-useful/how-effectively" framing): N-04, N-09, N-10, N-11, N-16, and likely N-19, N-13, N-14. OUT on SUBSTRATE (finetuning runs, agent tournaments, frontier models): N-01, N-02, N-03, N-06, N-08, N-17. Borderline: N-05 (committed benchmark exists but universally-quantified question), N-07 (concrete register, survey scope), N-15 (agent infra, but ground-truth-by-construction is exactly our planted-null pattern). **Predicted survivors: N-12, N-18, N-20, plus at most two of {N-15, N-07, N-05}** — 3–5 total, and all replication/validation-shaped, which is my key Pred-N2 claim. One prediction about the criteria themselves: N-20 (GPT-2 positional embeddings) will survive our filter while Nanda's own doc disfavors GPT-2 work — if so, that's a discovered gap: **our criteria list contains no taste/relevance criterion**, because taste was always supplied by the human choosing seeds.

content.text:
Filter done. Neutral observations first, predictions scored, then selection and the a/b launch.

## Observations on the filter output

**Survivors: N-07 (diffusion-LM monitorability), N-20 (GPT-2 positional dims), N-18 (J-lens layer-band replication), N-13 (SAEs vs baselines on planted corruptions), N-14 (user-attribute probes, TalkTuner anchor).** Five of twenty, killed overwhelmingly by DECIDABLE (7) and SUBSTRATE (3) — the filter's own preamble names the surviving shape unprompted: "replication-flavored questions, not discovery-flavored ones... a named prior finding, a concrete register readable by forward passes or probes on one small open model, and ground truth plantable by construction." That is my Pred-N2 key claim, articulated independently by an agent that never saw it. **The criteria structurally reselect the audit-prior-work shape. Confirmed.**

**Prediction scoring, honestly:** N-18 ✓, N-20 ✓, N-07 ✓ (was in my borderline set), N-05 ✓ OUT, N-15 ✓ borderline-OUT. Two misses, both informative. **N-12 I predicted SURVIVES; it died on DECIDABLE** — I had mentally redesigned its why-question into a comparison because the substrate (pretrained Gemma Scope SAEs) was attractive; the filter refused exactly the leniency it was built to refuse. I violated my own criterion under temptation — evidence the blind mechanical filter beats the invested selector, which is H1 restated. **N-13 I predicted OUT; it survived** — but its fix ("define metric: planted-error detection rate") arguably exceeds the one-sentence-fix rule; the filter was generous exactly once, and on the FIXABLE boundary, not on a FAIL. Pred-N6 (committed-data leniency) mostly did not fire: the filter treated committed-data as universally fixable, which is optimistic in the B-gated-dataset case, but no survivor actually depends on a gated set. **The taste-gap prediction confirmed cleanly:** N-20 survived our criteria while Nanda's own doc says there is "no good reason to use GPT-2" now — our criteria list contains no taste criterion, because taste was always the human seed-chooser's contribution. Calibration outcome for the criteria themselves: they measure runnability and honesty, not worth; they need pairing with a taste source (a human, or the assessments-as-counterpart trick), and they need an explicit anchor-absent path — which the filter already exercised via "declare the anchor absent" on four of five survivors.

**Per-survivor yield predictions, against our evidence:** N-20: cleanest run of the five (D2-grade linear algebra, <$1), lowest worth — high collision risk with known results plus the taste fail. N-07: informative fork either way, but the highest infrastructure risk (open diffusion-LM tooling inside the 90-minute cap — the F2-class build-failure precedent). N-18: seed-D shaped, high taste, but the original's conventions are unpublished — the gatepress R6 class of harness-mismatch risk. N-13: best fork (either answer extends a named Nanda line), but the largest invention surface (what counts as "the SAE detector") — seed A's guessed-coordinates trap; triage would rightly hammer decidability-by-construction. **N-14: the only survivor with a C2-grade anchor** (published probe accuracies on an open 13B model, reproducible in-setting before any extension), planted ground truth by generator (the D-line stimulus pattern), cheap probe readout — and one real, known construct trap: probes trained on synthetic conversations may read surface tokens, not a "user model." That trap is load-bearing for the a/b: it gives skeptics genuine room to differ, which K-cells need.

**Selection: N-14**, highest combined confidence and the only candidate that also does diagnostic work in the wording test. Amending the pre-registered protocol visibly (exploratory K4 cell, scored by nothing in P-w1–P-w4, with its own registered P-w5), committing the amendment to both branches identically, then launching.

Fixing: stop my tainted runs, book the deviation in-repo, stage a frozen sandbox, launch the manager session.

content.text:
Fixed. Answer to your question: as originally staged, no — and now yes.

**The gap:** the v2.2 branches were cut from published `latent_skeptic` main, which had removed the per-role model pins ("model inherits the session"). All previous runs went through the harness **test copy**, which pins skeptics/adjudicator/runner to sonnet and reader/author to opus — so every historical verdict backing K1–K3 came from sonnet skeptics. Unpinned, the manager's arms would have inherited its own session model (Fable): wrong tier, roughly an order more cost, and no comparability with the record the K-claims anchor on. My excluded pilot had the same flaw — one more reason it deserved exclusion.

**What was done, in the safe window** (manager was still reading; `out/` empty, no run started — checked before touching anything, per the launcher-edit rule):

1. **Pins restored on both branches identically** — `model: 'sonnet'` on skeptic, skeptic-retry, both adjudicator sites, runner; `model: 'opus'` on reader and author; header comment updated to say pinned-by-Operating-discipline. Committed on `v2.2-a` (557d7f7), cherry-picked clean to `v2.2-b` (e19323c). Inter-branch diff re-verified: still 4 lines, the skeptic wording only — the single-factor rerun stands.
2. **Sandbox re-provisioned atomically**: old read-only copies removed, pinned versions extracted branch-pure, byte-identity to their commits verified, `chmod 444` re-applied.
3. **Manager notified** with one infrastructure-only line (re-read the scripts from disk before invoking; nothing about what's being tested leaked). The notice is queued into its session and lands when its current thinking turn ends; Workflow reads the script from disk at invoke time regardless, so even an un-reread invoke runs the pinned version.

Net effect on the experiment: the manager (Fable, xhigh) manages; the pipeline's judges run at the deployment tier (sonnet skeptics, opus reader — reader idle anyway if it passes `ground:false`); the wording a/b now measures the sentences at the tier they'd actually ship at, against history generated at that same tier.

# Lambda GPU access — how it worked, and the APIs used

How the GPU session for this project was provisioned, in plain terms, so it can
be reproduced. Date: 2026-06-15. All steps were driven from the local Windows
workstation (`LAPTOP-ULDACBRE`), **not** the Claude Code web sandbox — the
sandbox's HTTPS-only egress proxy blocks outbound SSH (see `archive/README_RUN.md`),
whereas the workstation has normal outbound network, which is what makes
"instrument from here over SSH" viable at all.

## The shape of it

1. Generate an SSH keypair locally.
2. Add the **public** key to the Lambda account via the Lambda Cloud API.
3. Launch a GPU instance via the API, selecting that key by name.
4. Lambda provisions the box and **injects the public key automatically** — no
   manual `ssh-copy-id`, no password. Once the instance is `active` you SSH in as
   `ubuntu@<ip>` with the matching private key.
5. Poll the API for the instance's IP, connect, run, then terminate.

The key point (and the reason no in-instance setup was needed for access):
**SSH access is completed by Lambda at provision time from the account's key
list.** You only have to get the public key onto the account once; every
instance launched thereafter with that key name is reachable immediately.

## Credentials

- Lambda API key: a `secret_…` bearer token, stored as `LAMBDA_KEY_ONE` in
  `./.keys` (single line `LAMBDA_KEY_ONE=secret_…`). `.keys` is **gitignored**
  (added to `.gitignore` this session) so the token can't be committed.
- SSH keypair: `~/.ssh/lambda_ed25519` (private) + `.pub`, ed25519, **no
  passphrase** (matches the existing `vastai_ed25519` pattern; enables
  non-interactive automation). Comment `lambda-latent_verify-helios-2026-06-15`.
  Treat the private key as sensitive; the rented box is ephemeral.
- The private key lives ONLY on the machine that generated it. A new
  workstation generates its own `~/.ssh/lambda_ed25519`, registers it under a
  NEW unique name via `POST /ssh-keys`, and launches with
  `SSH_KEY_NAME=<that name> bash lambda_run.sh …` (2026-07-21: this Linux
  workstation uses `latent_verify_hal_20260721`; the 06-15 name belongs to the
  Windows laptop). 1× H100 capacity flickers by the minute — poll
  `/instance-types` and launch into the window (see the capacity-watch pattern

All observed. Scoring against the registered predictions, then the sampled calls and the wording result.

## What happened (ignoring my predictions)

The manager ran the complete arc: searched the local record for TalkTuner first, fetched the published numbers from the web, iterated a conversation generator with a selftest (determinism, balance, attribute-naming lint), wrote **PREREG.md at 16:05Z with hashes and bands, launched at 16:07Z** — pre-registration genuinely before the run — on one A100 for 20 minutes, **$0.67 of the $15 cap**, teardown API-confirmed by an until-loop, ten provenance records plus raw fp16 activations saved. Then it re-ran **both frozen pipelines with byte-identical args, `execute_runs` on and both instruments now carrying validation artifacts** (generator selftest + a 16-way topic-probe positive control — instrument queue empty in round 2). Verdict: **protocol-void.** All five attributes decode far above chance (0.81–1.00), but the anchor fired — gender reproduced at 0.4467 vs published 0.94, below chance on template-disjoint families — and QUESTION.md's own gate voids every extension. The failure mode (template-family surface overfit) is exactly the declared construct risk, made concrete by its own permutation controls.

## Predictions scored

- **P-M1 wrong in the best way:** no HF gate halt — the token had Llama-2 acceptance; it just ran. The "void, not clean answer" half held.
- **P-M2 held strongly:** band authored pre-run, anchor out-of-band, extensions void. Anchors on others' settings have now fired 3 of 5 times in this record.
- **P-M3 held nearly completely:** created generator/runner/onbox/per-launch launcher copy/PREREG/re-triage args; used frozen trio, provenance.py, API doc as given; pipelines untouched (zero writes to them in all 83 tool calls). Spend below even my low band.
- **P-M4 held**, plus two things I didn't predict: `execute_runs:true` and H4 closed with real validation artifacts — the manager is the first actor ever to complete the instrument-validation loop this machinery was built around.
- **P-M6 mostly held**; the predicted F2-class infra retry apparently never happened — clean first launch.

## The sampled tool calls (seed 19, 10 of 83)

Every sampled call fits the intended pipeline shape and the historical human-orchestrated usage: local-record search before web (H3 order), reading its own round-1 workflow outputs, ToolSearch for WebFetch to source the anchor, generator edit → PREREG write → launcher verbatim → TaskStop + curl teardown poll → local venv analysis. Nothing off-model; the manager reconstructed the operating discipline (sealed-predictions analog, launcher-verbatim, teardown-confirm) from the frozen headers and one 145-word prompt.

## How the seeded wording differences behaved — the actual surprise

**P-M5 failed, informatively.** Index-matched over 59 cells: **66% status agreement**, not ≥90%. Flips run both directions (6 NEEDS_RUN→EXPLAINS, 6 EXPLAINS→RULED_OUT toward b; 7 back the other way); net drift is ~3 cells toward arm **b** — the *un*-hardened text — being slightly more decisive, opposite to the sentences' purpose. Crux lengths identical (499 vs 507 chars). Two honest caveats before reading that as a wording effect: one dropped finding in a2's age-bracket claim shifts up to 9 cells of the alignment, and — decisive — there is **no same-text/same-text noise floor**, so ~34% disagreement cannot be split between wording and ordinary sampling instability. What the data does establish: no differential wrongful acquittal (the RULED_OUTs sit on claims whose numbers ground-reproduce), no hedging difference, no direction consistent with the sentences' intent — and a **skeptic-verdict instability on the order of a third of cells**, which dwarfs any wording signal and is itself the finding. By the committed decision rule this run can't authorize the merge (it isn't the K-cell protocol); what it adds is that the wording question is smaller than the stability question it uncovered.

**Skeptic-verdict instability, defined:** the same claim, same evidence, same assigned confound, same prompt tier — sampled twice — returns a different status. The verdict is a draw from a distribution, not a function of its inputs.

**Evidence, all in-record:** (1) a2 vs b2: 20 of 59 index-matched cells disagree, and the flips run in *both* directions (12 toward stricter, 8 toward looser). A wording effect predicts directional flips; near-symmetric flips that mostly cancel (net drift ~3 cells) are the signature of noise. (2) Round 1 was 120/120 identical (all NEEDS_RUN) — so the instability appears only where evidence leaves discretion: it's decision-boundary noise, not random output. (3) The D2 "test"/"test" schema-valid garbage finding — same class, single-sample unreliability. (4) F9 precedent: identical seeds produced different designs (sealed, high confidence, held) — the same phenomenon one layer up. (5) Structurally: the `rounds:1` policy means the machinery has *never measured its own verdict variance* — the skeptic is an instrument with no stability validation artifact, H4 applied to itself. What's missing to make it a clean claim: a same-text/same-text repeat (noise floor). Never run — the a/b disagreement is an upper bound on noise+wording, not a separation.

That's why the new dir gets **v2.2-b** — the text *without* "Think before answering; do not guess" and "do not then hedge" is the arm we'd expect noisier, so your question probes stability where it should be worst. Building:

# Self-contained pipeline repo - setup guide

Everything a fresh session needs to pursue one research question, with no
outside context. Six pieces; nothing else.

## The pieces

- QUESTION.md   the question (template in this repo; you write it)
- pipeline.js   frozen claim-triage workflow, read-only (chmod 444) - the only
                audit tool; the session must never edit it or work around its
                verdicts. This copy is branch v2.2-b of latent_skeptic.
- frozen/       provenance.py, lambda_run.sh, remote_run.sh - given
                infrastructure; adapt ONLY at points their headers declare;
                broken infrastructure means halt and report, never patch
- LAMBDA_API.md how GPU provisioning works (keys, ssh, launch, poll, teardown)
- .keys         symlink to the Lambda + Hugging Face tokens (gitignored)
- out/          empty; everything produced lands here

## Writing QUESTION.md (the five duties only the question can carry)

1. Committed data: verbatim file + hash, or a committed deterministic
   generator rule. Data described in prose gets reconstructed and measures
   the wrong thing (proven twice in the parent record).
2. Anchor: a prior measured number + band to reproduce in-setting first, or
   "anchor absent" declared. Fired anchors are what caught every silent
   infidelity so far.
3. Refuting outcome per claim, measurable.
4. Scope: one cell; sweeps out of scope.
5. Construct risks declared, with whether validation is possible.

Everything else (design, prereg bands, generator, runner, launcher payload
copy, endpoint arithmetic) the session creates itself - observed to work.

## Launching

In this directory:

    tmux new-session -As <name>
    claude --dangerously-skip-permissions

Seed prompt (paste as one message; the two closing sentences verbatim):

    Your /goal: answer the research question in QUESTION.md in this
    directory, even if the answer is a refutation of the question.
    pipeline.js is a frozen claim-triage workflow: your only audit tool,
    read-only; never edit it or work around its verdicts. frozen/ is given
    infrastructure - adapt only at the points its file headers declare;
    broken infrastructure means halt and report, never patch. .keys holds
    Lambda and Hugging Face keys; LAMBDA_API.md explains provisioning.
    Rules: total spend cap 15 USD; confirm every instance teardown via the
    API; never edit a launcher while a box runs - copy per launch.
    Pre-register your design, bands, and hashes in PREREG.md before any
    run. Audit your claims with the pipeline before measuring and again
    after, with byte-identical claim framing. Save everything under out/.
    Think and explain yourself as simply as possible, but no simpler. Do
    not provide solutions until you have thought and reasoned about the
    problem as thoroughly as possible without providing any.

## Operator rules (learned the hard way)

- Never send the session a message while it is mid-turn; a queued message
  can be silently clobbered by the next command. Wait for idle.
- Watch remotely: /rename <name>, then /rc.
- Expect and want halts: a gated dataset, a failed anchor, or an
  unbuildable instrument is the pipeline working, not failing.

# Program brief - agent-run falsification pipeline (as of 2026-08-24)

One research question goes in; a pre-registered experiment, adversarial audits,
and plain-language takeaways come out. Agents speak only through typed
contracts; anything unfaithful returns a refusal (halt, void, on-hold), never
an answer. A human appears three times: choose the question, approve budget,
read the open questions.

The stack: doctrine (four heuristics: independence of actors, decisiveness of
numbers, groundedness in raw artifacts, the-instrument-is-a-claim) -> a
claim-triage tool (fresh skeptics, one confound each; an isolated reader
re-derives every cited number) -> a pipeline (design, diff, triage, human
gate, build, box run, elicit, takeaways) -> since this week, a delegated
manager session that drives all of it from a 150-word prompt.

## Six seeds, one line each

- A (reasoning direction, two 8B models): all testable endpoints refuted at
  guessed coordinates; the refutation is scoped to those coordinates.
- B (deliberately flawed twin): halted on a licence-gated dataset the design
  had invented - a question built on unnamed data cannot run faithfully.
- C (self-vs-other happiness at 3 sizes, data described in prose): ran clean,
  anchor fired (recovered 4.58 vs recorded 0.9) - the runner had reconstructed
  its own stimulus. Everything on hold.
- C2 (same question, exact prompts embedded): anchor passed (-0.934 vs -0.9);
  effect present at 9B (-0.93) and 27B (-1.39), indeterminate at 2B (-0.33),
  monotone with scale - but its own takeaways showed the readout reporting
  impossible probability shares above 1.0.
- D (character-count ripple, Pythia-410m): curve replicated (0.781 in band),
  ripple null - but the post phase showed the predicted 140-character period
  was never testable by the instrument. Seed amended before execute.
- D2 (aperture invariance, built from D's failures): shuffle nulls cleared at
  all three windows - and the anchor fired (0.549 vs band 0.701-0.861), so
  the whole run is void by its own rule. Second anchor save.

Lesson distilled: a good question carries five things nothing downstream can
conjure - committed data (or a committed generator), an anchor number with a
band (or "anchor absent" declared), a refuting outcome per claim, one-cell
scope, and declared construct risks. Everything else the machinery can build.

## This week's additions (v2.2, two branches)

Consumption law: a run halts unless the human gate answered, of record, every
queued question, non-reproducing grounding note, and instrument validation.
Forced by: a pre-run note flagged C2's readout as non-physical and nothing
consumed it. Also: instrument validation wired (H4), degenerate skeptic
findings rejected (a committed finding once read confound "test", crux
"test"), void flags propagate to every record (D2's void lived only in its
summary while per-window files said "null cleared").

## The two live experiments

1. Idea-to-question calibration: one blind agent harvested 20 research ideas
   from Neel Nanda's writings; a second blind agent filtered them against our
   criteria. Five survived; all replication-shaped. Finding: our criteria
   select runnable-and-honest, not interesting - taste is a missing criterion
   (a GPT-2 idea survived that the source explicitly disfavours).
2. The manager experiment: a fresh session, seeded with only the chosen
   question (user-attribute probing on Llama-2-13B-chat), the frozen tool,
   and GPU keys, ran the entire arc itself for $0.67: pre-registered bands
   before launch, built and hashed its own dataset generator, validated its
   instruments (first actor ever to complete that loop), probed all five
   attributes far above chance (0.81-1.00) - and returned VOID, because its
   anchor fired: the published gender-probe accuracy (0.94) reproduced at
   0.4467 on template-disjoint families. Its own diagnosis: the probes learn
   template-family surface cues, not a user model - exactly the construct
   risk the question declared.

## The wording A/B and the instability finding

Two branches differ by three skeptic-prompt sentences ("Most strong effects
are confounded", "Think before answering; do not guess", "State your
conclusion; do not then hedge it away"). Both audited the manager's claims
with identical inputs. Statuses agree in 66 percent of 59 matched cells;
flips run both directions and mostly cancel (net drift about 3 cells). No
wrongful acquittals, no hedging difference. The real finding: single-sample
skeptic verdicts are unstable on roughly a third of discretionary cells,
which dwarfs any wording effect - and no same-text repeat has ever been run
to measure that noise floor. The pre-registered decision (which wording
merges) is therefore still open, along with: the original known-claim
protocol cells, and a fresh sandbox (auto_interp_2) ready for a new question
on the noisier branch.
