**The retro as a tree** — simplest true hierarchy of what was actually done:

```
retro/
├── question-formation study          # why do questions form at all
│   ├── H-top (second representation) ── partially refuted → "asking is the trigger"
│   ├── co-presence decides the question class (claims-beside-data)
│   ├── notice ≠ press — ranking is the scarce step, not detection
│   └── naming-gate ×3: named categories move output 20x; principles ~0
├── harness                           # those findings, mechanized
│   ├── prompts/  elicit · contract · meta   (the ask, the register, the inhibition)
│   ├── gates/    density · scope            (mechanical blocks; blocks work, marks don't)
│   └── latent_skeptic_test/                 (H1–H4 claim triage)
├── seed probes                       # one question = one experiment
│   ├── A   faithful question    → all endpoints refuted, at guessed coordinates
│   ├── B   flawed twin          → halt: invented, licence-gated data
│   ├── C   data described       → ran clean, anchor fired (4.58 vs 0.9)
│   ├── C2  data embedded        → anchor passed; scale result; instrument rot found
│   ├── D   pre-registration     → anchor passed; null was aperture-censored
│   └── D2  fork + escape hatch  → nulls cleared, anchor fired → VOID
├── v2.2                              # failures promoted to machinery
│   ├── consumption law (halt on any unanswered finding)
│   ├── H4 wired · degenerate-finding filter · void propagation
│   └── branches a/b — three doctrine sentences under registered test
└── delegation                        # this session
    ├── idea→filter calibration: 20 Nanda ideas → 5 survive, all replication-shaped
    ├── manager: full arc solo from 150 words, $0.67 → VOID by its own anchor
    └── wording A/B: 66% cell agreement → verdict instability > wording effect
```

**The second diagram is a loop, not a tree** — because that's the working manner: the hierarchy above is just sediment left by one repeated motion, and the motion also runs on itself:

```
        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ QUESTION — carries only what nothing downstream │
        │ can conjure: data, anchor, scope, fork, risks   │
        └──────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┘
               ▼
     seal predictions ──► run under gates ──► REFUSAL or FINDING
               ▲                                    │
               │              every miss forks two ways
               │            ┌───────────────────────┴──────────────────────┐
               │            ▼                                              ▼
               │   clause in the NEXT question                    law in the MACHINERY
               │   (C→C2: data-in-seed;                           (grounding note ignored
               │    D→D2: fork + escape hatch)                     → consumption halt;
               │            │                                      "test/test" → filter)
               │            └───────────────────────┬──────────────────────┘
               └────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
              …and the same loop, one level down, aimed at itself:
        the skeptics become the experiment (wording A/B, sealed P-w1–5);
        the orchestrator seals predictions about its own reading (press files);
        the rerun ledger applies the halt rule to its own untested pieces —
        a piece whose rerun never ran is itself an unconsumed finding.
```

One motion, two feedback edges (question-side, machinery-side), applied recursively downward — that's the whole retro in one sentence.

# latent_skeptic

Adversarial verification for empirical research claims, built from stateless parts. `HEURISTICS.md` is the binding contract; everything else is a way of applying it.

The parts, each independently usable and self-describing:

- `HEURISTICS.md`: the rules. Read first; nothing normative lives anywhere else.
- `agents/*.md`: claim-blind roles (reader grounds numbers in artifacts, runner executes one control verbatim, author writes one instrument from a spec). Each file is its own documentation. Invoke any of them directly with the Agent tool, alone or in a composition of your own, provided the composition honours the heuristics: fresh contexts, bounded evidence, one lens per agent.
- `triage_workflow.js`: an EXAMPLE composition, full per-claim confound fan-out with run/author queues. Self-documented in its header; other compositions can be produced the same way.

Install: from the host project root, `cp <clone>/agents/*.md .claude/agents/` (the harness does not discover agents inside the clone). Keep `settings.local.json` scoped to the instance ssh/scp/python; never `Bash(*)`.

content.text:
All verified and the rename is done (`v2.3-a`/`v2.3-b` local and remote, old names deleted, SETUP.md provenance corrected). Answers, thought through:

## Git structure right now

**Tracked, with remotes:** `latent_skeptic` (main; your `v2.2` question-format port — triage renamed to pipeline.js, +838 lines; my `v2.3-a`/`v2.3-b`; merge decision still open pending the K-cell protocol), `welfare_probe` (retro merged to main), `latent_verify`. **Tracked, no remote:** `mats_r1d1` (full history, unpushable), `auto_interp_2` (local git, one small repo, `.keys` ignored). **Untracked entirely:** `mats_manifold` — now the largest loss-surface: it ran on without us through seeds D2.1, D3, D3.1, D4, D4.1, ending in a genuinely strong result (four-phase counter formation: instant crude counter at step 512, destructive high-dimensional reorganization 2k–8k, relocation, precision boundary forming *last* at 45% of training then fossilizing while dimensionality still compresses) — none of it in git. Also untracked: `auto_interp` (the manager sandbox, incl. ANSWER.md), `mats_open` loose files (BRIEF, CONTEXT_PACK). Heavy raw results run 30–116MB per seed plus 2.5GB of activations in auto_interp — gitignore territory, not commit territory.

## Do we need latent_skeptic_meta? Yes — and it's the third instance of one pattern

The copy-drift problem was solved for the *tool* by giving it a canonical repo. The same problem exists one level up: experiments propagate by copy + deviation-record chains across non-repos, and the deviation chain already broke silently once (manifold's "byte-identical except listed" claim is checked by nothing). A meta repo with `latent_skeptic` as a **pinned submodule** solves, in one move: mats_r1d1's missing remote, manifold's missing git, mats_open's loose artifacts, and — the real point — it gives the **L5 layer a home**: the ledgers, briefs, gate-commits, and the seed-lineage itself, which is currently the least-tracked and most valuable thing. The submodule pin also mechanizes the rule compositions/README already states ("projects pin a version") — each experiment records exactly which tool commit judged it. Structure: `latent_skeptic_meta/{latent_skeptic@pin, mats_r1d1/, mats_manifold/, mats_open/, LOOP.md}`, gitignoring raw archives while keeping provenance records and per-row files. The one thing it must not do: pre-empt the open v2.3 merge decision.

## The RETRO-D refinement loop vs. the repo's design — barely anticipated, and that's the gap

How well does latent_skeptic describe the loop that actually produced its best results (C→C2, D→D2→D3→D4.1)? Almost not at all. The repo describes **one pass over claims**: skeptics, queues, "between passes make each run_queue item a full command" — pass-iteration, not question-iteration. The only hooks that gesture at evolution are the instrument `version` field and HEURISTICS' git-blame provenance culture. Everything that makes the loop work — takeaways becoming the next seed's clauses, seed amendment before execute, gate-commits answering diff questions of record, sealed predictions per iteration, the observe-then-preregister rule (gatepress R7) — lives in mats_* ledgers and welfare_probe's retro, i.e., in the untracked and un-canonical layers. The engine of the research is documented only in its exhaust. Your v2.2 "pure question format" port and a meta repo both point at the same repair: the loop deserves a first-class description where the tool lives, because RETRO-D demonstrated it's the tool's actual mode of use — five consecutive seeds, each built from the previous one's audited failure, converging on a result no single seed could have asked for.

## The latent_verify experiment — shape, and one warning

Posing "the research done as part of latent_verify" is a *project*, not a question — it fails our own SCOPE criterion as stated. But the manager experiment showed the fix is free: given one page, a fresh session decomposed it into six atomic claims unaided. So the seed should be: point QUESTION.md at latent_verify's committed record (its repo is tracked — good), ask *which of its headline claims reproduce*, and let the manager decompose. The five duties: data — whatever stimuli latent_verify committed ship in the payload (the C-lesson; anything it only described will be reconstructed and measure the wrong thing); anchors — its own recorded numbers, which makes this the first experiment with C2-grade anchors *for free*; expect and want partial reproduction — the D1 precedent says the interesting output is which claims ground as "unauditable" (artifacts never saved), which diverge, and which hold. `auto_interp_2` is ready for exactly this; its pipeline is v2.3-b.

## The E-manager run

Went as reported, and cleanly: full arc solo from 150 words — pre-registered bands before launch, self-built hashed generator, first-ever completed H4 instrument validation, five attributes decoded 0.81–1.00, and the verdict its own anchor forced: **VOID**, gender reproducing at 0.4467 against a published 0.94 on template-disjoint families, with the correct diagnosis (surface-cue overfit — the declared construct risk). $0.67 of $15, teardown API-confirmed, frozen files untouched across 83 tool calls. Since then: idle, tmux `auto-interp` still alive, nothing new produced. Its one enduring contribution beyond the science: the a/b it hosted surfaced the verdict-instability finding (66% cell agreement, flips canceling), which is now the standing open measurement — and worth one line in whatever QUESTION.md you write next: two same-text audit passes cost pennies and would finally buy the noise floor.

content.text:
Predictions registered first, from current understanding, before touching the evidence:

**P-1 (which subagents D used):** Across every D-seed triage, only reader + skeptics + adjudicator ran. Runner, author, and the instruments surface were never invoked — manifold's pipeline.js calls the workflow with `{claims}` only and was frozen by deviation record. Evidence will show `runner_results: null`, no `authored`, no instrument queues in all manifold records.

**P-2 (call shape constant):** Design triage always 1 claim ("design-core") × 2 custom confounds; post-run question-triage 3 claims × 10 defaults. Unchanged D→D4.1 — the machinery's use is frozen; only inputs evolve.

**P-3 (where change lives):** In seed text and records practice, not tool use: seeds stay long (800–1300 words) but shift content — constants migrate to calibration stages, artifact-retention clauses multiply, anchors multiply (D4.1's ledger says "twice-anchored"), presence questions become forks, and later seeds cite prior result files by path. Direction: phenomenon-questions → instrument-questions.

**P-4 (records practice):** GATE_COMMIT + sealed predictions exist per D3/D4 seed; deviation records only for launcher payload touches; pipeline.js byte-stable since the D-era deviation record.

**P-5 (vs E-manager):** E-manager differs in five ways D never did: no design phase (decomposed the question itself into 6 per-attribute claims), default confound menu on pre-run claims, `instruments` passed, `execute_runs: true` with the runner actually firing (once), and a byte-identical pre/post double audit. D iterated the *question* across runs; the manager iterated the *evidence* within one run.

**P-6 (seed size):** roughly plateau after D2, slight shrink as calibration absorbs constants. Low-medium confidence.

Now the evidence.

content.text:
All evidence in. Answers first on the repo mechanics, then predictions scored against citations.

## Submodule sync — the worry is backwards

A submodule doesn't track a branch; the superproject commits a **specific SHA**. Changing latent_skeptic changes nothing anywhere until an experiment explicitly commits a pin-bump. So each experiment permanently records *which tool judged it* — that's the feature, and it mechanizes two rules the record already paid for: the deviation-chain ("byte-identical except listed", currently checked by nothing) and the launcher-edit law generalized (never change an instrument under a live experiment; a pin-bump mid-lineage = new sealed run).

**How others split fixed/variable:** lockfile pinning (our submodule SHA); vendor-and-freeze (what mats_* did — the deviation record is a hand-written lockfile, and it's the weakest of these because nothing verifies it); container images (pin + environment; our runs instead rebuild env and log it in provenance records); the benchmark-harness pattern — fixed harness version, variable task/config files — which is exactly the pipeline/seed split; and registered reports — protocol committed, then executed — which is SEALED_PREDICTIONS + the gate. We independently reinvented most of this list; the meta repo just makes the pinning mechanical.

## LOOP.md, and whether not specifying the loop was a problem

LOOP.md = the refinement loop as spec, not folklore: seed lifecycle (seed → design-mode dry run → gate-commit answering diff and grounding of record → execute → post → takeaways feed the next seed's clauses); amendment rules (pre-execute only, deviation-recorded — `seed_d_ripple_v2.md`); anchor inheritance (each seed anchors on its predecessor's committed numbers); and lineage termination — which RETRO-D invented too: `seed_d3_1_close.md` is literally a *closing* seed.

Was the absence problematic? The decisive evidence is E-manager: **same tool, no loop knowledge → no loop.** It ran one immaculate iteration, hit VOID, and stopped — where RETRO-D, hitting D2's identical anchor-void, wrote D2.1. The loop lives in the operator, not the tool, so it doesn't transfer; and its records live in the untracked layer (manifold has no git). Also: loop practices don't even persist within RETRO-D unforced — the press-prediction files (`PREDICTIONS_gatepress_seedD.md`, `d2press`) appear at D only, never again. Not a problem for the inventor; a problem for anyone else, which now includes every delegated manager.

## Predictions scored

**P-1 confirmed exactly.** All 14 manifold triage records: `runner=0`, `authored=False`, `instrument_queue` empty (the key exists because the workflow always returns it; nothing ever fed it). D used 3 of 5 legs: reader (groundings consumed at gates — "Noted from triage grounding, accepted as-is", GATE_COMMIT_seedD), skeptics, adjudicator. **Unpredicted:** the runner/author legs' *jobs* got done anyway — by hand. `records/CONTROL_d4_1_label_reachability.txt` is a decision-rule reachability control (all five labels reachable — the D2 outcome-space lesson, executed as an orchestrator-side selftest), and `EXPLORATORY_k2_rerank_seedD3.md` is a queue item run manually with explicit post-hoc labeling ("POST-HOC, not pre-registered… superseded by seed D3.1's committed version if run"). The queues found a consumer; it just wasn't the machinery.

**P-2 confirmed to the digit.** Every D design-triage: 1 claim × 2 findings; every post-qtriage: 3 claims × 30 findings, D through D4.1 — seven seeds, zero variation in call shape. The only historical change is v1→v2: seedA/B v1 records show 1×10 (the confound menu), cut to 1×2 by subtraction S4. So: **the tool's use never changed across D's entire arc. All change lived in inputs and surrounding practice.**

**P-3 confirmed with numbers.** Anchor mentions per seed: D3=4, D4=3, D4.1=5 (ledger: "twice-anchored object"); every later seed cites prior committed records/results by path (2–3 cites each); GUESS counts stay low (2–5) because constants now come from measured priors, not guesses. One miss inside it: "calibration" as a named stage appears in D-v2/D2 then vanishes (0 mentions in D3/D4) — the device was absorbed into constants-from-prior-measurements rather than kept as a stage.

**P-4 mostly confirmed.** GATE_COMMIT per seed (7 files); pipeline.js single copy, still byte-stable per its one deviation record. Miss: press files not repeated (above).

**P-5 confirmed.** The contrast stands: D = one design-core claim, 2 custom confounds, queues consumed manually, question iterated *across* runs. E-manager = 6 self-decomposed claims, full default menu, `instruments` passed (first ever), `execute_runs:true` with the runner firing, byte-identical pre/post double audit — evidence iterated *within* one run, question never iterated.

**P-6 partial.** Sizes plateau (692–1067 words), no monotone shrink: 871→899→1067→907→966→692→825→839. The 692 is the closing seed, not a trend.

**Unpredicted observation worth keeping:** the post-triage status mix moves with instrument maturity. NEEDS_RUN in post-qtriage: D=4, D2=12, D2.1=12, D3=8, D3.1=10, D4.1=3 — it peaks exactly when a seed introduces a new instrument (apertures, the scale axis) and collapses at the arc's ends, with D4.1 reaching 11 RULED_OUT / 3 NEEDS_RUN: by the last seed, nearly every elicited question was decidable from committed artifacts alone. The save-everything clauses, accumulated seed over seed, are visible in the machinery's own output statistics — the loop improving the *auditability* of its runs, measurably, while its use of the tool never changed at all.

**Where the A–C research actually lives — three layers, two of them at risk:**

1. **Conclusions** (heuristics, prompts, gates): committed — latent_skeptic repo and `welfare_probe/retro/harness/`, both pushed.
2. **Experiments and outputs** (BATTERY.md, OBSERVATIONS.md + rerun-B/C, SKEPTIC_SUBSTITUTION.md, the elicited outputs verbatim in `elicited/`, `elicited_b/`, `elicited_c/`, QUEUE/EVENTS/PREDICTIONS): committed in `welfare_probe/retro/` — pushed to latent_welfare last week.
3. **The conversations themselves and the material reviewed** — the part you're asking about — are in no repo at all. The RETRO sessions are Claude Code transcripts in `~/.claude/projects/`: the A–C lineage is the Aug 16–19 jsonl set under `-home-hal-dev-interp-dm-hack/` (several 3–5MB files, incl. the currently-active `DM-HACK-RETRO-C-ii`), RETRO-D is one 4.2MB file under `-…-mats-manifold/`, E and E-manager under the mats-open dirs. Machine-local, chmod 600, deletable by a cache cleanup. The reviewed material is likewise loose: `dm_hack/refs/` (welfare papers + SOURCES.md), `retro/mats/` PDFs, the sprint brief — `dm_hack/` root isn't a git repo. **The primary sources of the whole program are the untracked layer.**

**The sketch** — provenance by layout, no tooling, no rules:

```
latent_skeptic_meta/
├── README.md            five sentences: what this is, what lives where. Nothing else.
├── latent_skeptic/      submodule, pinned. The tool. An experiment that used a different
│                        pin says so in its own records (they already do — SETUP.md, deviations).
├── sessions/            PRIMARY SOURCES — the conversations that did the work
│   ├── INDEX.md         one line each: name, dates, working dir, one-clause summary
│   └── retro-A..C*.jsonl, retro-D.jsonl, retro-E.jsonl, retro-E-manager.jsonl
│                        (copied from ~/.claude/projects/; ~35MB total, fine for git)
├── elicitation/         the A–C research program itself
│   ├── retro/           moved from welfare_probe/retro — battery, observations, reruns,
│   │                    elicited outputs verbatim, harness
│   └── sources/         what was read: refs/ papers + SOURCES.md, the mats PDFs, sprint brief
├── experiments/
│   ├── mats_r1d1/       imported as-is (ledgers, seeds, records; gets git for the first time usable remotely)
│   ├── mats_manifold/   same — first time in git at all; seven seeds of lineage
│   ├── auto_interp/     the E-manager run: QUESTION, PREREG, ANSWER, out/ records
│   └── auto_interp_2/   absorbed (its one-repo history noted in INDEX)
└── .gitignore           .keys, venvs, __pycache__, raw activation/generation archives
                         (per-row records and endpoint JSONs stay tracked — they're the audit trail)
```

The directory order *is* the provenance chain: sources → sessions → elicitation → tool → experiments. No provenance.py needed — git history plus the ledgers the experiments already carry plus one INDEX.md do the whole job for an audience of us.

**Three decisions to make before building, flagged not decided:**

1. **Move vs mirror `retro/`.** Moving is cleaner — retro was always a guest in welfare_probe (it's *about* that repo, but it's this program's research); leave one pointer commit behind. Mirroring keeps latent_welfare self-contained but forks the record.
2. **Transcripts contain everything.** Before this repo ever gets a remote, one scrub pass over the jsonl for token patterns (`secret_…`, `hf_…`) — commands that *read* .keys appear in transcripts; values shouldn't, but "shouldn't" isn't a check. Private remote regardless.
3. **mats_r1d1's existing git history**: import as subtree (keeps its 20+ commits — the C→C2 story is told *in* those commit messages) rather than flat copy. Manifold has no history to lose.

And the deferred point, kept deferred: no LOOP.md, agreed — but the repo quietly serves that goal anyway, because the loop's evidence (sessions, gate-commits, seed lineages) all lands in one place, so when enough iterations exist to say what best practice is, the material to derive it from will already be sitting there.

content.text:
Skeleton committed. The remaining answers:

**Session vs experiment — the split isn't clean, so we drop it.** An experiment is a subject (question + ledger + records); a session is one actor's run of attention. In practice they're nearly 1:1 (RETRO-D ↔ mats_manifold, E-manager ↔ auto_interp), and where they are, the transcript belongs *beside* the artifacts — that's our own co-presence doctrine: a transcript next to its exhaust is claims-beside-data for any future elicitation pass, and a lone `sessions/` directory is exactly the "object sent alone" the harness forbids. The messy cases (RETRO-E drove auto_interp, auto_interp_2, *and* the v2.3 branches; the early dm_hack-dir sessions wander) go at root with an INDEX line listing everything they touched. And yes — **A–C is itself an experiment**, unambiguously: it has a battery, filed predictions, a named refuting outcome, and scored observations. So `elicitation/` folds into `experiments/elicitation/`, its sources (the mats PDFs, refs/ papers it actually consumed) inside it. Final shape: `README.txt`, `PROMPT.txt`, `INDEX.txt`, root transcripts for spanning sessions, `latent_skeptic/` submodule, `experiments/{elicitation, mats_r1d1, mats_manifold, auto_interp, auto_interp_2}` each carrying its own transcript.

**README.txt and PROMPT.txt** are written as above — README is nine sentences, says nothing about contents beyond the reading order, flags private-forever with the reason. PROMPT.txt is the "how do I do a new one" answer: the six-piece checklist, the seed prompt **verbatim** (unchanged from the one that ran E-manager for $0.67), plus the two operational facts a future you needs: the interface is learned from pipeline.js's header, not the prompt; and copy the transcript back into the experiment dir when done.

**Subtree, plainly.** A submodule is a *pointer* to another repo — you need that other repo to exist forever. `git subtree add --prefix=experiments/mats_r1d1 <path> master` instead *splices the entire foreign commit DAG into this repo* via one merge commit — content and history both live here, one clone gets everything, the source repo can die. **Navigability caveat, honestly:** spliced commits keep their original paths, so `git log experiments/mats_r1d1/README.md` won't walk into pre-import history (only `--follow` per-file partially rescues it). The fix that makes navigation seamless: rewrite the source first with `git filter-repo --to-subdirectory-filter experiments/mats_r1d1`, then a plain `git merge --allow-unrelated-histories` — every old commit then already lives under the prefix, and path-scoped log, blame, and bisect all work as if it was born here. mats_r1d1 is ~25 commits; the rewrite is seconds, and those commit messages are worth keeping — the C→C2 story ("anchor guard fired… data-in-seed fix proven") is told *in* them. Recommendation: filter-repo variant for mats_r1d1; everything else has no history to preserve and just moves. Say go and I'll run the migration — retro move with pointer commit, r1d1 import, manifold/auto_interp/auto_interp_2 moves, transcript copies, submodule pin.

===================

Private, permanently. The session transcripts in this repo contain full
tool output, local paths, keys-adjacent commands, and infrastructure
detail. Never public, never mirrored.

The tool is latent_skeptic/ (submodule, pinned; an experiment that used a
different version says so in its own records). Each directory under
experiments/ is one experiment: question, ledgers, records, results, and
the transcript of the session that drove it, side by side. Transcripts
that drove several experiments sit at the root. To answer "how was this
done": ledger first, records second, transcript last. Heavy raw artifacts
(activations, generations archives) stay on disk but out of git; every
provenance record and per-row result file is tracked.

Sessions
--------
Root jsonl files are the DM-HACK-RETRO lineage driven from the dm_hack
directory (question-elicitation experiments A-C and the mats_r1d1 seeds;

Colocated transcripts:

  experiments/auto_interp/4b5dae78.jsonl    RETRO-E-manager, the $0.67 run

New experiment
--------------
Make experiments/<name>/ with: QUESTION.md (committed data or generator
rule; anchor + band, or "anchor absent" declared; refuting outcome per
claim; one-cell scope; declared construct risks), pipeline.js (frozen copy
from the latent_skeptic pin, chmod 444), frozen/ (provenance.py,
lambda_run.sh, remote_run.sh), LAMBDA_API.md, .keys symlink, empty out/.

claude --dangerously-skip-permissions; paste this as one message:

    directory, even if the answer is a refutation of the question.
    pipeline.js is a frozen claim-triage workflow: your only audit tool,
    read-only; never edit it or work around its verdicts. frozen/ is given
    infrastructure - adapt only at the points its file headers declare;
    broken infrastructure means halt and report, never patch. .keys holds
    Lambda and Hugging Face keys; LAMBDA_API.md explains provisioning.
    Rules: total spend cap 15 USD; confirm every instance teardown via the
    API; never edit a launcher while a box runs - copy per launch.
    Pre-register your design, bands, and hashes in PREREG.md before any
    run. Audit your claims with the pipeline before measuring and again
    after, with byte-identical claim framing. Save everything under out/.
    Think and explain yourself as simply as possible, but no simpler. Do
    not provide solutions until you have thought and reasoned about the
    problem as thoroughly as possible without providing any.

The prompt never explains the pipeline's interface; the session learns it
from pipeline.js's own header comment. Do not message the session while it
is mid-turn: a queued message can be silently clobbered. Expect and want
halts: a gated dataset, a failed anchor, or an unbuildable instrument is
the pipeline working. Afterwards: copy the session's transcript jsonl from
~/.claude/projects/ into the experiment directory and add it to Sessions
above.
